   384	
   385	  /** End a tool span exactly once; tracing failures never change tool results. */
   386	  private endToolSpan(client: TraceClient, span: TraceSpan, outcome: SpanOutcome): void {
   387	    try {
   388	      client.endSpan(span, outcome);
   389	    } catch {
   390	      // Tracing must never throw into tool execution.
   391	    }
   392	  }
   393	
   394	  private async dispatch(request: ToolCallRequest): Promise<ExecuteResult> {
   395	    const startedAt = Date.now();
   396	    const { toolCallId, name } = request;
   397	    const agentPayload = request.agentId ? { agentId: request.agentId } : {};
   398	    let args = request.args;
   399	    const capability = inferCapability(name);
   400	    const canonicalCapability = canonicalCapabilityOf(name);
   401	    // Routers need the same owned-path authority policy uses: a write worker
   402	    // rewriting its own declared output must be able to replace it.
   403	    if (!request.ownedPaths?.length && this.ownedPaths?.length) {
   404	      (request as { ownedPaths?: readonly string[] }).ownedPaths = this.ownedPaths;
   405	    }
   406	
   407	    // === TOOL REPAIR LAYER — runs before policy so hash and decision use repaired args ===
   408	    let repairHint: string | undefined;
   409	    if (this.repair && name !== "task.complete" && !name.startsWith("mcp.")) {
   410	      const repairResult = this.repair.process(name, args);
   411	      if (repairResult.repaired) {
   412	        repairHint = repairResult.hint;
   413	        args = repairResult.args;
   414	        (request as Record<string, unknown>).args = args;
   415	      }
   416	    }
   417	    // === END TOOL REPAIR ===
   418	
   419	    const argumentHash = hashArgs(args);
   420	    // Track the claim across execution so the crash-recovery state is honest:
   421	    // a claimed approval that never reports an outcome stays `pending` and a
   422	    // later replay classifies it `unverified` instead of reissuing authority.
   423	    let claimedApprovalId: string | undefined;
   424	    // T5 hierarchy: executionId → invocationId → toolCallId — typed via CorrelationContext, no loose Record
   425	    // For T5 parallel path, correlation is required (asserted in tool-correlation); for serial/back-compat allow fallback to empty.
   426	    const correlation: CorrelationContext = {
   427	      executionId: request.executionId ?? "",
   428	      invocationId: request.invocationId ?? "",
   429	    };
   430	
   431	    await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.REQUESTED, {
   432	      toolCallId,
   433	      toolName: name,
   434	      capability,
   435	      canonicalCapability,
   436	      argumentHash,
   437	      argsPreview: sanitizeArgs(args),
   438	      executionId: correlation.executionId,
   439	      invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   440	      ...agentPayload,
   441	      ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   442	    });
   443	
   444	    if (request.allowedMutationPaths?.length) {
   445	      const mutationPaths = extractMutationPaths(name, args);
   446	      const allowed = new Set(request.allowedMutationPaths.map((path) => resolve(this.root, path)));
   447	      const changedTarget = mutationPaths.find((path) => !allowed.has(resolve(this.root, path)));
   448	      if (changedTarget) {
   449	        const message = `Task constraint denied: ${changedTarget} is not the explicitly requested target`;
   450	        await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.FAILED, {
   451	          toolCallId,
   452	          toolName: name,
   453	          error: message,
   454	          durationMs: 0,
   455	          canonicalCapability,
   456	          argumentHash,
   457	          executionId: correlation.executionId,
   458	          invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   459	          ...agentPayload,
   460	          ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   461	        });
   462	        return { kind: "error", message, retryable: false };
   463	      }
   464	    }
   465	
   466	    // Continuation resumes bypass main policy gate — approval was already verified
   467	    // by ContinuationManager. R1.5: the executor independently re-validates the
   468	    // durable approval (present, still `approved`, not expired) — a caller-set
   469	    // `source` string is not authorization. Missing/invalid evidence fails closed.
   470	    if (request.source === "continuation-resume") {
   471	      const approval = request.approvalId && this.approvalStore
   472	        ? this.approvalStore.get?.(request.approvalId)
   473	        : undefined;
   474	      const stillAuthorized =
   475	        !!approval &&
   476	        approval.status === "approved" &&
   477	        (!approval.expiresAt || new Date(approval.expiresAt).getTime() > Date.now());
   478	      if (!stillAuthorized) {
   479	        return {
   480	          kind: "denied",
   481	          reason: request.approvalId
   482	            ? `Continuation resume rejected: approval ${request.approvalId} missing, not approved, or expired`
   483	            : "Continuation resume rejected: no durable approval backing this request",
   484	        };
   485	      }
   486	      const contGateResult = await this.checkOwnershipGate(request, name, args);
   487	      if (contGateResult) return contGateResult;
   488	      // R1.5: the continuation tombstone is NOT authorization — claim the
   489	      // backing approval atomically so two parallel resumes cannot both run.
   490	      if (request.approvalId) {
   491	        const claimed = await this.claimApproval(request.approvalId, {
   492	          ...this.invocationIdentity(capability, name, argumentHash, request.agentId),
   493	          });
   494	        if (claimed) return claimed;
   495	        claimedApprovalId = request.approvalId;
   496	      }
   497	      await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.STARTED, {
   498	        toolCallId,
   499	        toolName: name,
   500	        argumentHash,
   501	        executionId: correlation.executionId,
   502	        invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   503	        ...agentPayload,
   504	        ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   505	      });
   506	      const resumed = await this.toolAwareRouter.downstream.execute(request);
   507	      if (claimedApprovalId) {
   508	        await this.recordApprovalOutcome(claimedApprovalId, resumed.kind === "success" ? "succeeded" : "failed");
   509	      }
   510	      return resumed;
   511	    }
   512	
   513	    // Safe shell bypass for ask mode: read-only commands skip policy gate
   514	    const mode = this.config.permissions.sessionMode ?? "ask";
   515	    if (mode === "ask" && name === "shell.run") {
   516	      const command = typeof args?.command === "string" ? args.command : "";
   517	      if (command && isSafeShellCommand(command)) {
   518	        // Skip the approval gate for a whitelisted read-only command, but do
   519	        // not execute it here: the downstream ShellToolRouter owns workspace
   520	        // path validation and command-failure classification.
   521	        await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.STARTED, {
   522	          toolCallId,
   523	          toolName: name,
   524	          argumentHash,
   525	          executionId: correlation.executionId,
   526	          invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   527	          ...agentPayload,
   528	          ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   529	        });
   530	        return await this.toolAwareRouter.downstream.execute(request);
   531	      }
   532	    }
   533	
   534	    // Unified authorization via ExecutionAuthorization — composes PolicyGate,
   535	    // OwnershipGate, and audit/event emission into a single decision.
   536	    const { ExecutionAuthorization } = await import("../../runtime-state/runtime/execution-authorization.js");
   537	    const policyGate = await this.policyGate();
   538	    const execAuth = new ExecutionAuthorization({
   539	      policyGate,
   540	      toolRegistry: this.toolRegistry,
   541	      ownershipGateConfig: this.ownershipRegistry && this.workspacePathResolver
   542	        ? { registry: this.ownershipRegistry, resolver: this.workspacePathResolver, autoAcquire: this.config.ownership?.autoAcquire ?? true }
   543	        : undefined,
   544	    });
   545	
   546	    const decision = await execAuth.evaluate({
   547	      requestId: toolCallId,
   548	      capability,
   549	      toolName: name,
   550	      args,
   551	      cwd: this.root,
   552	      sessionMode: this.config.permissions.sessionMode ?? "ask",
   553	      sessionId: this.sessionId(),
   554	      agentId: request.agentId ?? "alix",
   555	      source: "tool",
   556	      ownedPaths: this.ownedPaths,
   557	    });
   558	
   559	    // Denied — policy or ownership rejected this call
   560	    if (decision.status === "denied") {
   561	      await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.FAILED, {
   562	        toolCallId,
   563	        toolName: name,
   564	        error: decision.reason,
   565	        durationMs: 0,
   566	        canonicalCapability,
   567	        argumentHash,
   568	        executionId: correlation.executionId,
   569	        invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   570	        ...agentPayload,
    30	  matchedRuleId?: string;
    31	  approvalId?: string;
    32	  policyRevision?: string;
    33	  /** Exact binding key the approval was created/bound with (coordination path). */
    34	  bindingKey?: string;
    35	  /** The request fingerprint that key was computed from. */
    36	  requestFingerprint?: string;
    37	  /**
    38	   * Set only by the coordination exact-binding branch, which consumes the
    39	   * approval inside the gate. The executor must NOT claim it again.
    40	   */
    41	  approvalConsumed?: boolean;
    42	};

    93	/** Write tools whose mutation targets can be scoped to ownedPaths. */

   104	/** Extract the mutation targets from a write-tool's args. */
   105	function mutationTargets(args: Record<string, unknown>): string[] {
   106	  const path = typeof args.path === "string" ? args.path : undefined;
   107	  if (path) return [path];
   108	  const format = typeof args.format === "string" ? args.format : undefined;
   109	  return extractPatchPaths(format, args.patchText);

   112	// Owned-scope matching is `isWithinOwnedScope` (see the Local Contracts in
   113	// src/governance/policy/AGENTS.md). This gate runs BEFORE the file router, so a
   114	// normalization difference between them would silently deny every owned write
   115	// the router allowed — call the shared function directly, do not alias it.
     1	/**
     2	 * ownership-gate.ts — Ownership enforcement for tool execution.
     3	 *
     4	 * Sits AFTER PolicyGate, before workspace/path validation and execution.
     5	 * Delegates all authorization to registry.authorizeMutation() which operates
     6	 * under the ownership lock to reload state, check conflicts, and verify/acquire
     7	 * coverage atomically.
     8	 *
     9	 * Execution order:
    10	 *   argument repair
    11	 *   → request logging
    12	 *   → PolicyGate (skip on continuation-resume)
    13	 *   → OwnershipGate (ALWAYS — even for continuation-resume)
    14	 *   → workspace/path validation
    15	 *   → tool execution
    16	 */
    17	
    18	import type { OwnershipRegistry } from "./ownership-registry.js";
    19	import type { WorkspacePathResolver } from "../../runtime-state/runtime/workspace-path.js";
    20	import type { ToolResult } from "../../capabilities/tools/types.js";
    21	import { extractMutationTargets } from "./mutation-targets.js";
    22	
    23	export type OwnershipGateConfig = {
    24	  registry: OwnershipRegistry;
    25	  resolver: WorkspacePathResolver;
    26	  /**
    27	   * When true, automatically acquires a lease for each confident
    28	   * mutation target as the tool runs.
    29	   * Single-agent default: true. Parallel-agent: false.
    30	   */
    31	  autoAcquire?: boolean;
    32	};
    33	
    34	/**
    35	 * Check ownership for a tool call.
    36	 *
    37	 * Returns null if allowed, or a ToolResult error if blocked.
    38	 *
    39	 * Fail-closed:
    40	 * - unknown-write classification (e.g. shell.run) is denied
    41	 * - autoAcquire=false requires existing exclusive-write coverage
    42	 */
    43	export async function checkOwnershipGate(
    44	  config: OwnershipGateConfig,
    45	  agentId: string,
    46	  toolName: string,
    47	  args: Record<string, unknown>,
    48	  mutates: boolean,
    49	): Promise<ToolResult | null> {
    50	  // Non-mutating tools pass without ownership check
    51	  if (!mutates) return null;
    52	
    53	  // Extract mutation targets with classification
    54	  const extraction = extractMutationTargets(toolName, args, config.resolver);
    55	
    56	  // Fail-closed: unknown-write (shell, patch without target, etc.)
    57	  if (extraction.classification === "unknown-write") {
    58	    return {
    59	      kind: "error",
    60	      message: `Cannot determine mutation targets for ${toolName} — ownership check failed closed. ` +
    61	        `Acquire an explicit lease covering the expected paths and retry.`,
    62	      retryable: false,
    63	    };
    64	  }
    65	
    66	  // no-write tools (read-only shell etc.) pass through
    67	  if (extraction.classification === "no-write") {
    68	    return null;
    69	  }
    70	
    71	  // Delegate to registry which acquires lock, reloads, checks, and persists
    72	  const decision = await config.registry.authorizeMutation({
    73	    agentId,
    74	    targets: extraction.targets,
    75	    autoAcquire: config.autoAcquire !== false,
    76	  });
    77	
    78	  if (!decision.allowed) {
    79	    return {
    80	      kind: "error",
    81	      message: `Ownership check failed: ${decision.reason}`,
    82	      retryable: false,
    83	    };
    84	  }
    85	
    86	  return null; // pass
    87	}

    62	export type ExecuteResult =
    63	  | ToolResult
    64	  | {
    65	      kind: "denied";
    66	      reason: string;
    67	      /**
    68	       * Set on the approval-gated FIRST attempt of `handleToolCall`'s
    69	       * execute-twice flow — the pause that waits for operator resolution and
    70	       * is then re-executed for real. Structurally flagged (design §21); the
    71	       * `reason` string keeps its historical "Approval required (id): …" shape.
    72	       */
    73	      approvalRequired?: true;
    74	      /** The pending approval's id, when `approvalRequired` is set. */
    75	      approvalId?: string;
    76	    };
    77	
    78	/**
    79	 * True when a `denied` result is the approval-gated FIRST attempt in
    80	 * `handleToolCall`'s execute-twice flow. That attempt does not execute the
    81	 * tool — it waits for operator approval and is re-executed for real, so it
    82	 * must NOT emit a terminal span (design §21 exactly-once-per-physical-call).
    83	 * Genuine policy/ownership/mcp denials are NOT this case and keep their single
    84	 * error span.
    85	 *
    86	 * The structured `approvalRequired` flag is the primary signal. The reason
    87	 * prefix fallback keeps hand-constructed denials (tests, tool adapters that
    88	 * build `{ kind: "denied", reason }` directly) classified correctly without
    89	 * requiring them to know the flag.
    90	 */
    91	function isPreApprovalDenial(result: ExecuteResult | null | undefined): boolean {
    92	  return (
    93	    result?.kind === "denied" &&
    94	    (result.approvalRequired === true || /^Approval required \(/.test(result.reason))
    95	  );
    96	}

   175	  /**
   176	   * Authoritative approval read for a call that is WAITING on a decision.
   177	   *
   178	   * The in-memory `get` above reflects only decisions this process made. In a
   179	   * coordination run the operator resolves from the TUI while the worker is a
   180	   * separate execution context, so a wait built solely on `get` would never
   181	   * observe the decision — the worker would sit until its 5-minute timeout and

   187	   * mistaking a broken read for a denial.

   189	  async loadApprovalForWait(id: string): Promise<{ status?: string } | undefined | null> {
   190	    if (!this.approvalStore?.loadFresh) return this.getApproval(id);
    65	  signal?: AbortSignal,
    66	  envAllowlist?: string[],
    67	): { promise: Promise<ToolResult>; cancel: () => void } {
    68	  const child = spawn(command, [], {
    69	    cwd: cwd || undefined,
    70	    shell: true,
    71	    detached: process.platform !== "win32",
    72	    env: buildChildEnv(envAllowlist),
    73	  });
    74	  let stdout = "";
    75	  let stderr = "";
    76	  let settled = false;
    77	
    78	  const promise = new Promise<ToolResult>((resolve, reject) => {
    79	    const onAbort = (): void => {
    80	      if (settled) return;
    81	      settled = true;
    82	      if (signal) signal.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);
    83	      // Kill the child (the operator-abort kill path) and route the outcome
    84	      // to cancellation, never to a "command exited with code" failure.
    85	      killProcessTree(child.pid);
    86	      reject(new ExecutionCancelledError(signalReason(signal) ?? "cancelled by operator"));
    87	    };
    88	    const finish = (result: ToolResult) => {
    89	      if (settled) return;
    90	      settled = true;
    91	      if (signal) signal.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);
    92	      resolve(result);
    93	    };
    94	
    95	    if (signal) {
    96	      // Already-aborted at spawn time: kill the just-spawned child and reject
    97	      // immediately. Otherwise listen — the loop may cancel mid-flight.
    98	      if (signal.aborted) onAbort();
    99	      else signal.addEventListener("abort", onAbort, { once: true });
   100	    }
   101	
   102	    child.stdout.on("data", (chunk) => { stdout += chunk; });
   103	    child.stderr.on("data", (chunk) => { stderr += chunk; });
   104	
   105	    child.on("close", (code) => {
   106	      if (settled) return;
   107	      const combined = stderr ? `${stdout}\n--- stderr ---\n${stderr}` : stdout;
   108	      const output = truncate(combined, MAX_BYTES);
   109	      if ((code ?? 0) !== 0) {
   110	        finish({ kind: "error", message: `Command exited with code ${code}: ${command}\n${output}` });
   111	        return;
   112	      }
   113	      finish({ kind: "success", output, exitCode: code ?? 0 });
   114	    });
   115	
   116	    child.on("error", (err) => {
   117	      finish({ kind: "error", message: `Command failed: ${command} -- ${err.message}` });
   118	    });
   119	  });
   120	
   121	  return {
   122	    promise,
   123	    cancel: () => {
   124	      if (!settled) killProcessTree(child.pid);
   125	    },
   126	  };
   127	}
   128	
   129	function killProcessTree(pid: number | undefined): void {
   130	  if (!pid) return;
   131	  if (process.platform === "win32") {
   132	    // Synchronous: `cancel()` is fire-and-forget and the caller returns the
   133	    // timeout/abort result immediately, so the kill MUST complete before we
   134	    // return — otherwise the child (and any grandchild) outlives the call,
   135	    // leaving the test's temp dir locked (EBUSY) and the "child was killed"
   136	    // assertions racing. `taskkill /T /F` is fast.
   137	    try {
   138	      execFileSync("taskkill", ["/pid", String(pid), "/T", "/F"], { stdio: "ignore", timeout: 5_000 });
   139	    } catch { /* already exited / taskkill unavailable */ }
   140	    return;
   141	  }
   142	  try { process.kill(-pid, "SIGKILL"); } catch {
   143	    try { process.kill(pid, "SIGKILL"); } catch { /* already exited */ }
   144	  }

   493	   *

   497	   * moves the emission here.
   498	   */
   499	  private storeEmitsCreationEvents(): boolean {

   502	      | undefined;
   503	    return store?.emitsLifecycleEvents !== false;
   504	  }

   334	  /** Validate a path through the resolver. Returns error result if blocked. */
   335	  private checkPath(rawPath: string): ToolResult | null {
   336	    const r = this.pathResolver.check(rawPath);
   337	    if (!r.insideWorkspace || !this.pathResolver.isCanonicalInWorkspace(r.absolute)) {
   338	      return { kind: "error", message: "Shell access denied: path is outside workspace (" + r.absolute + ")", retryable: false };
   339	    }
   340	    // Check protected first — user-configured protections take priority over
   341	    // the generic sensitive pattern message for better UX (mirrors FileToolRouter).
   342	    if (r.protected && r.insideWorkspace) {
   343	      return { kind: "error", message: "Shell access denied: path is protected (" + r.absolute + ")" };
   344	    }
   345	    if (r.sensitive) {
   346	      return { kind: "error", message: "Shell access denied: path is sensitive (" + r.absolute + ")" };
   347	    }
   348	    return null;
   349	  }
   350	
   351	  async execute(request: ToolCallRequest): Promise<ToolResult> {
   352	    const { command, cwd, timeoutMs, root: r, persistent } = request.args as {
   353	      command?: string;
   354	      cwd?: string;
   355	      timeoutMs?: number;
   356	      root?: string;
   357	      persistent?: boolean;
   358	    };
   359	
   360	    // Path validation via WorkspacePathResolver
   361	    if (cwd) {
   362	      const blocked = this.checkPath(cwd);
   363	      if (blocked) return blocked;
   364	    }
   365	    if (r) {
   366	      const blocked = this.checkPath(r);

   125	  /**
   126	   * Execute fn inside lock. On failure: clear pending events, reload,
   127	   * rethrow. Events emitted after lock release.
   128	   */
   129	  private async withLock<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T | null> {
   130	    const acquired = await this.lock.acquire();
   131	    if (!acquired) {
   132	      await this.emitEvents([{ event: "ownership.lock_failed", data: { reason: "timeout" } }]);
   133	      return null;
   134	    }
   135	    let events: Array<{ event: string; data: Record<string, unknown> }> = [];
   136	    try {
   137	      this.reloadFromDisk();
   138	      this.applyExpiration();
   139	      this.changed = false;
   140	      const result = await fn();
   141	      this.persistIfChanged();
   142	      events = this.takePendingEvents();
   143	      return result;
   144	    } catch (err) {
   145	      this.pendingEvents = [];
   146	      this.reloadFromDisk();
   147	      throw err;
   148	    } finally {
   149	      this.lock.release();
   150	      await this.emitEvents(events);
   151	    }
   152	  }

   158	  }

   165	    }
   166	  }

DEFECTS

D1 — major — Hard deny bypassed by safe-shell dispatch.
src/capabilities/tools/executor.ts:513 dispatches directly to downstream at :530, before authorization at :534.
Counterexample: ask mode, shell.run: deny, denyCommands: ["ls"], command "ls". A probe executing the extracted source dispatch body reached a mock router once; policy gate calls: zero.
Minimal fix: evaluate mandatory denies before bypassing approval prompts. Add executor-level denied-result and zero-router-call assertions.

D2 — major — Declared ownership does not constrain shell writes.
src/governance/policy/policy-gate.ts:94 limits owned-scope enforcement to file.create, file.delete, patch.apply. Capability allow returns at :331 for shell.run. ShellToolRouter executes arbitrary commands at src/capabilities/tools/tool-router.ts:451 without checking ownedPaths.
A gate probe with ownedPaths ["inside.txt"], shell.run allowed, and "printf x > outside.txt" returned allow. Child executor construction supplies ownedPaths but no ownership registry: src/agents/subagent-cli.ts:723.
Minimal fix: deny unscopable mutation channels for scoped workers, or enforce scope through an actual execution sandbox. Cover shell and dynamic tools explicitly.

D3 — major — Stale-lock takeover can remove a new owner’s live lock.
src/governance/approvals/approval-store-lock.ts:48 checks staleness, then unconditionally removes the directory at :49.
Two processes can observe one stale lock; the delayed contender then deletes the first contender’s replacement lock. Both can load the approved state and claim.
The ledger CAS does not necessarily prevent this: src/governance/approvals/approval-store.ts:308 obtains the latest version during commit, rather than retaining the version read with the approval.
Minimal fix: atomic conditional approved-to-consumed transition against the loaded version, plus race-safe stale-lock recovery. Add deterministic two-process contention coverage.
This is a source-derived interleaving, not an executed race reproduction.

D4 — major — Coordination replay creates replacement authority instead of denying uncertainty.
src/governance/policy/policy-gate.ts:715 recognizes only an approved exact binding. A consumed binding falls through to creation of another pending approval at :739. It is neither classified unverified nor denied.
Minimal fix: explicitly handle consumed coordination bindings before creating requests; assert deny, original unverified state, and no replacement request.

D5 — major — Preconsumed approvals lose execution receipts.
src/capabilities/tools/executor.ts:682 skips both claiming and assigning claimedApprovalId when approvalConsumed is true. Outcome recording at :875 requires that variable.
Consequently, gate-consumed coordination approvals can remain pending after successful execution.
Minimal fix: retain the approval ID for both consumption routes; test through executor, effect, terminal receipt, and replay.

D6 — major — Worker facade is not an exclusive approval-authority boundary.
Normal wiring uses openWorkerApprovalPort: src/agents/subagent-cli.ts:708. But that function itself imports unrestricted ApprovalStore at src/governance/approvals/worker-approval-port.ts:119.
Child spawning provides ordinary process execution under the same user, without an OS authority boundary: src/agents/subagent-manager.ts:364. Approval CLI directly calls store.resolve without worker-origin checks: src/interfaces/cli/commands/approval.ts:106.
A child capable of executing JavaScript or invoking that CLI can reopen the store. The facade narrows an object; it does not confine a compromised process.

Minimal fix: bind identity internally, enforce it inside the locked mutation, and return detached immutable records. Add foreign-consumption, foreign-classification, and record-alias tests.

A gate probe with ownedPaths ["inside.txt"], shell.run allowed, and "printf x > outside.txt" returned allow. Child executor construction supplies ownedPaths but no ownership registry: src/agents/subagent-cli.ts:723.
Minimal fix: deny unscopable mutation channels for scoped workers, or enforce scope through an actual execution sandbox. Cover shell and dynamic tools explicitly.

D3 — major — Stale-lock takeover can remove a new owner’s live lock.
src/governance/approvals/approval-store-lock.ts:48 checks staleness, then unconditionally removes the directory at :49.
Two processes can observe one stale lock; the delayed contender then deletes the first contender’s replacement lock. Both can load the approved state and claim.
The ledger CAS does not necessarily prevent this: src/governance/approvals/approval-store.ts:308 obtains the latest version during commit, rather than retaining the version read with the approval.
Minimal fix: atomic conditional approved-to-consumed transition against the loaded version, plus race-safe stale-lock recovery. Add deterministic two-process contention coverage.
This is a source-derived interleaving, not an executed race reproduction.

Minimal fix: explicitly handle consumed coordination bindings before creating requests; assert deny, original unverified state, and no replacement request.

 succeeded in 0ms:
     1	/**
     2	 * gate-e-qualification-record.mjs — validate a Gate E execution/security record.
     3	 *
     4	 * WHY THIS EXISTS
     5	 *
     6	 * Gate E asks for five things — "F8b, authority, crash/recovery, ownership and
     7	 * denied-action negatives qualified independently" — and the acceptance matrix
     8	 * has never had a record to check. The failure mode is not "no record". It is a
     9	 * record that counts a test file as a qualified control, or drops the word
    10	 * "independently" because the tests pass.
    11	 *
    12	 * So this validator is deliberately hostile in three specific ways:
    13	 *   - every clause must be present; four of five is a HOLD, not 80%
    14	 *   - every clause must cite evidence files that EXIST
    15	 *   - every clause must state the NEGATIVE case, because a positive assertion
    16	 *     does not catch the regression the control exists to prevent
    17	 *   - declared gaps are preserved, never counted as covered
    18	 *   - independence is a separate axis. Author-side tests cannot close it, and
    19	 *     the outcome label says so instead of hiding it in a footnote.
    20	 *
    21	 * What this cannot do: create a second party. `QUALIFIED-AUTHOR-ONLY` is the
    22	 * honest ceiling for a record this repository can produce alone.
    23	 *
    24	 * Usage:
    25	 *   node benchmark/evidence/gate-e-qualification-record.mjs <record.json>
    26	 *
    27	 * Exit codes distinguish "the record is sound" from "the gate is cleared", which
    28	 * are different questions:
    29	 *   0 = qualified INDEPENDENTLY (gate closed)
    30	 *   3 = sound record, author-only coverage (gate NOT closed)
    31	 *   1 = HOLD, 2 = usage error
    32	 *
    33	 * Collapsing 3 into 0 would let a CI step read a passing exit code as a cleared
    34	 * security gate. The distinction is the whole point of the label.
    35	 */
    36	
    37	import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
    38	import { resolve } from 'node:path';
    39	import {
    40	  PATH_BASES,
    41	  isEntryPoint,
    42	  isIsoTimestamp,
    43	  nonEmpty,
    44	  resolveCited,
    45	  runRecordCli,
    46	} from './record-validation.mjs';
    47	
    48	/**
    49	 * The five clauses of Gate E, frozen from PRD §9.
    50	 * An unknown clause is a validation error, not an extra credit.
    51	 */
    52	export const GATE_E_CLAUSES = ['F8b', 'authority', 'crash/recovery', 'ownership', 'denied-action negatives'];
    53	
    54	/**
    55	 * Independence classes. There is no `independent` value in this vocabulary:
    56	 * a record cannot certify its own independence, so a record that claimed it
    57	 * would have to be trusted on the one point it cannot establish.
    58	 */
    59	export const INDEPENDENCE_CLASSES = ['author-only', 'model-independent', 'declared-independent'];
    60	
    61	/** Per-clause observation states. */
    62	export const COMPONENT_STATES = ['qualified', 'partial', 'unqualified'];
    63	
    64	/** Gate E outcomes. Independence upgrades the label; it never upgrades coverage. */
    65	export { PATH_BASES } from './record-validation.mjs';
    66	
    67	export const GATE_E_OUTCOMES = {
    68	  independent: 'QUALIFIED-INDEPENDENT',
    69	  authorOnly: 'QUALIFIED-AUTHOR-ONLY',
    70	  hold: 'HOLD',
    71	};
    72	
    73	/** D9: what may stand as evidence for a control. */
    74	export const EVIDENCE_PATH_PATTERN = /\.(test|spec)\.(ts|mts|js|mjs)$|\.vitest\.ts$|^src\//;
    75	
    76	/**
    77	 * Validate a Gate E qualification record.
    78	 *
    79	 * `problems` are reasons the record cannot be used at all.
    80	 * `declaredGaps` are accepted limitations and never produce a problem — they are
    81	 * the opposite: hiding one WOULD.
    82	 */
    83	export function validateGateERecord(record, options = {}) {
    84	  const baseDir = options.baseDir ? resolve(options.baseDir) : process.cwd();
    85	  const problems = [];
    86	  const notes = [];
    87	
    88	  if (!record || typeof record !== 'object' || Array.isArray(record)) {
    89	    return {
    90	      ok: false,
    91	      problems: ['record must be an object'],
    92	      notes,
    93	      summary: null,
    94	      outcome: GATE_E_OUTCOMES.hold,
    95	    };
    96	  }
    97	
    98	  // ── Artifact pin ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    99	  const artifact = record.artifact;
   100	  if (!artifact || typeof artifact !== 'object' || Array.isArray(artifact)) {
   101	    problems.push('artifact is required: a qualification must name the commit it qualified');
   102	  } else if (!/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/.test(String(artifact.commit ?? ''))) {
   103	    problems.push('artifact.commit must be a full 40-character commit sha');
   104	  }
   105	  if (!Number.isFinite(Date.parse(record.observedAt))) {
   106	    problems.push('observedAt must be an ISO timestamp: a stale record is not a qualification');
   107	  }
   108	
   109	  // A record must declare how its citations resolve. Guessing is how a path
   110	  // check becomes decorative: it either rejects valid citations or accepts
   111	  // nonexistent ones, and both look like a working check.
   112	  const pathBase = record.pathBase;
   113	  if (!PATH_BASES.includes(pathBase)) {
   114	    problems.push(
   115	      `pathBase must be one of ${PATH_BASES.join('|')} and must be explicit: cited paths resolve either beside the record ("record") or from the repository root ("repo-root")`,
   116	    );
   117	  }
   118	
   119	  // ── Runs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   120	  // A record with no runs is a description of intent. It must carry what was
   121	  // actually executed, with counts, so a failing suite cannot hide behind prose.
   122	  const runs = Array.isArray(record.runs) ? record.runs : null;
   123	  if (!runs || runs.length === 0) {
   124	    problems.push('runs is required: a qualification must record what was executed, not what exists');
   125	  } else {
   126	    let totalTests = 0;
   127	    let totalPassed = 0;
   128	    for (const [index, run] of runs.entries()) {
   129	      const at = `runs[${index}]`;
   130	      if (!run || typeof run !== 'object') {
   131	        problems.push(`${at} is not an object`);
   132	        continue;
   133	      }
   134	      if (!nonEmpty(run.runner)) problems.push(`${at}.runner is required`);
   135	      // D9: a runner NAME proves nothing — the review's probe passed
   136	      // "IMAGINARY-RUNNER" and was accepted. Requiring the exact command makes
   137	      // the claim falsifiable: a third party can re-run it and compare counts.
   138	      if (!nonEmpty(run.command)) {
   139	        problems.push(
   140	          `${at}.command is required: a runner name is not reproducible, the exact invocation is`,
   141	        );
   142	      } else {
   143	        for (const file of Array.isArray(run.files) ? run.files : []) {
   144	          if (!nonEmpty(file)) continue;
   145	          // Compare stem + extension, because a compiled run names
   146	          // `dist/tests/x.test.js` for a source file `tests/x.test.ts`.
   147	          const stem = file.replace(/\.(ts|mts)$/, "");
   148	          if (!run.command.includes(stem) && !run.command.includes(file)) {
   149	            problems.push(
   150	              `${at}.command does not reference ${file}: the command must be the one that ran those files`,
   151	            );
   152	          }
   153	        }
   154	      }
   155	      if (!Array.isArray(run.files) || run.files.length === 0) {
   156	        problems.push(`${at}.files is required: name the files that ran`);
   157	      } else {
   158	        for (const file of run.files) {
   159	          if (!nonEmpty(file)) {
   160	            problems.push(`${at}.files contains an empty path`);
   161	          } else if (pathBase && !existsSync(resolveCited(file, baseDir, pathBase))) {
   162	            problems.push(`${at}.files cites a path that does not exist: ${file}`);
   163	          }
   164	        }
   165	      }
   166	      if (!Number.isInteger(run.tests) || run.tests <= 0) {
   167	        problems.push(`${at}.tests must be a positive integer`);
   168	      }
   169	      if (!Number.isInteger(run.passed) || run.passed < 0) {
   170	        problems.push(`${at}.passed must be a non-negative integer`);
   171	      }
   172	      if (run.failed !== 0) {
   173	        problems.push(`${at}.failed is ${String(run.failed)}: a qualification cannot be built on a failing suite`);
   174	      }
   175	      if (!Number.isInteger(run.passed) || (Number.isInteger(run.tests) && Number.isInteger(run.passed) && run.passed !== run.tests)) {
   176	        problems.push(`${at}: passed (${String(run.passed)}) does not equal tests (${String(run.tests)})`);
   177	      }
   178	      if (Number.isInteger(run.tests)) totalTests += run.tests;
   179	      if (Number.isInteger(run.passed)) totalPassed += run.passed;
   180	    }
   181	    if (totalTests > 0) notes.push(`observed: ${totalPassed}/${totalTests} tests passed in this run`);
   182	  }
   183	
   184	  // ── Components: all five clauses, each with a negative case and real evidence
   185	  const components = Array.isArray(record.components) ? record.components : null;
   186	  const seen = new Set();
   187	  const counts = { qualified: 0, partial: 0, unqualified: 0 };
   188	  if (!components) {
   189	    problems.push('components must be an array: Gate E is five clauses, not one verdict');
   190	  } else {
   191	    for (const [index, component] of components.entries()) {
   192	      const at = `components[${index}]`;
   193	      if (!component || typeof component !== 'object') {
   194	        problems.push(`${at} is not an object`);
   195	        continue;
   196	      }
   197	      const clause = component.clause;
   198	      if (!GATE_E_CLAUSES.includes(clause)) {
   199	        // A near-miss is the interesting failure: "denied action" vs
   200	        // "denied-action negatives" would silently drop a required clause.
   201	        problems.push(`${at} has an unknown Gate E clause: ${String(clause)}`);
   202	        continue;
   203	      }
   204	      if (seen.has(clause)) problems.push(`clause ${clause} is recorded more than once`);
   205	      seen.add(clause);
   206	
   207	      if (!COMPONENT_STATES.includes(component.observed)) {
   208	        problems.push(`${clause} has an invalid observed state: ${String(component.observed)}`);
   209	      } else {
   210	        counts[component.observed] += 1;
   211	      }
   212	
   213	      if (!nonEmpty(component.question)) {
   214	        problems.push(`${clause} has no question: a control must state what it is being asked to prove`);
   215	      }
   216	
   217	      // The negative case is the whole point of a security control. Without it
   218	      // the record asserts that something works, not that removing it would fail.
   219	      if (!nonEmpty(component.negativeCase)) {
   220	        problems.push(
   221	          `${clause} does not state its negative case: a positive assertion does not catch the regression the control exists to prevent`,
   222	        );
   223	      }
   224	
   225	      if (!Array.isArray(component.evidence) || component.evidence.length === 0) {
   226	        problems.push(`${clause} cites no evidence files`);
   227	      } else {
   228	        for (const file of component.evidence) {
   229	          if (!nonEmpty(file)) {
   230	            problems.push(`${clause} cites an empty evidence path`);
   231	          } else if (pathBase && !existsSync(resolveCited(file, baseDir, pathBase))) {
   232	            problems.push(`${clause} cites a path that does not exist: ${file}`);
   233	          } else if (!EVIDENCE_PATH_PATTERN.test(file)) {
   234	            // D9: the probe used package.json as every clause's evidence and was
   235	            // accepted. Evidence for a control must be code that can assert it —
   236	            // a test or the implementation under test.
   237	            problems.push(
   238	              `${clause} cites ${file}, which cannot assert a control: evidence must be a test or source file`,
   239	            );
   240	          }
   241	        }
   242	      }
   243	    }
   244	    for (const clause of GATE_E_CLAUSES) {
   245	      if (!seen.has(clause)) problems.push(`clause ${clause} has no entry: Gate E requires all five`);
   246	    }
   247	  }
   248	
   249	  // ── Declared gaps ───────────────────────────────────────────────
   250	  // Presence is required. An empty list is legitimate; an ABSENT list usually
   251	  // means gaps were dropped rather than none found.
   252	  if (!Array.isArray(record.declaredGaps)) {
   253	    problems.push(
   254	      'declaredGaps must be present (may be empty): a record that reports no gaps must say so explicitly, not by omission',
   255	    );
   256	  } else {
   257	    for (const [index, gap] of record.declaredGaps.entries()) {
   258	      if (!gap || typeof gap !== 'object') {
   259	        problems.push(`declaredGaps[${index}] is not an object`);
   260	        continue;
   261	      }
   262	      if (!nonEmpty(gap.id)) problems.push(`declaredGaps[${index}] has no id`);
   263	      if (!nonEmpty(gap.gap)) problems.push(`declaredGaps[${index}] has no gap description`);
   264	    }
   265	    if (record.declaredGaps.length > 0) {
   266	      notes.push(
   267	        `gaps preserved, NOT covered: ${record.declaredGaps.map(g => g.id).join(', ')}`,
   268	      );
   269	    }
   270	  }
   271	
   272	  // ── Independence ────────────────────────────────────────────────
   273	  const independence = record.independence;
   274	  let independenceClass = 'unknown';
   275	  if (!independence || typeof independence !== 'object' || Array.isArray(independence)) {
   276	    problems.push('independence is required: Gate E specifies "qualified independently" and the class must be stated');
   277	  } else {
   278	    if (!INDEPENDENCE_CLASSES.includes(independence.class)) {
   279	      problems.push(`independence.class must be one of ${INDEPENDENCE_CLASSES.join('|')}; got ${String(independence.class)}`);
   280	    } else {
   281	      independenceClass = independence.class;
   282	    }
   283	    if (independenceClass !== 'author-only' && !nonEmpty(independence.note)) {
   284	      problems.push('independence.note is required when independence is claimed: say how it was obtained');
   285	    }
   286	    // Independent review D9: changing `class` to `declared-independent` plus a
   287	    // free-text note produced QUALIFIED-INDEPENDENT, so the strongest label in
   288	    // the vocabulary was reachable by typing it. Independence must be a CITED
   289	    // artifact that exists and names the qualifier — the same rule Gate B's
   290	    // waiver and Gate F's approval already enforce.
   291	    if (independenceClass !== 'author-only') {
   292	      const qualifier = independence.qualifier;
   293	      if (!qualifier || typeof qualifier !== 'object' || Array.isArray(qualifier)) {
   294	        problems.push(
   295	          `${independenceClass} requires independence.qualifier {ref, identity, reviewedAt}: a record may not declare its own independence from free text`,
   296	        );
   297	      } else {
   298	        if (!nonEmpty(qualifier.identity)) {
   299	          problems.push('independence.qualifier.identity is required: an independent qualifier must be named');
   300	        }
   301	        if (!Number.isFinite(Date.parse(qualifier.reviewedAt))) {
   302	          problems.push('independence.qualifier.reviewedAt must be an ISO timestamp');
   303	        }
   304	        if (!nonEmpty(qualifier.ref)) {
   305	          problems.push('independence.qualifier.ref is required: name the artifact holding the review');
   306	        } else if (pathBase) {
   307	          const qualifierPath = resolveCited(qualifier.ref, baseDir, pathBase);
   308	          if (!existsSync(qualifierPath)) {
   309	            problems.push(`independence.qualifier.ref does not exist: ${qualifier.ref}`);
   310	          } else if (nonEmpty(qualifier.identity)) {
   311	            let body = '';
   312	            try {
   313	              body = readFileSync(qualifierPath, 'utf-8');
   314	            } catch {
   315	              problems.push(`independence.qualifier.ref is unreadable: ${qualifier.ref}`);
   316	            }
   317	            if (body && !body.includes(qualifier.identity.trim())) {
   318	              problems.push(
   319	                `independence.qualifier.ref does not contain the named qualifier: ${qualifier.identity}`,
   320	              );
   321	            }
   322	          }
   323	        }
   324	      }
   325	    }
   326	  }
   327	
   328	  // ── Outcome ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   329	  // Coverage and independence are separate axes. A perfect author-side record is
   330	  // still author-only, and the label must carry that rather than implying more.
   331	  const allQualified =
   332	    !!components &&
   333	    seen.size === GATE_E_CLAUSES.length &&
   334	    counts.qualified === GATE_E_CLAUSES.length;
   335	
   336	  let outcome = GATE_E_OUTCOMES.hold;
   337	  if (problems.length === 0 && allQualified) {
   338	    outcome = independenceClass === 'author-only'
   339	      ? GATE_E_OUTCOMES.authorOnly
   340	      : GATE_E_OUTCOMES.independent;
   341	  }
   342	
   343	  if (outcome === GATE_E_OUTCOMES.authorOnly) {
   344	    notes.push(
   345	      'author-side qualification only: Gate E requires independent qualification, and passing tests authored with the code are not a second party',
   346	    );
   347	    notes.push('this does not clear Gate E; it records the coverage an independent qualifier would review');
   348	  }
   349	
   350	  return {
   351	    ok: problems.length === 0,
   352	    problems,
   353	    notes,
   354	    outcome,
   355	    summary: {
   356	      clauses: GATE_E_CLAUSES.length,
   357	      recorded: seen.size,
   358	      ...counts,
   359	      declaredGaps: Array.isArray(record.declaredGaps) ? record.declaredGaps.length : null,
   360	      independence: independenceClass,
   361	      outcome,
   362	    },
   363	  };
   364	}
   365	
   366	/** Render a validated record for an operator to read, never to sign blind. */
   367	export function renderGateEReport(result) {
   368	  const lines = [];
   369	  lines.push(`valid: ${result.ok}`);
   370	  lines.push(`gate E: ${result.outcome}`);
   371	  if (result.summary) {
   372	    const s = result.summary;
   373	    lines.push(
   374	      `clauses: ${s.recorded}/${s.clauses} (qualified ${s.qualified}, partial ${s.partial}, unqualified ${s.unqualified})`,
   375	    );
   376	    lines.push(`independence: ${s.independence}`);
   377	    if (s.declaredGaps !== null) lines.push(`declared gaps: ${s.declaredGaps}`);
   378	  }
   379	  for (const note of result.notes) lines.push(`note: ${note}`);
   380	  if (result.problems.length > 0) {
   381	    lines.push('problems:');
   382	    for (const problem of result.problems) lines.push(`  - ${problem}`);
   383	  }
   384	  return lines.join('\n');
   385	}
   386	
   387	if (isEntryPoint(import.meta.url, process.argv)) {
   388	  runRecordCli({
   389	    argv: process.argv,
   390	    usage: 'node benchmark/evidence/gate-e-qualification-record.mjs <record.json>',
   391	    render: renderGateEReport,
   392	    validate: validateGateERecord,
   393	    // Exit codes must never collapse "valid" into "cleared": a HOLD is non-zero
   394	    // whether or not the record itself is well-formed, and a sound author-only
   395	    // record is 3 so a pipeline cannot read it as a cleared gate.
   396	    exitCodeFor: (result) =>
   397	      result.outcome === GATE_E_OUTCOMES.hold
   398	        ? 1
   399	        : !result.ok
   400	          ? 1
   401	          : result.outcome === GATE_E_OUTCOMES.authorOnly
   402	            ? 3
   403	            : 0,
   404	  });
   405	}

 succeeded in 0ms:
     1	/**
     2	 * worker-approval-port.ts — a RESTRICTED view of the authoritative approval
     3	 * ledger for isolated coordination worker processes.
     4	 *
     5	 * A subagent worker runs as its own OS process, so it cannot receive the
     6	 * parent's in-memory `ApprovalStore`. It needs the durable ledger to request
     7	 * and observe tool-level approvals — but handing a child a full `ApprovalStore`
     8	 * would let it call `resolve(...)` and APPROVE ITS OWN REQUEST, which is
     9	 * authority escalation (a compromised worker could grant itself any
    10	 * capability).
    11	 *
    12	 * This port exposes exactly the operations a worker legitimately needs and
    13	 * nothing else:
    14	 *
    15	 *   allowed   read a record by id / binding key / pending capability
    16	 *             create-or-reuse a pending request bound to this worker
    17	 *             atomically consume an APPROVED record it is authorized to use
    18	 *             report its own execution outcome
    19	 *
    20	 *   forbidden approve / deny / revoke / invalidate / group resolution /
    21	 *             mutating another worker's record
    22	 *
    23	 * Consumption is NOT reimplemented here: `consumeApproved` runs inside the
    24	 * store's cross-process lock and re-validates status, expiry, binding key and
    25	 * invocation under that lock, so two processes cannot both consume one
    26	 * single-use approval. The port is a narrowing layer, never a second authority:
    27	 * it always delegates to a store instance opened on the SAME workspace.
    28	 *
    29	 * Decisions stay operator-controlled: `resolve`, `resolveWithEvidence`,
    30	 * `resolveGroup`, `revoke` and `invalidate` are not reachable, so no method on
    31	 * this port can move a request to `approved`. A worker CAN report the outcome of
    32	 * an execution it performed, but only for a record it owns — see
    33	 * `recordExecutionOutcome` below.
    34	 */
    35	
    36	import type { ApprovalStore } from "../../governance/approvals/approval-store.js";
    37	import type { ApprovalRecord } from "../../governance/approvals/approval-types.js";
    38	/** The operations a worker process may perform against the ledger. */
    39	export interface WorkerApprovalPort {
    40	  /** Current durable record, or undefined when it does not exist. */
    41	  get(id: string): ApprovalRecord | undefined;
    42	  /** Authoritative re-read from the ledger (cross-process visibility). */
    43	  loadFresh(id: string): Promise<ApprovalRecord | undefined>;
    44	  /** Look up by the exact binding key an approval was created with. */
    45	  findExact(bindingKey: string): ApprovalRecord | undefined;
    46	  /** A pending approval for this binding key, if one exists. */
    47	  findPendingByBindingKey(bindingKey: string): ApprovalRecord | undefined;
    48	  /** A pending approval for a capability (legacy, non-coordination path). */
    49	  findPending(query: { capability: string }): ApprovalRecord | undefined;
    50	  /**
    51	   * Most recent NON-pending record for a graph/node/capability. Read-only.
    52	   * Needed by the auto-mode branch, which reuses a prior resolution.
    53	   */
    54	  findResolved(opts: { graphId?: string; nodeId?: string; capability?: string }): ApprovalRecord | undefined;
    55	  /**
    56	   * Most recent record for a stable request id (typically the toolCallId).
    57	   *
    58	   * Required by `PolicyGate`'s legacy de-dup branch: after the operator approves,
    59	   * the agent loop re-evaluates the SAME tool call, and without this lookup it
    60	   * mints a second approval instead of honouring the first — the
    61	   * "many pending approvals pile up" failure. Optional chaining at the call site
    62	   * means omitting it here fails SILENTLY, so it must be exposed.
    63	   */
    64	  findByRequestId(requestId: string): ApprovalRecord | undefined;
    65	  /**
    66	   * Create a fresh PENDING approval (legacy capability path).
    67	   *
    68	   * Safe for a worker: it can only ever mint `pending`. Reconciliation of that
    69	   * request requires an operator decision through a path this port does not
    70	   * expose.
    71	   */
    72	  request(opts: Parameters<ApprovalStore["request"]>[0]): Promise<ApprovalRecord>;
    73	  /** Create-or-reuse the pending request for an exact binding. */
    74	  requestOrReusePending(input: Parameters<ApprovalStore["requestOrReusePending"]>[0]): Promise<ApprovalRecord>;
    75	  /** Atomically claim an approved record. Single-use across processes. */
    76	  consumeApproved: ApprovalStore["consumeApproved"];
    77	  /**
    78	   * Report the outcome of an execution THIS worker performed.
    79	   *
    80	   * Scope-limited by the worker identity and optional attempt captured at
    81	   * construction: original and consumption bindings must all match. Only
    82	   * records without either binding retain legacy access. Without this, a worker
    83	   * holding a consumed id could falsify another worker's receipt. The store checks this
    84	   * trusted scope against fresh ledger state inside its mutation lock.
    85	   *
    86	   * Returns the store's own boolean: `true` only when the transition landed.
    87	   */
    88	  recordExecutionOutcome(
    89	    id: string,
    90	    outcome: "succeeded" | "failed" | "cancelled",
    91	  ): Promise<boolean>;
    92	  /** Re-read the ledger so cross-process decisions become visible. */
    93	  load(): Promise<void>;
    94	  /**
    95	   * Classify a still-`pending` consumed claim as `unverified` (terminal,
    96	   * fail-closed). Exposed so `PolicyGate`'s consumed-replay branch can report an
    97	   * exact reason instead of silently degrading to "already consumed".
    98	   */
    99	  markExecutionUnverified?(id: string): Promise<"unverified" | "pending" | "terminal" | "missing">;
   100	}
   101	
   102	/**
   103	 * Open the restricted worker view for an isolated process.
   104	 *
   105	 * This is the ONE sanctioned ApprovalStore construction seam for worker
   106	 * processes (pinned by the R1 boundary freeze): a child cannot receive the
   107	 * parent's in-memory store, so it opens its own instance on the SAME
   108	 * authoritative workspace. Callers pass the workspace they were spawned in —
   109	 * never a config-derived or guessed path — so a worker can never accidentally
   110	 * read a different `.alix` directory.
   111	 *
   112	 * Throws when the ledger cannot be opened or loaded; callers must treat that
   113	 * as "no approval authority" and keep gated operations denied.
   114	 */
   115	export async function openWorkerApprovalPort(
   116	  workspace: string,
   117	  options: { eventLog?: unknown; workerId?: string; workerAttempt?: number } = {},
   118	): Promise<WorkerApprovalPort> {
   119	  const { ApprovalStore } = await import("../../governance/approvals/approval-store.js");
   120	  const store = new ApprovalStore(
   121	    workspace,
   122	    options.eventLog ? { eventLog: options.eventLog as never } : {},
   123	  );
   124	  await store.load();
   125	  return createWorkerApprovalPort(store, { workerId: options.workerId, workerAttempt: options.workerAttempt });
   126	}
   127	
   128	/** Methods that would let a worker authorize its own operations. */
   129	const FORBIDDEN = [
   130	  "resolve",
   131	  "resolveWithEvidence",
   132	  "resolveGroup",
   133	  "revoke",
   134	  "invalidate",
   135	  "append",
   136	  "mutate",
   137	] as const;
   138	
   139	/**
   140	 * Throw if a candidate worker view exposes any decision-recording method.
   141	 *
   142	 * Exported so it can be exercised directly. The previous version of this check
   143	 * lived inline and its test constructed a port from a CLEAN store and asserted
   144	 * the methods were absent — which is true by construction, so the test passed
   145	 * even with this function deleted. A reviewer deleted the guard and all 14 tests
   146	 * stayed green (Gate E review, vacuous assertion #1).
   147	 *
   148	 * A guard that cannot be made to fire is not a guard. Testing it needs a
   149	 * contaminated candidate, and that is what the export exists for.
   150	 */
   151	export function assertNoForbiddenDecisionMethods(candidate: object): void {
   152	  for (const method of FORBIDDEN) {
   153	    if (method in candidate) {
   154	      throw new Error(`WorkerApprovalPort must not expose "${method}"`);
   155	    }
   156	  }
   157	}
   158	
   159	/**
   160	 * Build the restricted worker view over a store instance opened on the worker's
   161	 * own authoritative workspace.
   162	 *
   163	 * The returned object is a plain facade with only the allowed methods, so a
   164	 * worker's tool executor and PolicyGate behave exactly as they do in the parent
   165	 * without ever holding a decision-recording handle.
   166	 */
   167	export function createWorkerApprovalPort(
   168	  store: ApprovalStore,
   169	  options: { workerId?: string; workerAttempt?: number } = {},
   170	): WorkerApprovalPort {
   171	  const boundWorkerId = options.workerId;
   172	  const boundWorkerAttempt = options.workerAttempt;
   173	  // A bound worker can only observe its own records and explicitly legacy
   174	  // unbound approvals. An unbound compatibility port cannot observe records
   175	  // owned by any worker. Do not leak metadata via alternate lookup methods.
   176	  const visible = (record: ApprovalRecord | undefined): ApprovalRecord | undefined =>
   177	    record && (boundWorkerId ? record.workerId === boundWorkerId && (boundWorkerAttempt === undefined || record.workerAttempt === boundWorkerAttempt) : !record.workerId) ? record : undefined;
   178	  const port: WorkerApprovalPort = {
   179	    get: (id) => visible(store.get(id)),
   180	    loadFresh: async (id) => visible(await store.loadFresh(id)),
   181	    findExact: (bindingKey) => visible(store.findExact(bindingKey)),
   182	    findPendingByBindingKey: (bindingKey) => visible(store.findPendingByBindingKey(bindingKey)),
   183	    findPending: (query) => visible(store.findPending(query)),
   184	    findResolved: (opts) => visible(store.findResolved(opts)),
   185	    findByRequestId: (requestId) => visible(store.findByRequestId(requestId)),
   186	    request: (opts) => store.request(boundWorkerId ? { ...opts, workerId: boundWorkerId, workerAttempt: boundWorkerAttempt } : opts),
   187	    requestOrReusePending: (input) => {
   188	      if (boundWorkerId && input.workerId && input.workerId !== boundWorkerId) {
   189	        throw new Error("worker approval request identity mismatch");
   190	      }
   191	      return store.requestOrReusePending(boundWorkerId ? { ...input, workerId: boundWorkerId, workerAttempt: boundWorkerAttempt } : input);
   192	    },
   193	    consumeApproved: (id, bindingKey, consumer, invocation) => {
   194	      if (boundWorkerId && consumer.workerId && consumer.workerId !== boundWorkerId) {
   195	        return Promise.resolve({ consumed: false, reason: "worker mismatch" });
   196	      }
   197	      // consumeApproved reloads under the store lock and enforces worker/attempt
   198	      // identity atomically. A cached get() can be stale across processes.
   199	      return store.consumeApproved(id, bindingKey, boundWorkerId ? { ...consumer, workerId: boundWorkerId, workerAttempt: boundWorkerAttempt, requireWorkerBinding: true } : consumer, invocation);
   200	    },
   201	    recordExecutionOutcome: (id, outcome) =>
   202	      store.recordExecutionOutcome(id, outcome, { workerId: boundWorkerId, workerAttempt: boundWorkerAttempt }),
   203	    load: () => store.load(),
   204	    markExecutionUnverified: (id) =>
   205	      store.markExecutionUnverified(id, { workerId: boundWorkerId, workerAttempt: boundWorkerAttempt }),
   206	  };
   207	
   208	  // Structural guarantee, not a convention: no forbidden method is reachable
   209	  // from the object a worker receives. A future refactor that added one would
   210	  // fail this check immediately.
   211	  assertNoForbiddenDecisionMethods(port);
   212	  return port;
   213	}

     1	/**
     2	 * gate-e-qualification-record.mjs — validate a Gate E execution/security record.
     3	 *
     4	 * WHY THIS EXISTS
     5	 *
     6	 * Gate E asks for five things — "F8b, authority, crash/recovery, ownership and
     7	 * denied-action negatives qualified independently" — and the acceptance matrix
     8	 * has never had a record to check. The failure mode is not "no record". It is a
     9	 * record that counts a test file as a qualified control, or drops the word
    10	 * "independently" because the tests pass.
    11	 *
    12	 * So this validator is deliberately hostile in three specific ways:
    13	 *   - every clause must be present; four of five is a HOLD, not 80%
    14	 *   - every clause must cite evidence files that EXIST
    15	 *   - every clause must state the NEGATIVE case, because a positive assertion
    16	 *     does not catch the regression the control exists to prevent
    17	 *   - declared gaps are preserved, never counted as covered
    18	 *   - independence is a separate axis. Author-side tests cannot close it, and
    19	 *     the outcome label says so instead of hiding it in a footnote.
    20	 *
    21	 * What this cannot do: create a second party. `QUALIFIED-AUTHOR-ONLY` is the
    22	 * honest ceiling for a record this repository can produce alone.
    23	 *
    24	 * Usage:
    25	 *   node benchmark/evidence/gate-e-qualification-record.mjs <record.json>
    26	 *
    27	 * Exit codes distinguish "the record is sound" from "the gate is cleared", which
    28	 * are different questions:
    29	 *   0 = qualified INDEPENDENTLY (gate closed)
    30	 *   3 = sound record, author-only coverage (gate NOT closed)
    31	 *   1 = HOLD, 2 = usage error
    32	 *
    33	 * Collapsing 3 into 0 would let a CI step read a passing exit code as a cleared
    34	 * security gate. The distinction is the whole point of the label.
    35	 */
    36	
    37	import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
    38	import { resolve } from 'node:path';
    39	import {
    40	  PATH_BASES,
    41	  isEntryPoint,
    42	  isIsoTimestamp,
    43	  nonEmpty,
    44	  resolveCited,
    45	  runRecordCli,
    46	} from './record-validation.mjs';
    47	
    48	/**
    49	 * The five clauses of Gate E, frozen from PRD §9.
    50	 * An unknown clause is a validation error, not an extra credit.
    51	 */
    52	export const GATE_E_CLAUSES = ['F8b', 'authority', 'crash/recovery', 'ownership', 'denied-action negatives'];
    53	
    54	/**
    55	 * Independence classes. There is no `independent` value in this vocabulary:
    56	 * a record cannot certify its own independence, so a record that claimed it
    57	 * would have to be trusted on the one point it cannot establish.
    58	 */
    59	export const INDEPENDENCE_CLASSES = ['author-only', 'model-independent', 'declared-independent'];
    60	
    61	/** Per-clause observation states. */
    62	export const COMPONENT_STATES = ['qualified', 'partial', 'unqualified'];
    63	
    64	/** Gate E outcomes. Independence upgrades the label; it never upgrades coverage. */
    65	export { PATH_BASES } from './record-validation.mjs';
    66	
    67	export const GATE_E_OUTCOMES = {
    68	  independent: 'QUALIFIED-INDEPENDENT',
    69	  authorOnly: 'QUALIFIED-AUTHOR-ONLY',
    70	  hold: 'HOLD',
    71	};
    72	
    73	/** D9: what may stand as evidence for a control. */
    74	export const EVIDENCE_PATH_PATTERN = /\.(test|spec)\.(ts|mts|js|mjs)$|\.vitest\.ts$|^src\//;
    75	
    76	/**
    77	 * Validate a Gate E qualification record.
    78	 *
    79	 * `problems` are reasons the record cannot be used at all.
    80	 * `declaredGaps` are accepted limitations and never produce a problem — they are
    81	 * the opposite: hiding one WOULD.
    82	 */
    83	export function validateGateERecord(record, options = {}) {
    84	  const baseDir = options.baseDir ? resolve(options.baseDir) : process.cwd();
    85	  const problems = [];
    86	  const notes = [];
    87	
    88	  if (!record || typeof record !== 'object' || Array.isArray(record)) {
    89	    return {
    90	      ok: false,
    91	      problems: ['record must be an object'],
    92	      notes,
    93	      summary: null,
    94	      outcome: GATE_E_OUTCOMES.hold,
    95	    };
    96	  }
    97	
    98	  // ── Artifact pin ────────────────────────────────────────────────
    99	  const artifact = record.artifact;
   100	  if (!artifact || typeof artifact !== 'object' || Array.isArray(artifact)) {
   101	    problems.push('artifact is required: a qualification must name the commit it qualified');
   102	  } else if (!/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/.test(String(artifact.commit ?? ''))) {
   103	    problems.push('artifact.commit must be a full 40-character commit sha');
   104	  }
   105	  if (!Number.isFinite(Date.parse(record.observedAt))) {
   106	    problems.push('observedAt must be an ISO timestamp: a stale record is not a qualification');
   107	  }
   108	
   109	  // A record must declare how its citations resolve. Guessing is how a path
   110	  // check becomes decorative: it either rejects valid citations or accepts
   111	  // nonexistent ones, and both look like a working check.
   112	  const pathBase = record.pathBase;
   113	  if (!PATH_BASES.includes(pathBase)) {
   114	    problems.push(
   115	      `pathBase must be one of ${PATH_BASES.join('|')} and must be explicit: cited paths resolve either beside the record ("record") or from the repository root ("repo-root")`,
   116	    );
   117	  }
   118	
   119	  // ── Runs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   120	  // A record with no runs is a description of intent. It must carry what was
   121	  // actually executed, with counts, so a failing suite cannot hide behind prose.
   122	  const runs = Array.isArray(record.runs) ? record.runs : null;
   123	  if (!runs || runs.length === 0) {
   124	    problems.push('runs is required: a qualification must record what was executed, not what exists');
   125	  } else {
   126	    let totalTests = 0;
   127	    let totalPassed = 0;
   128	    for (const [index, run] of runs.entries()) {
   129	      const at = `runs[${index}]`;
   130	      if (!run || typeof run !== 'object') {
   131	        problems.push(`${at} is not an object`);
   132	        continue;
   133	      }
   134	      if (!nonEmpty(run.runner)) problems.push(`${at}.runner is required`);
   135	      // D9: a runner NAME proves nothing — the review's probe passed
   136	      // "IMAGINARY-RUNNER" and was accepted. Requiring the exact command makes
   137	      // the claim falsifiable: a third party can re-run it and compare counts.
   138	      if (!nonEmpty(run.command)) {
   139	        problems.push(
   140	          `${at}.command is required: a runner name is not reproducible, the exact invocation is`,
   141	        );
   142	      } else {
   143	        for (const file of Array.isArray(run.files) ? run.files : []) {
   144	          if (!nonEmpty(file)) continue;
   145	          // Compare stem + extension, because a compiled run names
   146	          // `dist/tests/x.test.js` for a source file `tests/x.test.ts`.
   147	          const stem = file.replace(/\.(ts|mts)$/, "");
   148	          if (!run.command.includes(stem) && !run.command.includes(file)) {
   149	            problems.push(
   150	              `${at}.command does not reference ${file}: the command must be the one that ran those files`,
   151	            );
   152	          }
   153	        }
   154	      }
   155	      if (!Array.isArray(run.files) || run.files.length === 0) {
   156	        problems.push(`${at}.files is required: name the files that ran`);
   157	      } else {
   158	        for (const file of run.files) {
   159	          if (!nonEmpty(file)) {
   160	            problems.push(`${at}.files contains an empty path`);
   161	          } else if (pathBase && !existsSync(resolveCited(file, baseDir, pathBase))) {
   162	            problems.push(`${at}.files cites a path that does not exist: ${file}`);
   163	          }
   164	        }
   165	      }
   166	      if (!Number.isInteger(run.tests) || run.tests <= 0) {
   167	        problems.push(`${at}.tests must be a positive integer`);
   168	      }
   169	      if (!Number.isInteger(run.passed) || run.passed < 0) {
   170	        problems.push(`${at}.passed must be a non-negative integer`);
   171	      }
   172	      if (run.failed !== 0) {
   173	        problems.push(`${at}.failed is ${String(run.failed)}: a qualification cannot be built on a failing suite`);
   174	      }
   175	      if (!Number.isInteger(run.passed) || (Number.isInteger(run.tests) && Number.isInteger(run.passed) && run.passed !== run.tests)) {
   176	        problems.push(`${at}: passed (${String(run.passed)}) does not equal tests (${String(run.tests)})`);
   177	      }
   178	      if (Number.isInteger(run.tests)) totalTests += run.tests;
   179	      if (Number.isInteger(run.passed)) totalPassed += run.passed;
   180	    }
   181	    if (totalTests > 0) notes.push(`observed: ${totalPassed}/${totalTests} tests passed in this run`);
   182	  }
   183	
   184	  // ── Components: all five clauses, each with a negative case and real evidence
   185	  const components = Array.isArray(record.components) ? record.components : null;
   186	  const seen = new Set();
   187	  const counts = { qualified: 0, partial: 0, unqualified: 0 };
   188	  if (!components) {
   189	    problems.push('components must be an array: Gate E is five clauses, not one verdict');
   190	  } else {
   191	    for (const [index, component] of components.entries()) {
   192	      const at = `components[${index}]`;
   193	      if (!component || typeof component !== 'object') {
   194	        problems.push(`${at} is not an object`);
   195	        continue;
   196	      }
   197	      const clause = component.clause;
   198	      if (!GATE_E_CLAUSES.includes(clause)) {
   199	        // A near-miss is the interesting failure: "denied action" vs
   200	        // "denied-action negatives" would silently drop a required clause.
   201	        problems.push(`${at} has an unknown Gate E clause: ${String(clause)}`);
   202	        continue;
   203	      }
   204	      if (seen.has(clause)) problems.push(`clause ${clause} is recorded more than once`);
   205	      seen.add(clause);
   206	
   207	      if (!COMPONENT_STATES.includes(component.observed)) {
   208	        problems.push(`${clause} has an invalid observed state: ${String(component.observed)}`);
   209	      } else {
   210	        counts[component.observed] += 1;
   211	      }
   212	
   213	      if (!nonEmpty(component.question)) {
   214	        problems.push(`${clause} has no question: a control must state what it is being asked to prove`);
   215	      }
   216	
   217	      // The negative case is the whole point of a security control. Without it
   218	      // the record asserts that something works, not that removing it would fail.
   219	      if (!nonEmpty(component.negativeCase)) {
   220	        problems.push(
   221	          `${clause} does not state its negative case: a positive assertion does not catch the regression the control exists to prevent`,
   222	        );
   223	      }
   224	
   225	      if (!Array.isArray(component.evidence) || component.evidence.length === 0) {
   226	        problems.push(`${clause} cites no evidence files`);
   227	      } else {
   228	        for (const file of component.evidence) {
   229	          if (!nonEmpty(file)) {
   230	            problems.push(`${clause} cites an empty evidence path`);
   231	          } else if (pathBase && !existsSync(resolveCited(file, baseDir, pathBase))) {
   232	            problems.push(`${clause} cites a path that does not exist: ${file}`);
   233	          } else if (!EVIDENCE_PATH_PATTERN.test(file)) {
   234	            // D9: the probe used package.json as every clause's evidence and was
   235	            // accepted. Evidence for a control must be code that can assert it —
   236	            // a test or the implementation under test.
   237	            problems.push(
   238	              `${clause} cites ${file}, which cannot assert a control: evidence must be a test or source file`,
   239	            );
   240	          }
   241	        }
   242	      }
   243	    }
   244	    for (const clause of GATE_E_CLAUSES) {
   245	      if (!seen.has(clause)) problems.push(`clause ${clause} has no entry: Gate E requires all five`);
   246	    }
   247	  }
   248	
   249	  // ── Declared gaps ───────────────────────────────────────────────
   250	  // Presence is required. An empty list is legitimate; an ABSENT list usually
   251	  // means gaps were dropped rather than none found.
   252	  if (!Array.isArray(record.declaredGaps)) {
   253	    problems.push(
   254	      'declaredGaps must be present (may be empty): a record that reports no gaps must say so explicitly, not by omission',
   255	    );
   256	  } else {
   257	    for (const [index, gap] of record.declaredGaps.entries()) {
   258	      if (!gap || typeof gap !== 'object') {
   259	        problems.push(`declaredGaps[${index}] is not an object`);
   260	        continue;
   261	      }
   262	      if (!nonEmpty(gap.id)) problems.push(`declaredGaps[${index}] has no id`);
   263	      if (!nonEmpty(gap.gap)) problems.push(`declaredGaps[${index}] has no gap description`);
   264	    }
   265	    if (record.declaredGaps.length > 0) {
   266	      notes.push(
   267	        `gaps preserved, NOT covered: ${record.declaredGaps.map(g => g.id).join(', ')}`,
   268	      );
   269	    }
   270	  }
   271	
   272	  // ── Independence ────────────────────────────────────────────────
   273	  const independence = record.independence;
   274	  let independenceClass = 'unknown';
   275	  if (!independence || typeof independence !== 'object' || Array.isArray(independence)) {
   276	    problems.push('independence is required: Gate E specifies "qualified independently" and the class must be stated');
   277	  } else {
   278	    if (!INDEPENDENCE_CLASSES.includes(independence.class)) {
   279	      problems.push(`independence.class must be one of ${INDEPENDENCE_CLASSES.join('|')}; got ${String(independence.class)}`);
   280	    } else {

    93	// ─── Owned-path auto-approval helpers ─────────────────────────────────
    94	
    95	/**
    96	 * True when the request declares an owned scope for a write tool — the case
    97	 * where the owned-path rule (step 5.5) is the authority for the write.
    98	 */
    99	function hasOwnedWriteScope(request: ToolPolicyRequest): boolean {
   100	  return Boolean(request.ownedPaths?.length) && SCOPABLE_WRITE_TOOLS.has(request.toolName);
   101	}
   102	
   103	/** Extract the mutation targets from a write-tool's args. */
   104	function mutationTargets(args: Record<string, unknown>): string[] {
   105	  const path = typeof args.path === "string" ? args.path : undefined;
   106	  if (path) return [path];
   107	  const format = typeof args.format === "string" ? args.format : undefined;
   108	  return extractPatchPaths(format, args.patchText);
   109	}

   111	// Owned-scope matching is `isWithinOwnedScope` (see the Local Contracts in
   112	// src/governance/policy/AGENTS.md). This gate runs BEFORE the file router, so a
   113	// normalization difference between them would silently deny every owned write
   114	// the router allowed — call the shared function directly, do not alias it.
