   116	// ─── Evasion patterns (single authority) ───────────────────────────────
   117	
   118	type EvasionPattern = {
   119	  pattern: RegExp;
   120	  severity: "deny" | "ask";
   121	  reason: string;
   122	};
   123	
   124	const EVASION_PATTERNS: EvasionPattern[] = [
   125	  { pattern: /\|.*base64.*-d\s*\|.*sh/si, severity: "deny", reason: "Base64 encoded command execution" },
   126	  { pattern: /xxd.*-r.*-p.*\|.*sh/si, severity: "deny", reason: "Hex encoded command execution" },
   127	  { pattern: /\$.*rm/si, severity: "ask", reason: "Variable expansion with rm - need approval" },
   128	  { pattern: /\/dev\/tcp\//, severity: "deny", reason: "Network socket /dev/tcp detected" },
   129	  { pattern: /nc\s+-[eEv]\s+.*\/(bash|sh|bin)/, severity: "deny", reason: "Netcat reverse shell detected" },
   130	  { pattern: /bash\s+-i\s*>&.*\/dev\/tcp\//, severity: "deny", reason: "Bash reverse shell detected" },
   131	  { pattern: /curl\s+.*\|.*(bash|sh)\s*$/smi, severity: "deny", reason: "Download and execute pipe detected" },
   132	  { pattern: /wget.*-O-.*\|.*(bash|sh)\s*$/smi, severity: "deny", reason: "Wget pipe execute detected" },
   133	  { pattern: /sudo\s+su\s+-/, severity: "ask", reason: "Privilege escalation attempt" },
   134	  { pattern: /passwd\s+root/, severity: "deny", reason: "Root password modification" },
   135	  { pattern: /chmod\s+777.*\/(etc|usr|var|bin)/, severity: "deny", reason: "Permission escalation on system directories" },
   136	  { pattern: /crontab\s+-r/, severity: "ask", reason: "Crontab manipulation detected" },
   137	  // Persistence mechanisms: the agent proposes schedules via schedule.propose
   138	  // (human-approved); writing OS persistence directly is always reviewed.
   139	  { pattern: /\bcrontab\b/, severity: "ask", reason: "Crontab access — use schedule.propose (approval-gated) instead" },
   140	  { pattern: /\bat\s+(?:\d|now)\b|\bbatch\s+-f\b/, severity: "ask", reason: "at(1)/batch job access detected" },
   141	  { pattern: /\bsystemd-run\b|\bloginctl\b|\bsystemctl\s+(?:enable|start)\b/, severity: "ask", reason: "systemd unit control detected" },
   142	  { pattern: /\/etc\/(?:cron|systemd|init\.d)|\/var\/spool\/cron|\.config\/systemd\/|\/\.ssh\/authorized_keys/, severity: "ask", reason: "Write to a persistence location detected" },
   143	  { pattern: /authorized_keys|ssh.*key.*>>/, severity: "ask", reason: "SSH key injection detected" },
   144	  // Merged from the retired PolicyEngine (#689) so no prior denial is lost
   145	  // now that PolicyGate is the single authority:
   146	  { pattern: /python.*-c.*import\s+socket/s, severity: "ask", reason: "Python socket creation - manual review recommended" },
   147	  { pattern: /php.*exec.*socket_create/s, severity: "ask", reason: "PHP socket creation - manual review recommended" },
   148	  { pattern: /\.bashrc|\.bash_profile.*rm/si, severity: "ask", reason: "Shell profile modification detected" },
   149	  { pattern: /export\s+PATH=.*:\/\$PATH/, severity: "ask", reason: "PATH manipulation detected" },
   150	  { pattern: /alias\s+rm=/, severity: "ask", reason: "Alias manipulation detected" },
   151	  { pattern: /nohup\s+.*rm\s/si, severity: "deny", reason: "Background execution of destructive command" },
   152	  { pattern: /disown\s+.*rm/si, severity: "deny", reason: "Disowned destructive command" },
   153	  { pattern: /setsid\s+.*rm/si, severity: "deny", reason: "Setsid background destructive command" },
   154	  { pattern: /\&\&.*rm\s+-rf/si, severity: "deny", reason: "Chained destructive rm command" },
   155	];
   156	
   157	function detectEvasion(command: string): { blocked: boolean; ask: boolean; reason?: string } {
   158	  for (const p of EVASION_PATTERNS) {
   159	    if (p.pattern.test(command)) {
   160	      return { blocked: p.severity === "deny", ask: p.severity === "ask", reason: p.reason };
   161	    }
   162	  }
   163	  return { blocked: false, ask: false };
   164	}
   165	
   166	// ─── Session mode application ────────────────────────────────────────
   167	
   168	function applySessionMode(toolDecision: string, mode: SessionMode): "allow" | "ask" | "deny" {
   169	  if (toolDecision === "allow") return "allow";
   170	  if (toolDecision === "deny") return "deny";
   171	  if (mode === "auto" || mode === "bypass") return "allow";
   172	  return "ask";
   173	}
   174	
   175	// ─── Protected path check ────────────────────────────────────────────
   176	
   177	/**
   178	 * Match `path` against protected-path patterns.
   179	 *
   180	 * Patterns are workspace-RELATIVE by convention (`.git/**`, `.env`,
   181	 * `secrets/**`), while the gate holds resolved absolute paths. Comparing the two
   182	 * directly never matched, so this rule silently never fired for the default
   183	 * configuration. Callers therefore pass both forms; matching either is enough.
   184	 */
   185	function isProtectedPath(patterns: string[], absolutePath: string, relativePath?: string): boolean {
   186	  const candidates = relativePath === undefined ? [absolutePath] : [absolutePath, relativePath];
   187	  return patterns.some((pattern) => {
   188	    if (pattern.endsWith("/**")) {
   189	      // The prefix must be the directory ITSELF or a descendant. A bare
   190	      // `startsWith` would match `.gitignore` and `.github/` against `.git/**`,
   191	      // which over-blocks unrelated files.
   192	      const prefix = pattern.slice(0, -3);
   193	      return candidates.some((p) => p === prefix || p.startsWith(`${prefix}/`));
   194	    }
   195	    if (pattern.endsWith(".*")) {
   196	      const base = pattern.slice(0, -2);
   197	      return candidates.some((p) => p === base || p.startsWith(pattern.slice(0, -1)));
   198	    }
   199	    return candidates.some((p) => p === pattern);
   200	  });
   201	}
   202	
   203	/** Workspace-relative form of an absolute path, or undefined when outside it. */
   204	function workspaceRelative(cwd: string, absolutePath: string): string | undefined {
   205	  const rel = relative(cwd, absolutePath);
   206	  return rel.startsWith("..") ? undefined : rel.split(sep).join("/");
   207	}
   208	
   209	// ─── PolicyGate ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   210	
   211	export class PolicyGate {
   212	  constructor(
   213	    private readonly config: AlixConfig,
   214	    private readonly deps: {
   215	      approvalStore?: ApprovalStore;
   216	      eventLog?: EventLog;
   217	    } = {},
   218	  ) {}
   219	
   220	  /**
   221	   * Evaluate a tool call against policy.
   222	   * Returns one decision that should be both logged and enforced.
   223	   */
   224	  async evaluateToolCall(request: ToolPolicyRequest): Promise<PolicyGateDecision> {
   225	    const policyRevision = computePolicyRevision(this.config);
   226	
   227	    const capability = request.capability ?? inferCapability(request.toolName);
   228	    const args = request.args;
   229	
   230	    // 1. Check protected paths
   231	    const rawPath = typeof args.path === "string" ? args.path : undefined;
   232	    if (rawPath) {
   233	      const resolvedPath = resolvePolicyPath(request.cwd, rawPath);
   234	      if (isProtectedPath(this.config.permissions.protectedPaths, resolvedPath, workspaceRelative(request.cwd, resolvedPath))) {
   235	        return {
   236	          requestId: request.requestId,
   237	          capability,
   238	          decision: "deny",
   239	          reason: `Path is protected: ${resolvedPath}`,
   240	          matchedRuleId: "protected-path-rule",
   241	          policyRevision,
   242	        };
   243	      }
   244	    }
   245	
   246	    // 1.5 Owned-scope channel check (Gate E defect D2).
   247	    //
   248	    // A declared scope is only meaningful if every mutation channel can be
   249	    // evaluated against it. A shell command, a dynamic MCP tool, or a delegate
   250	    // that spawns another agent cannot be — their targets are not in the args.
   251	    // Before this check a worker owning `inside.txt` was allowed
   252	    // `printf x > outside.txt`: the owned-path rule never ran (shell.run is not
   253	    // a scopable write tool) and the capability's blanket allow short-circuited.
   254	    //
   255	    // This sits with the hard denies rather than later, because a rule that can
   256	    // be reached only after a permissive branch is not a rule.
   257	    const unscopableReason = unscopableChannelDenial({
   258	      capability,
   259	      toolName: request.toolName,
   260	      ownedPaths: request.ownedPaths,
   261	    });
   262	    if (unscopableReason) {
   263	      return {
   264	        requestId: request.requestId,
   265	        capability,
   266	        decision: "deny",
   267	        reason: unscopableReason,
   268	        matchedRuleId: "unscopable-mutation-rule",
   269	        policyRevision,
   270	      };
   271	    }
   272	
   273	    // 2. Check deny commands
   274	    const command = typeof args.command === "string" ? args.command : undefined;
   275	    if (command && this.config.permissions.denyCommands.includes(command)) {
   276	      return {
   277	        requestId: request.requestId,
   278	        capability,
   279	        decision: "deny",
   280	        reason: `Command is denied: ${command}`,
   281	        matchedRuleId: "deny-command-rule",
   282	        policyRevision,
   283	      };
   284	    }
   285	
   286	    // Explicit tool denials precede every branch that can request approval,
   287	    // including the shell whitelist. Session modes never weaken a deny (D11).
   288	    if (this.config.permissions.tools?.[capability] === "deny") {
   289	      return {
   290	        requestId: request.requestId,
   291	        capability,
   292	        decision: "deny",
   293	        reason: `Denied by tool policy (mode: ${request.sessionMode})`,
   294	        matchedRuleId: `tool-policy-${capability}`,
   295	        policyRevision,
   296	      };
   297	    }
   298	
   299	    // 3. Check shell whitelist
   300	    if (command && this.config.permissions.shellWhitelist?.enabled) {
   301	      const whitelist = this.config.permissions.shellWhitelist;
   302	      const commands = whitelist.commands.length > 0
   303	        ? whitelist.commands
   304	        : parseWhitelistEnv(process.env.ALIX_SHELL_WHITELIST ?? "");
   305	      const baseCmd = command.split(/\s+/)[0];
   306	
   307	      if (BLOCKED_COMMANDS.includes(baseCmd)) {
   308	        return {
   309	          requestId: request.requestId,
   310	          capability,
   311	          decision: "deny",
   312	          reason: `Command '${baseCmd}' is blocked for security reasons`,
   313	          matchedRuleId: "blocked-command-rule",
   314	          policyRevision,
   315	        };
   316	      }
   317	
   318	      if (!commands.includes(baseCmd)) {
   319	        if (whitelist.allowUnmatched) {
   320	          return {
   321	            requestId: request.requestId,
   322	            capability,
   323	            decision: "ask",
   324	            reason: `Command '${baseCmd}' requires approval (not in whitelist)`,
   325	            matchedRuleId: "shell-whitelist-rule",
   326	            policyRevision,
   327	          };
   328	        }
   329	        return {
   330	          requestId: request.requestId,
   331	          capability,
   332	          decision: "deny",
   333	          reason: `Command '${baseCmd}' is not in the allowed whitelist`,
   334	          matchedRuleId: "shell-whitelist-rule",
   335	          policyRevision,
   336	        };
   337	      }
   338	    }
   339	
   340	    // 4. Evasion detection
   341	    if (command) {
   342	      const evasionResult = detectEvasion(command);
   343	      if (evasionResult.blocked || evasionResult.ask) {
   344	        return {
   345	          requestId: request.requestId,
   346	          capability,
   347	          decision: evasionResult.blocked ? "deny" : "ask",
   348	          reason: evasionResult.reason!,
   349	          matchedRuleId: "evasion-detection-rule",
   350	          policyRevision,
   351	        };
   352	      }
   353	    }
   354	
   355	    // 5. Tool permission from config
   356	    const toolDecision = this.config.permissions.tools?.[capability];
   357	    if (toolDecision) {
   358	      const effective = applySessionMode(toolDecision, request.sessionMode);
   359	      // A blanket allow must NOT widen past a declared owned scope: the
   360	      // owned-path rule (5.5) IS the authorization for an owned write, so an
   361	      // allowed capability falls through to it instead of short-circuiting.
   362	      // Returning allow here skipped the rule entirely — the write
   363	      // capability's permission resolves to "allow" under auto/bypass session
   364	      // modes, so a worker with ownedPaths could write anywhere in the
   365	      // workspace (observed on a real gpt-4o coordination run: a worker
   366	      // scoped to one file created two sibling files with no denial).
   367	      if (effective === "allow" && !hasOwnedWriteScope(request)) {
   368	        return { requestId: request.requestId, capability, decision: "allow", reason: `Allowed by tool policy (mode: ${request.sessionMode})`, matchedRuleId: `tool-policy-${capability}`, policyRevision };
   369	      }
   370	    }
   371	
   372	    // 5.5 Owned-path auto-approval (headless write subagents).
   373	    // The subagent's ownedPaths ARE the authorization: a write scoped entirely to
   374	    // owned paths is allowed; a write touching anything outside them is denied.
   375	    if (hasOwnedWriteScope(request)) {
   376	      const targets = mutationTargets(args);
   377	      if (targets.length === 0) {
   378	        // Unscoped (unparseable targets) — fall through to default/ask; headless
   379	        // subagents have no approval store so this fails closed.
   380	      } else {
   381	        const resolvedTargets = targets.map((t) => resolvePolicyPath(request.cwd, t));
   382	        // Protected paths are a hard deny even when owned (patch.apply has no
   383	        // args.path, so step 1 never sees its targets — check them here).
   384	        const protectedTarget = resolvedTargets.find((t) =>
   385	          isProtectedPath(this.config.permissions.protectedPaths, t, workspaceRelative(request.cwd, t)));
   386	        if (protectedTarget) {
   387	          return {
   388	            requestId: request.requestId, capability, decision: "deny",
   389	            reason: `Path protected: ${protectedTarget}`, matchedRuleId: "protected-path-rule", policyRevision,
   390	          };
   391	        }
   392	        if (resolvedTargets.every((t) => isWithinOwnedScope(t, request.ownedPaths!, request.cwd))) {
   393	          return {
   394	            requestId: request.requestId, capability, decision: "allow",
   395	            reason: "Write targets owned path", matchedRuleId: "owned-path-rule", policyRevision,
   396	          };
   397	        }
   398	        const outside = resolvedTargets.filter((t) => !isWithinOwnedScope(t, request.ownedPaths!, request.cwd));
   399	        return {
   400	          requestId: request.requestId, capability, decision: "deny",
   401	          reason: `Write target outside owned paths: ${outside.join(", ")}`, matchedRuleId: "owned-path-rule", policyRevision,
   402	        };
   403	      }
   404	    }
   405	
   406	    // 6. Default policy
   407	    const defaultDecision = applySessionMode(this.config.permissions.default ?? "ask", request.sessionMode);
   408	    if (defaultDecision === "allow") {
   409	      return { requestId: request.requestId, capability, decision: "allow", reason: `Allowed by default policy (mode: ${request.sessionMode})`, matchedRuleId: "default-policy", policyRevision };
   410	    }
   411	    if (defaultDecision === "deny") {
   412	      return { requestId: request.requestId, capability, decision: "deny", reason: "Denied by default policy", matchedRuleId: "default-policy", policyRevision };
   413	    }
   414	
   415	    // 7. Ask — approval lifecycle
   416	    // Embed the target (file path or command) in the reason so the operator
   417	    // can see WHAT they're approving in the TUI approval panel — otherwise
   418	    // every shell.run shows "shell.run" with no command context.
   419	    let askReason = `Requires approval for capability: ${capability}`;
   420	    if (capability === "shell.run" && typeof args.command === "string") {
   421	      askReason = `Requires approval to run command: ${args.command}`;
   422	    } else if (capability === "file.write" && typeof args.path === "string") {
   423	      askReason = `Requires approval to write file: ${args.path}`;
   424	    }
   425	    const askDecision = await this.handleAskDecision(
   426	      request.requestId,
   427	      capability,
   428	      request.sessionMode,
   429	      askReason,
   430	      request.sessionId,
   431	      request.agentId,
   432	      request.coordinationRunId ? {
   433	        coordinationRunId: request.coordinationRunId,
   434	        workerId: request.workerId,
   435	        workerAttempt: request.workerAttempt,
   436	        ownershipClaims: request.ownershipClaims,
   437	        requestFingerprint: request.requestFingerprint,
   438	      } : undefined,
   439	      // Exact invocation identity for the tool path. Persisted at creation and
   440	      // re-derived at authorization so authority cannot drift to a changed
   441	      // capability/tool/workspace/args/session/agent.
   442	      {
   443	        capability,
   444	        toolName: request.toolName,
   445	        workspace: resolve(request.cwd),
   446	        argsHash: (await import("../../capabilities/tools/hash-args.js")).hashArgs(args),
   447	        sessionId: request.sessionId,
   448	        agentId: request.agentId,
   449	      },
   450	    );
   451	
   452	    // Emit approval lifecycle events.
   453	    //
   454	    // DEDUPLICATION (F1-B): on a NEW approval the store emits `approval.created`
   455	    // from its committed creation transition, with a payload that is a superset
   456	    // of this one (approvalId, requestId, agentId, capabilities, bindingKey,
   457	    // policyRevision, reason, status, toolId). Emitting again here produced two
   458	    // creation events per logical request, which inflates approval-volume
   459	    // counters.
   460	    //
   461	    // ...but the store only emits when IT was constructed with an EventLog.
   462	    // `ApprovalStore.emit()` is a no-op otherwise, and a production caller does
   463	    // exactly that: headless `alix run` builds the store WITHOUT one
   464	    // (`run.ts`) while the executor's gate has one. Suppressing this site
   465	    // unconditionally therefore produced ZERO creation events on that path —
   466	    // the opposite failure, and a silent one. Exactly one emitter must fire:
   467	    // the store when it can, this gate when it cannot.
   468	    //
   469	    // The `toolName`/`cwd` fields this site adds are not lost on the store path:
   470	    // `approval-projection.ts` resolves a display tool name as
   471	    // `toolName ?? capabilities[0] ?? toolId`, and the store payload carries
   472	    // `capabilities` and `toolId`.
   473	    //
   474	    // On REUSE the store emits nothing (`requestOrReusePending` returns the
   475	    // existing record without an event), so `approval.reused` here remains the
   476	    // only record that a pending approval was observed and reused.
   477	    if (this.deps.eventLog && askDecision.approvalId && askDecision.decision === "ask") {
   478	      const isReused = askDecision.matchedRuleId === "pending-approval";
   479	      if (isReused) {
   480	        await this.deps.eventLog.append({
   481	          sessionId: request.sessionId ?? "unknown",
   482	          actor: "policy",
   483	          type: "approval.reused",
   484	          payload: {
   485	            approvalId: askDecision.approvalId,
   486	            requestId: request.requestId,
   487	            sessionId: request.sessionId,
   488	            agentId: request.agentId,
   489	            capability,
   490	            toolName: (request as ToolPolicyRequest).toolName,
   491	            status: "reused" as const,
   492	            reason: askDecision.reason,
   493	            cwd: (request as ToolPolicyRequest).cwd,
   494	            previousApprovalId: askDecision.approvalId,
   495	          },
   496	        }).catch(() => {});
   497	      } else if (this.storeEmitsCreationEvents() === false) {
   498	        // The store has no EventLog, so this is the ONLY creation record.
   499	        await this.deps.eventLog.append({
   500	          sessionId: request.sessionId ?? "unknown",
   501	          actor: "policy",
   502	          type: "approval.created",
   503	          payload: {
   504	            approvalId: askDecision.approvalId,
   505	            requestId: request.requestId,
   506	            sessionId: request.sessionId,
   507	            agentId: request.agentId,
   508	            capability,
   509	            toolName: (request as ToolPolicyRequest).toolName,
   510	            status: "pending" as const,
   511	            reason: askDecision.reason,
   512	            cwd: (request as ToolPolicyRequest).cwd,
   513	          },
   514	        }).catch(() => {});
   515	      }
   516	    }
   517	
   518	    return askDecision;
   519	  }
   520	
   521	  /**
   522	   * Whether the approval store supplies its own `approval.created` event.
   523	   *
   524	   * The store emits from its committed creation transition only when it was
   525	   * constructed with an EventLog (`ApprovalStore.emit()` is a no-op otherwise).
   526	   * This gate must therefore emit the creation record itself on exactly the
   527	   * paths where the store cannot, or the approval lifecycle disappears from the
   528	   * event stream — headless `alix run` is one such composition root.
   529	   *
   530	   * Fail toward "the store emits": a late/absent capability must never cause a
   531	   * second creation event, because duplicate records inflate approval-volume
   532	   * counters (F1-B). Only a store that positively reports it has no EventLog
   533	   * moves the emission here.
   534	   */
   535	  private storeEmitsCreationEvents(): boolean {
   536	    const store = this.deps.approvalStore as
   537	      | { emitsLifecycleEvents?: boolean }
   538	      | undefined;
   539	    return store?.emitsLifecycleEvents !== false;
   540	  }

   543	   * Evaluate a capability against policy (for graph node checks).
   544	   * Simpler than evaluateToolCall — no path/command/evasion checks.
   545	   */
   546	  async evaluateCapability(request: CapabilityPolicyRequest): Promise<PolicyGateDecision> {
   547	    const policyRevision = computePolicyRevision(this.config);
   548	
   549	    const toolDecision = this.config.permissions.tools?.[request.capability];
   550

 succeeded in 0ms:
     1	/**
     2	 * rule-evaluator.ts — Policy rule evaluator with deny-wins precedence.
     3	 *
     4	 * Separate from the PolicyGate (which is wired to config, capability registry,
     5	 * shell whitelist, etc). This is a pure, testable rule matching engine.
     6	 *
     7	 * PRECEDENCE: deny > ask > allow, over ALL matching rules.
     8	 *
     9	 * This was `first-match-wins`, which made a deny advisory: it held only when no
    10	 * permissive rule appeared before it in file order. The shipped defaults
    11	 * demonstrate the hole without anyone editing anything — `allow-file-read`
    12	 * (match: capability) is declared before `deny-critical-risk` (match: risk
    13	 * level), so a critical-risk file read matched the allow first and was
    14	 * permitted. Independent Gate E review defect D11.
    15	 *
    16	 * Two properties the ordering no longer has:
    17	 *   - file order cannot grant authority; only an absence of stricter matches can
    18	 *   - adding a deny rule anywhere in the file takes effect immediately
    19	 *
    20	 * The reported rule is the strictest match, so audit records name the rule that
    21	 * actually decided. When several rules share the strictest decision, the
    22	 * earliest one is reported: nothing about the DECISION then depends on order,
    23	 * but the audit line stays stable across runs.
    24	 */
    25	
    26	import type { PolicyRule, PolicyEvaluationInput, PolicyEvaluation, PolicyDecision } from "./policy-rule.js";
    27	import { matchPolicy } from "./policy-rule.js";
    28	
    29	/**
    30	 * Strictness ranking. Higher wins.
    31	 *
    32	 * Declared here rather than inline so the precedence order is stated once and a
    33	 * future decision value cannot be silently ranked as permissive by an
    34	 * exhaustive `if` chain.
    35	 */
    36	const DECISION_RANK: Record<PolicyDecision, number> = {
    37	  allow: 0,
    38	  ask: 1,
    39	  deny: 2,
    40	};
    41	
    42	export class RuleEvaluator {
    43	  private rules: PolicyRule[];
    44	
    45	  constructor(rules: PolicyRule[] = []) {
    46	    this.rules = rules;
    47	  }
    48	
    49	  addRule(rule: PolicyRule): void {
    50	    this.rules.push(rule);
    51	  }
    52	
    53	  setRules(rules: PolicyRule[]): void {
    54	    this.rules = [...rules];
    55	  }
    56	
    57	  getEnabledRules(): PolicyRule[] {
    58	    return this.rules.filter(r => r.enabled);
    59	  }
    60	
    61	  getAllRules(): PolicyRule[] {
    62	    return [...this.rules];
    63	  }
    64	
    65	  /**
    66	   * Evaluate an input against enabled rules. The STRICTEST matching decision
    67	   * wins (deny > ask > allow), regardless of order. Falls back to "deny" when
    68	   * no rule matches.
    69	   */
    70	  evaluate(input: PolicyEvaluationInput): PolicyEvaluation {
    71	    let winner: PolicyRule | undefined;
    72	
    73	    for (const rule of this.rules) {
    74	      if (!rule.enabled) continue;
    75	      if (!matchPolicy(rule.match, input)) continue;
    76	      // Strictly greater, so the earliest rule wins among equals and the audit
    77	      // line does not drift between runs.
    78	      if (!winner || DECISION_RANK[rule.decision] > DECISION_RANK[winner.decision]) {
    79	        winner = rule;
    80	      }
    81	    }
    82	
    83	    if (!winner) {
    84	      return { decision: "deny", reason: "No matching policy rule; denied by default" };
    85	    }
    86	
    87	    return {
    88	      decision: winner.decision,
    89	      matchedRuleId: winner.id,
    90	      matchedRuleDescription: winner.description,
    91	      reason: winner.reason,
    92	    };
    93	  }
    94	
    95	  /** Evaluate multiple inputs at once. */
    96	  evaluateBatch(inputs: PolicyEvaluationInput[]): PolicyEvaluation[] {
    97	    return inputs.map(i => this.evaluate(i));
    98	  }
    99	}
     1	/**
     2	 * owned-scope-channels.ts — which mutation channels a declared owned scope can
     3	 * actually constrain.
     4	 *
     5	 * WHY THIS EXISTS
     6	 *
     7	 * A worker declares `ownedPaths` and the policy gate enforces them. That
     8	 * enforcement compares a set of TARGET PATHS against the declared scope. It can
     9	 * only work for a channel whose targets are discoverable from the tool
    10	 * arguments: a path here, a patch header there.
    11	 *
    12	 * A channel whose targets are NOT discoverable — an arbitrary shell command, a
    13	 * dynamic MCP tool, a delegate that spawns another agent — cannot be checked
    14	 * against the scope. Before this module the gate treated those channels as
    15	 * simply "not a write tool", so a worker owning `inside.txt` could run
    16	 * `printf x > outside.txt` and be allowed (Gate E review defect D2).
    17	 *
    18	 * THE RULE, AND WHY IT IS AN ALLOWLIST
    19	 *
    20	 * The first attempt listed the FORBIDDEN channels by name. That is the wrong
    21	 * polarity: every new capability would be permitted until someone remembered to
    22	 * add it, and the review found channels the list missed (`skill.create`,
    23	 * `agent.delegate`, dynamic `mcp__*`, `hook.create`, `coordination.run`). A
    24	 * deny-list of unscopable channels cannot be complete; an allowlist of scopable
    25	 * ones can be, because it is the short list.
    26	 *
    27	 * So: with a declared scope, a MUTATING tool is permitted only when its targets
    28	 * can be extracted and compared. Everything else is denied. Read-only tools are
    29	 * unaffected — they cannot violate a write scope.
    30	 *
    31	 * MUTABILITY COMES FROM THE TOOL'S OWN REGISTRY ROW, not from a capability id.
    32	 * The first version of this module asked `isReadonlyCapability(inferCapability(t))`
    33	 * and got `shell.run` and `file.create` back as READ-ONLY: `inferCapability`
    34	 * returns a `policyKey` while `isReadonlyCapability` matches `capabilityId`, so
    35	 * the two axes never met and every lookup silently answered "read-only". Reading
    36	 * `ToolCapabilityRegistry.resolve(toolName).mutates` is the one-hop version of
    37	 * the same fact.
    38	 */
    39	
    40	import { createToolCapabilityRegistry } from "../../capabilities/tools/tool-registry.js";
    41	import { resolveCataloguedExecutor } from "../../capabilities/tools/capability-map.js";
    42	
    43	const catalog = createToolCapabilityRegistry();
    44	
    45	/**
    46	 * Tool names whose mutation targets the shared extractors can enumerate.
    47	 *
    48	 * This is the allowlist. Adding a tool here is a claim that its arguments fully
    49	 * describe what it writes; adding one without that property reintroduces D2.
    50	 */
    51	export const SCOPABLE_WRITE_TOOLS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
    52	  "file.create",
    53	  "file.delete",
    54	  "patch.apply",
    55	]);
    56	
    57	/**
    58	 * Deny channels a declared owned scope cannot constrain. Known read-only tools
    59	 * need no write authority; unknown tools fail closed because their mutability
    60	 * is unproven. Capability policy keys never establish executor identity.
    61	 * Returns null for scopable writes (callers must still compare actual targets).
    62	 */
    63	export function unscopableChannelDenial(
    64	  params: { toolName: string; capability?: string; ownedPaths?: readonly string[] },
    65	): string | null {
    66	  if (!params.ownedPaths?.length || SCOPABLE_WRITE_TOOLS.has(params.toolName)) return null;
    67	  const entry = resolveCataloguedExecutor(catalog, params.toolName);
    68	  if (entry && !entry.mutates) return null;
    69	  const name = params.capability || params.toolName || "unknown";
    70	  return (
    71	    `Capability '${name}' cannot be constrained to owned paths ` +
    72	    `(${params.ownedPaths.length} declared); denied for scoped workers`
    73	  );
    74	}

   425	  /**
   426	   * Build request-side ToolSpanInput at the seam; capture is the adapter's job.
   427	   * `args` and `startedAt` are the PRE-repair snapshot taken at call entry —
   428	   * dispatch may reassign `request.args` to the repaired object, so the span
   429	   * intentionally records the args as the model issued them (pre-repair).
   430	   */
   431	  private buildToolSpanInput(
   432	    request: ToolCallRequest,
   433	    args: Record<string, unknown>,
   434	    startedAt: number,
   435	  ): ToolSpanInput {
   436	    return {
   437	      toolName: request.name,
   438	      capability: inferCapability(request.name),
   439	      toolCallId: request.toolCallId,
   440	      invocationId: request.invocationId,
   441	      executionId: request.executionId,
   442	      args,
   443	      startedAt,
   444	    };
   445	  }
   446	
   447	  /** Terminal outcome for a resolved (non-thrown) tool result. */
   448	  private buildSpanOutcome(result: ExecuteResult): SpanOutcome {
   449	    if (result?.kind === "denied") {
   450	      // Denials map to "error" (design status vocab), no output captured.
   451	      return { status: "error" };
   452	    }
   453	    if (result?.kind !== "success") {
   454	      // kind === "error" — a tool failure is still a terminal "error" span.
   455	      return { status: "error", error: result.message };
   456	    }
   457	    let output: string | undefined;
   458	    if (typeof result.output === "string") {
   459	      output = result.output;
   460	    } else if (typeof result.content === "string") {
   461	      output = result.content;
   462	    } else if (typeof result.value === "string") {
   463	      output = result.value;
   464	    }
   465	    return { status: "success", output };
   466	  }
   467	
   468	  /** End a tool span exactly once; tracing failures never change tool results. */
   469	  private endToolSpan(client: TraceClient, span: TraceSpan, outcome: SpanOutcome): void {
   470	    try {
   471	      client.endSpan(span, outcome);
   472	    } catch {
   473	      // Tracing must never throw into tool execution.
   474	    }
   475	  }
   476	
   477	  private async dispatch(request: ToolCallRequest): Promise<ExecuteResult> {
   478	    const startedAt = Date.now();
   479	    const { toolCallId, name } = request;
   480	    const agentPayload = request.agentId ? { agentId: request.agentId } : {};
   481	    let args = request.args;
   482	    const capability = inferCapability(name);
   483	    const canonicalCapability = canonicalCapabilityOf(name);
   484	    // Routers need the same owned-path authority policy uses: a write worker
   485	    // rewriting its own declared output must be able to replace it.
   486	    if (!request.ownedPaths?.length && this.ownedPaths?.length) {
   487	      (request as { ownedPaths?: readonly string[] }).ownedPaths = this.ownedPaths;
   488	    }
   489	
   490	    // === TOOL REPAIR LAYER — runs before policy so hash and decision use repaired args ===
   491	    let repairHint: string | undefined;
   492	    if (this.repair && name !== "task.complete" && !name.startsWith("mcp.")) {
   493	      const repairResult = this.repair.process(name, args);
   494	      if (repairResult.repaired) {
   495	        repairHint = repairResult.hint;
   496	        args = repairResult.args;
   497	        (request as Record<string, unknown>).args = args;
   498	      }
   499	    }
   500	    // === END TOOL REPAIR ===
   501	
   502	    const argumentHash = hashArgs(args);
   503	    // Track the claim across execution so the crash-recovery state is honest:
   504	    // a claimed approval that never reports an outcome stays `pending` and a
   505	    // later replay classifies it `unverified` instead of reissuing authority.
   506	    let claimedApprovalId: string | undefined;
   507	    // T5 hierarchy: executionId → invocationId → toolCallId — typed via CorrelationContext, no loose Record
   508	    // For T5 parallel path, correlation is required (asserted in tool-correlation); for serial/back-compat allow fallback to empty.
   509	    const correlation: CorrelationContext = {
   510	      executionId: request.executionId ?? "",
   511	      invocationId: request.invocationId ?? "",
   512	    };
   513	
   514	    await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.REQUESTED, {
   515	      toolCallId,
   516	      toolName: name,
   517	      capability,
   518	      canonicalCapability,
   519	      argumentHash,
   520	      argsPreview: sanitizeArgs(args),
   521	      executionId: correlation.executionId,
   522	      invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   523	      ...agentPayload,
   524	      ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   525	    });
   526	
   527	    if (request.allowedMutationPaths?.length) {
   528	      const mutationPaths = extractMutationPaths(name, args);
   529	      const allowed = new Set(request.allowedMutationPaths.map((path) => resolve(this.root, path)));
   530	      const changedTarget = mutationPaths.find((path) => !allowed.has(resolve(this.root, path)));
   531	      if (changedTarget) {
   532	        const message = `Task constraint denied: ${changedTarget} is not the explicitly requested target`;
   533	        await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.FAILED, {
   534	          toolCallId,
   535	          toolName: name,
   536	          error: message,
   537	          durationMs: 0,
   538	          canonicalCapability,
   539	          argumentHash,
   540	          executionId: correlation.executionId,
   541	          invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   542	          ...agentPayload,
   543	          ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   544	        });
   545	        return { kind: "error", message, retryable: false };
   546	      }
   547	    }
   548	
   549	    // Continuation resumes bypass main policy gate — approval was already verified
   550	    // by ContinuationManager. R1.5: the executor independently re-validates the
   551	    // durable approval (present, still `approved`, not expired) — a caller-set
   552	    // `source` string is not authorization. Missing/invalid evidence fails closed.
   553	    if (request.source === "continuation-resume") {
   554	      const approval = request.approvalId && this.approvalStore
   555	        ? this.approvalStore.get?.(request.approvalId)
   556	        : undefined;
   557	      const stillAuthorized =
   558	        !!approval &&
   559	        approval.status === "approved" &&
   560	        approvalExpiryState(approval.expiresAt) === "valid";
   561	      if (!stillAuthorized) {
   562	        return {
   563	          kind: "denied",
   564	          reason: request.approvalId
   565	            ? `Continuation resume rejected: approval ${request.approvalId} missing, not approved, or expired`
   566	            : "Continuation resume rejected: no durable approval backing this request",
   567	        };
   568	      }
   569	      // Prior approval does not override CURRENT hard policy. Re-check only
   570	      // mandatory denies without creating a second approval. This must happen
   571	      // before ownership awaits, approval consumption, or adapter entry.
   572	      const continuationDeny = await this.mandatoryContinuationDeny(request, name, args);
   573	      if (continuationDeny) {
   574	        await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.FAILED, {
   575	          toolCallId, toolName: name, error: continuationDeny, durationMs: 0,
   576	          canonicalCapability, argumentHash, executionId: correlation.executionId,
   577	          invocationId: correlation.invocationId, ...agentPayload,
   578	        });
   579	        return { kind: "denied", reason: continuationDeny };
   580	      }
   581	      // Ownership BEFORE the approval claim: a continuation resume is still a
   582	      // write, and a write outside the declared scope is refused on its own
   583	      // terms rather than incidentally by an invocation-binding mismatch. The
   584	      // ordering also keeps this check reachable in tests — with the claim
   585	      // first, every continuation resume failed on invocation identity and the
   586	      // ownership call was never exercised (Gate E review, vacuous #10).
   587	      const contGateResult = await this.checkOwnershipGate(request, name, args);
   588	      if (contGateResult) return contGateResult;
   589	      // Ownership/loading may have yielded after the host's cancellation check.
   590	      // Do not consume authority for a resume already known to be cancelled.
   591	      if (request.signal?.aborted) {
   592	        throw new ExecutionCancelledError(signalReason(request.signal) ?? "continuation cancelled");
   593	      }
   594	      // R1.5: the continuation tombstone is NOT authorization — claim the
   595	      // backing approval atomically so two parallel resumes cannot both run.
   596	      if (request.approvalId) {
   597	        const claimed = await this.claimApproval(request.approvalId, {
   598	          ...this.invocationIdentity(capability, name, argumentHash, request.agentId),
   599	          });

   602	      }

   605	        toolName: name,
   606	        argumentHash,
   607	        executionId: correlation.executionId,
   608	        invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   609	        ...agentPayload,

   615	        // from dispatch: even a router that ignores AbortSignal must not start.
   616	        if (request.signal?.aborted) {
   617	          throw new ExecutionCancelledError(signalReason(request.signal) ?? "continuation cancelled");
   618	        }
   619	        resumed = await executeWithEffectJournal(this.root, request, (boundRequest) => this.toolAwareRouter.downstream.execute(boundRequest));
   620	      } catch (error) {
   621	        if (claimedApprovalId) {
   622	          // After downstream dispatch began, a thrown error cannot establish whether
   623	          // an external effect happened. Keep the consumed claim pending for
   624	          // fail-closed reconciliation; cancellation retains its own status.
   625	          if (isCancellationError(error)) {
   626	            await this.recordApprovalOutcome(claimedApprovalId, "cancelled");
   627	          }
   628	        }
   629	        throw error;
   630	      }
   631	      if (claimedApprovalId) {
   632	        // The ordinary path below already refuses to write a receipt for an
   633	        // unknown outcome; the continuation branch must not be the loophole.
   634	        // A resumed call whose adapter reported no provable terminal outcome
   635	        // (`outcomeUnknown`) has unknown success, so recording `failed` would
   636	        // be a fabricated verdict AND would permanently retire a
   637	        // single-use approval that may in fact have applied its effect.
   638	        // Leaving the claim `pending` keeps the fail-closed state: a replay
   639	        // classifies it `unverified` and denies, and it is never reissued.
   640	        const outcomeUnknown = resumed.kind === "error" && resumed.outcomeUnknown === true;
   641	        if (!outcomeUnknown) {
   642	          await this.recordApprovalOutcome(claimedApprovalId, resumed.kind === "success" ? "succeeded" : "failed");
   643	        }
   644	      }
   645	      return resumed;
   646	    }
   647	
   648	    // Safe shell bypass for ask mode: read-only commands skip the approval gate.
   649	    //
   650	    // "Skip the approval gate" must NOT mean "skip policy". Mandatory denies are
   651	    // still evaluated first: a deny is an absolute, and consulting it only after

   653	    // in `denyCommands` (or blocked/evaded) still executed here, because the
   654	    // bypass returned before authorization. Independent Gate E review defect D1.
   655	    //
   656	    // This deliberately does not create approvals — `evaluateToolCall` would, and
   657	    // an `ask` verdict here must fall through to the real authorization path so
   658	    // the approval lifecycle stays in one place.
   659	    const mode = this.config.permissions.sessionMode ?? "ask";
   660	    if (mode === "ask" && name === "shell.run") {
   661	      const command = typeof args?.command === "string" ? args.command : "";
   662	      if (command && isSafeShellCommand(command)) {
   663	        const mandatoryDeny = await this.mandatoryShellDeny(command);
   664	        if (mandatoryDeny) {

   666	            toolCallId,
   667	            toolName: name,
   668	            argumentHash,
   669	            executionId: correlation.executionId,
   670	            invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   671	            ...agentPayload,
   672	            ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   673	          });
   674	          return {
   675	            kind: "error",
   676	            message: `Command denied by policy: ${mandatoryDeny}`,
   677	            retryable: false,
   678	          };
   679	        }
   680	        // Skip the approval gate for a whitelisted read-only command, but do
   681	        // not execute it here: the downstream ShellToolRouter owns workspace
   682	        // path validation and command-failure classification.
   683	        await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.STARTED, {
   684	          toolCallId,
   685	          toolName: name,
   686	          argumentHash,
   687	          executionId: correlation.executionId,
   688	          invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   689	          ...agentPayload,
   690	          ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   691	        });
   692	        return await this.toolAwareRouter.downstream.execute(request);
   693	      }
   694	    }
   695	
   696	    // Unified authorization via ExecutionAuthorization — composes PolicyGate,
   697	    // OwnershipGate, and audit/event emission into a single decision.
   698	    const { ExecutionAuthorization } = await import("../../runtime-state/runtime/execution-authorization.js");
   699	    const policyGate = await this.policyGate();
   700	    const execAuth = new ExecutionAuthorization({
   701	      policyGate,
   702	      toolRegistry: this.toolRegistry,
   703	      ownershipGateConfig: this.ownershipRegistry && this.workspacePathResolver
   704	        ? { registry: this.ownershipRegistry, resolver: this.workspacePathResolver, autoAcquire: this.config.ownership?.autoAcquire ?? true }
   705	        : undefined,
   706	    });
   707	
   708	    const decision = await execAuth.evaluate({
   709	      requestId: toolCallId,
   710	      capability,
   711	      toolName: name,
   712	      args,
   713	      cwd: this.root,
   714	      sessionMode: this.config.permissions.sessionMode ?? "ask",
   715	      sessionId: this.sessionId(),
   716	      agentId: request.agentId ?? "alix",
   717	      source: "tool",
   718	      ownedPaths: this.ownedPaths,
   719	      coordination: this.coordinationContext,
   720	    });
   721	
   722	    // Denied — policy or ownership rejected this call
   723	    if (decision.status === "denied") {
   724	      await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.FAILED, {
   725	        toolCallId,
   726	        toolName: name,
   727	        error: decision.reason,
   728	        durationMs: 0,
   729	        canonicalCapability,
   730	        argumentHash,
   731	        executionId: correlation.executionId,
   732	        invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   733	        ...agentPayload,
   734	        ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   735	      });
   736	      return { kind: "denied", reason: decision.reason };
   737	    }
   738
