   740	    if (decision.status === "approval_required") {
   741	      try {
   742	        const { ContinuationStore } = await import("../../runtime-state/runtime/continuation-store.js");
   743	        const continuationStore = new ContinuationStore(this.root);
   744	        await continuationStore.load();
   745	        await continuationStore.persist({
   746	          approvalId: decision.approvalId,
   747	          kind: "tool",
   748	          sessionId: this.sessionId(),
   749	          cwd: this.root,
   750	          toolCall: {
   751	            toolCallId,
   752	            name,
   753	            capability,
   754	            args,
   755	            argsHash: argumentHash,
   756	            agentId: request.agentId,
   757	          },
   758	          createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
   759	        });
   760	      } catch (err) {
   761	        console.error("Failed to persist continuation:", err);
   762	      }
   763	
   764	      await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.FAILED, {
   765	        toolCallId,
   766	        toolName: name,
   767	        error: `Approval required: ${decision.approvalId}`,
   768	        durationMs: 0,
   769	        canonicalCapability,
   770	        argumentHash,
   771	        executionId: correlation.executionId,
   772	        invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   773	        ...agentPayload,
   774	        ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   775	      });
   776	      return {
   777	        kind: "denied",
   778	        reason: `Approval required (${decision.approvalId}): ${decision.reason}`,
   779	        approvalRequired: true,
   780	        approvalId: decision.approvalId,
   781	      };
   782	    }
   783	
   784	    // Handle special case: the completion tool (not in router)
   785	    if (name === "task.complete") {
   786	      await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.STARTED, {
   787	        toolCallId,
   788	        toolName: name,
   789	        argumentHash,
   790	        executionId: correlation.executionId,
   791	        invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   792	        ...agentPayload,
   793	        ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   794	      });
   795	      const result: ToolResult = { kind: "success", output: "Task complete.", completed: true };
   796	      const durationMs = Date.now() - startedAt;
   797	      await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.OUTPUT, {
   798	        toolCallId,
   799	        outputPreview: "Task complete.",
   800	        outputSize: 14,
   801	        executionId: correlation.executionId,
   802	        invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   803	        ...agentPayload,
   804	        ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   805	      });
   806	      await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.COMPLETED, {
   807	        toolCallId,
   808	        toolName: name,
   809	        status: "success",
   810	        durationMs,
   811	        canonicalCapability,
   812	        argumentHash,
   813	        executionId: correlation.executionId,
   814	        invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   815	        ...agentPayload,
   816	        ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   817	      });
   818	      return result;
   819	    }
   820	
   821	    // MCP availability check — policy said "ask" or "allow", but is the tool connected?
   822	    if (name.startsWith("mcp.") && !this.mcpManager) {
   823	      const msg = "MCP manager not initialized. No MCP servers are connected.";
   824	      await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.FAILED, {
   825	        toolCallId,
   826	        toolName: name,
   827	        error: msg,
   828	        durationMs: 0,
   829	        canonicalCapability,
   830	        argumentHash,
   831	        executionId: correlation.executionId,
   832	        invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   833	        ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   834	      });
   835	      return { kind: "denied", reason: msg };
   836	    }
   837	
   838	    // R1.5: an allowed decision that cites a durable approval must CLAIM it
   839	    // before any router runs. This is the single seam both execution routes
   840	    // pass through, so the claim happens exactly once per execution and a
   841	    // concurrent or fresh-process replay loses the race and cannot execute.
   842	    // The coordination exact-binding branch already consumed inside the gate
   843	    // (`approvalConsumed`), so claiming again here would deny a legitimate
   844	    // worker — skip it.
   845	    if (decision.status === "allowed" && decision.approvalId) {
   846	      if (!decision.approvalConsumed) {
   847	        const claimed = await this.claimApproval(decision.approvalId, {
   848	          ...this.invocationIdentity(capability, name, argumentHash, request.agentId),
   849	        });
   850	        if (claimed) return claimed;
   851	      }
   852	      // The exact-binding branch may have consumed this approval atomically
   853	      // inside PolicyGate. Consumption is still single-use; carrying the id
   854	      // forward is only for the terminal execution receipt below.
   855	      claimedApprovalId = decision.approvalId;
   856	    }
   857	
   858	    await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.STARTED, {
   859	      toolCallId,
   860	      toolName: name,
   861	      argumentHash,
   862	      executionId: correlation.executionId,
   863	      invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   864	      ...agentPayload,
   865	      ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   866	    });
   867	    // Emit observability metric for tool call (via fail-open logEvent: a
   868	    // contended append must not fail the tool).
   869	    await this.logEvent("observability.metric", {
   870	      name: "tool_calls_total", type: "counter", value: 1, labels: { tool: name }, timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   871	    });
   872	
   873	    // Verify argument hash match before execution (M0.9 permissive placeholder)
   874	    let result: ToolResult;
   875	    try {
   876	      result = await executeWithEffectJournal(this.root, request, (boundRequest) => this.router.execute(boundRequest));
   877	    } catch (error) {
   878	      if (isCancellationError(error)) {
   879	        // Cancellation is a terminal outcome, never a tool failure. Keep the
   880	        // original cancellation even if persistence of its telemetry fails.
   881	        try {
   882	          await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.COMPLETED, {
   883	            toolCallId,
   884	            toolName: name,
   885	            status: "cancelled",
   886	            durationMs: Date.now() - startedAt,
   887	            canonicalCapability,
   888	            argumentHash,
   889	            executionId: correlation.executionId,
   890	            invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   891	            ...agentPayload,
   892	            ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   893	          });
   894	        } catch {
   895	          // Telemetry cannot reclassify an operator cancellation as failure.
   896	        }
   897	        if (claimedApprovalId) await this.recordApprovalOutcome(claimedApprovalId, "cancelled");
   898	      }
   899	      // A thrown router error cannot prove the effect was not applied.
   900	      // Keep a consumed approval pending for reconciliation, not `failed`.
   901	      throw error;
   902	    }
   903	
   904	    // Append repair hint to success output. Routed through `toolResultText`
   905	    // rather than hand-picking `output`/`content`: those two are only two of
   906	    // the success payload shapes. A `grep.search` carries `matches[]` and a
   907	    // `file.exists` carries `exists`, so the old pair-of-branches form wrote
   908	    // NO hint for either — and this module is the exact defect
   909	    // `result-text.ts` exists to prevent, one layer up.
   910	    if (repairHint && result.kind === "success") {
   911	      const hintBlock = `\n\n[Tool Repair Hint] ${repairHint}`;
   912	      const rendered = toolResultText(result);
   913	      if (rendered.length > 0) {
   914	        result.output = `${rendered}${hintBlock}`;
   915	      } else if (result.output !== undefined) {
   916	        result.output = `${result.output}${hintBlock}`;
   917	      } else if (result.content !== undefined) {
   918	        result.content = `${result.content}${hintBlock}`;
   919	      } else if (result.value !== undefined) {
   920	        result.value = `${result.value}${hintBlock}`;
   921	      }
   922	    }
   923	
   924	    // Classify MCP errors with hints
   925	    if (name.startsWith("mcp.") && result.kind === "error" && result.outcomeUnknown !== true && result.retryable === undefined) {
   926	      result = classifyError(result);
   927	    }
   928	
   929	    const durationMs = Date.now() - startedAt;
   930	
   931	    // The single renderer for a result's text — search tools answer with
   932	    // `matches[]`, which a bare `output`/`content` read would count as zero.
   933	    const rawOutput = toolResultText(result);
   934	
   935	    // Handle large outputs by writing to file
   936	    const outputSize = rawOutput.length;
   937	    let outputRef: string | undefined;
   938	
   939	    if (result.kind === "success" && outputSize > LARGE_OUTPUT_THRESHOLD) {
   940	      outputRef = await writeOutputToFile(
   941	        // Must be the rendered text: a search result carries `matches[]`, and
   942	        // passing `output ?? content` (undefined) here crashed the run with
   943	        // `The "data" argument must be of type string ... Received undefined`
   944	        // the first time a large grep crossed the threshold.
   945	        rawOutput,
   946	        this.log.sessionDir,
   947	        toolCallId,
   948	        this.log,
   949	        {
   950	          coordinationRunId: request.coordinationRunId,
   951	          agentId: request.agentId,
   952	          taskId: request.taskId,
   953	        },
   954	      );
   955	    }
   956	
   957	    // Build an explicit preview (so the model always sees something)
   958	    if (result.kind === "success") {
   959	      // Normalize preview: explicit for empty/empty-array results so the model isn't left guessing.
   960	      const preview = rawOutput === "" ? "[no output]" : truncateOutput(rawOutput);
   961	
   962	      const outputPayload: ToolOutputPayload = {
   963	        toolCallId,
   964	        outputRef,
   965	        outputPreview: preview,
   966	        outputSize,
   967	        executionId: correlation.executionId,
   968	        invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
   969	        ...agentPayload,
   970	      };
   971	      await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.OUTPUT, {
   972	        ...outputPayload,
   973	        ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   974	      });
   975	
   976	      // ── Loop detection & escalation ─────────────────────────────────
   977	      // If the call returned no useful output repeatedly, emit a single escalation hint
   978	      // so the model/operator can try a different tool (e.g., list the directory).
   979	      const key = `${name}:${argumentHash}`;
   980	      if (preview === "[no output]") {
   981	        const count = (this.consecutiveEmptyOutputs.get(key) ?? 0) + 1;
   982	        this.consecutiveEmptyOutputs.set(key, count);
   983	        const ESCALATION_THRESHOLD = 3;
   984	        if (count === ESCALATION_THRESHOLD) {
   985	          // Emit a high-level agent hint / escalation event (non-fatal)
   986	          await this.logEvent("agent.escalation", {
   987	            message: `Repeated empty outputs for ${name} — consider running a listing or reading candidate files.`,
   988	            suggestionTool: "alix_shell_run",
   989	            suggestionArgs: { command: "ls -1 src/tools || echo '(no files)'" },
   990	            toolName: name,
   991	            argumentHash,
   992	            toolCallId,
   993	            ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
   994	          });
   995	        }
   996	      } else {
   997	        // Reset counter on non-empty output
   998	        this.consecutiveEmptyOutputs.delete(key);
   999	      }
  1000	    }
  1001	
  1002	    // Build and emit tool.completed or tool.failed event
  1003	    if (result.kind === "success") {
  1004	      const completedPayload: ToolCompletedPayload = {
  1005	        ...(typeof result.observedLineCount === "number" && Number.isSafeInteger(result.observedLineCount) && result.observedLineCount >= 0
  1006	          ? { observedLineCount: result.observedLineCount } : {}),
  1007	        toolCallId,
  1008	        toolName: name,
  1009	        status: "success",
  1010	        durationMs,
  1011	        canonicalCapability,
  1012	        argumentHash,
  1013	        executionId: correlation.executionId,
  1014	        invocationId: correlation.invocationId,
  1015	      };
  1016	      await this.logEvent(TOOL_EVENT_TYPES.COMPLETED, {
  1017	        ...completedPayload,
  1018	        ...agentPayload,
  1019	        ...(request.replayId ? { replayId: request.replayId } : {}),
  1020	      });
  1021	    } else {
  1022	      const failedPayload: ToolFailedPayload = {
  1023	        toolCallId,
  1024	        toolName: name,
  1025	        error: result.message,
  1026	        durationMs,
  1027	        canonicalCapability,
  1028	        argumentHash,
  1029	        executionId: correlation.executionId,
  1030	        invocationId: correlation.invocationId,

hook: PostToolUse
hook: PostToolUse
hook: PostToolUse Failed
hook: PostToolUse Completed
hook: PreToolUse
hook: PreToolUse
hook: PreToolUse Failed
hook: PreToolUse Completed
exec
/bin/bash -lc "nl -ba src/governance/policy/policy-gate.ts | sed -n '545,950p'" in /home/babasola/Projects/ALiX
 succeeded in 0ms:
   545	   */
   546	  async evaluateCapability(request: CapabilityPolicyRequest): Promise<PolicyGateDecision> {
   547	    const policyRevision = computePolicyRevision(this.config);
   548	
   549	    const toolDecision = this.config.permissions.tools?.[request.capability];
   550	
   551	    if (toolDecision) {
   552	      const effective = applySessionMode(toolDecision, request.sessionMode);
   553	      if (effective === "allow") {
   554	        return { requestId: request.requestId, capability: request.capability, decision: "allow", reason: `Allowed by tool policy (mode: ${request.sessionMode})`, matchedRuleId: `tool-policy-${request.capability}`, policyRevision };
   555	      }
   556	      if (effective === "deny") {
   557	        return { requestId: request.requestId, capability: request.capability, decision: "deny", reason: `Denied by tool policy (mode: ${request.sessionMode})`, matchedRuleId: `tool-policy-${request.capability}`, policyRevision };
   558	      }
   559	    }
   560	
   561	    const defaultDecision = applySessionMode(this.config.permissions.default ?? "ask", request.sessionMode);
   562	    if (defaultDecision === "allow") {
   563	      return { requestId: request.requestId, capability: request.capability, decision: "allow", reason: "Allowed by default policy", matchedRuleId: "default-policy", policyRevision };
   564	    }
   565	    if (defaultDecision === "deny") {
   566	      return { requestId: request.requestId, capability: request.capability, decision: "deny", reason: "Denied by default policy", matchedRuleId: "default-policy", policyRevision };
   567	    }
   568	
   569	    // Pending-approval reuse (#687): consecutive capability asks for the same
   570	    // capability must share one pending approval instead of duplicating it —
   571	    // the same reuse the tool path gets via RuntimeGate. Scoped to
   572	    // non-coordination asks only: coordination asks carry an exact binding key
   573	    // and reuse through handleAskDecision, where a capability-wide match
   574	    // would wrongly merge distinct bindings.
   575	    let capAskDecision: PolicyGateDecision;
   576	    const existingPending = !request.coordinationRunId
   577	      ? this.deps.approvalStore?.findPending({ capability: request.capability })
   578	      : undefined;
   579	    if (existingPending) {
   580	      capAskDecision = {
   581	        requestId: request.requestId,
   582	        capability: request.capability,
   583	        decision: "ask",
   584	        reason: `Pending approval: ${existingPending.id}`,
   585	        approvalId: existingPending.id,
   586	        matchedRuleId: "pending-approval",
   587	        policyRevision,
   588	      };
   589	    } else {
   590	      capAskDecision = await this.handleAskDecision(
   591	        request.requestId,
   592	        request.capability,
   593	        request.sessionMode,
   594	        `Requires approval for capability: ${request.capability}`,
   595	        request.sessionId,
   596	        request.agentId,
   597	        request.coordinationRunId ? {
   598	          coordinationRunId: request.coordinationRunId,
   599	          workerId: request.workerId,
   600	          workerAttempt: request.workerAttempt,
   601	          ownershipClaims: request.ownershipClaims,
   602	          requestFingerprint: request.requestFingerprint,
   603	        } : undefined,
   604	      );
   605	    }
   606	
   607	    // Emit approval lifecycle event.
   608	    //
   609	    // DEDUPLICATION (F1-B): the store emits `approval.created` from its
   610	    // committed creation transition (`createApprovalRecord`) when it was
   611	    // constructed with an EventLog, and that payload is a SUPERSET of what this
   612	    // site would emit — it carries approvalId, requestId, agentId, capabilities,
   613	    // bindingKey, policyRevision, reason and status. Emitting `created` again
   614	    // here produced two creation events for one logical request (26 events
   615	    // across 13 approvals in a real session), which inflates any consumer
   616	    // counting approval volume.
   617	    //
   618	    // The store's emission is conditional on its own EventLog, so this site
   619	    // supplies `created` exactly when the store cannot (see
   620	    // `storeEmitsCreationEvents`). Silence on both paths would erase the
   621	    // approval lifecycle from the stream.
   622	    //
   623	    // On reuse the store emits nothing — `requestOrReusePending` returns the
   624	    // existing record without an event — so `approval.reused` here is always
   625	    // the only record of that observation.
   626	    //
   627	    // Historical logs may still contain duplicate `created` events; consumers
   628	    // deduplicate on `approvalId`, and those records remain valid evidence.
   629	    if (this.deps.eventLog && capAskDecision.approvalId && capAskDecision.decision === "ask") {
   630	      const isReused = capAskDecision.matchedRuleId === "pending-approval";
   631	      if (isReused) {
   632	        await this.deps.eventLog.append({
   633	          sessionId: request.sessionId ?? "unknown",
   634	          actor: "policy",
   635	          type: "approval.reused",
   636	          payload: {
   637	            approvalId: capAskDecision.approvalId,
   638	            requestId: request.requestId,
   639	            sessionId: request.sessionId,
   640	            agentId: request.agentId,
   641	            capability: request.capability,
   642	            status: "reused" as const,
   643	            reason: capAskDecision.reason,
   644	            previousApprovalId: capAskDecision.approvalId,
   645	          },
   646	        }).catch(() => {});
   647	      } else if (this.storeEmitsCreationEvents() === false) {
   648	        await this.deps.eventLog.append({
   649	          sessionId: request.sessionId ?? "unknown",
   650	          actor: "policy",
   651	          type: "approval.created",
   652	          payload: {
   653	            approvalId: capAskDecision.approvalId,
   654	            requestId: request.requestId,
   655	            sessionId: request.sessionId,
   656	            agentId: request.agentId,
   657	            capability: request.capability,
   658	            status: "pending" as const,
   659	            reason: capAskDecision.reason,
   660	          },
   661	        }).catch(() => {});
   662	      }
   663	    }
   664	
   665	    return capAskDecision;
   666	  }
   667	
   668	  /** Handle the approval lifecycle for "ask" decisions. */
   669	  private async handleAskDecision(
   670	    requestId: string,
   671	    capability: string,
   672	    sessionMode: string,
   673	    reason: string,
   674	    sessionId?: string,
   675	    agentId?: string,
   676	    coordinationContext?: {
   677	      coordinationRunId?: string;
   678	      workerId?: string;
   679	      workerAttempt?: number;
   680	      ownershipClaims?: WorkerOwnershipClaim[];
   681	      requestFingerprint?: string;
   682	    },
   683	    invocation?: InvocationIdentity,
   684	  ): Promise<PolicyGateDecision> {
   685	    const store = this.deps.approvalStore;
   686	    const policyRevision = computePolicyRevision(this.config);
   687	
   688	    if (!store) {
   689	      // Headless contexts (delegate subagent child CLI) configure no
   690	      // approval store, so every ask would fail closed here — including
   691	      // read-only public-web capabilities the default rules explicitly
   692	      // allow (allow-web-search / allow-web-fetch). Keep those usable
   693	      // headless; everything else still fails closed.
   694	      // `task.complete` (alix_done) is a zero-side-effect status signal:
   695	      // denying it headless means a subagent can never finish early and
   696	      // always burns its full iteration budget.
   697	      if (capability === "web.search" || capability === "web.fetch" || capability === "task.complete") {
   698	        return { requestId, capability, decision: "allow", reason: "Auto-allowed: read-only/headless-safe capability with no approval store", matchedRuleId: "headless-read-allow", policyRevision };
   699	      }
   700	      return { requestId, capability, decision: "deny", reason: "Approval required but no approval store configured", matchedRuleId: "approval-store-missing", policyRevision };
   701	    }
   702	
   703	    // When coordination context is provided, use exact binding key
   704	    if (coordinationContext?.coordinationRunId) {
   705	      // Cross-process approval-visibility boundary (SRAP D2 remediation).
   706	      //
   707	      // This gate is a long-running authorization authority: the daemon
   708	      // constructs ONE ApprovalStore for its lifetime and this method is the
   709	      // only place the authorization path reads it. The operator resolves
   710	      // approvals from a SEPARATE `alix approvals approve` process, which
   711	      // writes the authoritative ledger (R2.5). Reading only the in-memory
   712	      // projection would never observe that decision without a daemon
   713	      // restart — a blocked worker stayed blocked forever (the D2 operational
   714	      // defect). Refresh from the authoritative store BEFORE any
   715	      // authorization read so the persisted decision is visible.
   716	      //
   717	      // This is NOT a second authority and NOT an independent cache: it reuses
   718	      // `ApprovalStore.load()`, which rebuilds in-memory state from the
   719	      // authoritative ledger. Consumption stays atomic and single-use —
   720	      // `consumeApproved` reloads and re-validates status/expiry/binding
   721	      // UNDER THE STORE LOCK, so a stale-then-fresh read introduces no
   722	      // time-of-check/time-of-use gap.
   723	      //
   724	      // Fail closed: a broken authoritative store denies rather than
   725	      // authorizing, re-blocking, or minting an approval against stale state.
   726	      try {
   727	        await store.load();
   728	      } catch (err) {
   729	        return {
   730	          requestId,
   731	          capability,
   732	          decision: "deny",
   733	          reason: `Approval store refresh failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`,
   734	          matchedRuleId: "approval-refresh-failed",
   735	          policyRevision,
   736	        };
   737	      }
   738	
   739	      const { computeBindingKey } = await import("../approvals/approval-binding.js");
   740	      const bindingKey = computeBindingKey({
   741	        coordinationRunId: coordinationContext.coordinationRunId,
   742	        workerId: coordinationContext.workerId,
   743	        workerAttempt: coordinationContext.workerAttempt,
   744	        capabilities: [capability],
   745	        ownershipClaims: coordinationContext.ownershipClaims,
   746	        requestFingerprint: coordinationContext.requestFingerprint ?? capability,
   747	        policyRevision,
   748	      });
   749	
   750	      // Check for existing approved binding
   751	      const approved = store.findExact(bindingKey);
   752	
   753	      // A CONSUMED binding is a spent authority, and spent means denied — not
   754	      // "ask again". Falling through to requestOrReusePending here created a
   755	      // fresh pending approval, which hands back the authority single use exists
   756	      // to remove (Gate E review defect D4). The record is already attributed to
   757	      // this exact invocation, so a new request for it is a replay.
   758	      if (approved?.status === "consumed") {
   759	        return {
   760	          requestId,
   761	          capability,
   762	          decision: "deny",
   763	          reason: `Approval ${approved.id} is already consumed; a spent binding cannot authorize another attempt`,
   764	          matchedRuleId: "consumed-binding-denied",
   765	          policyRevision,
   766	          bindingKey,
   767	        };
   768	      }
   769	
   770	      if (approved?.status === "approved" && approvalExpiryState(approved.expiresAt) === "invalid") {
   771	        return {
   772	          requestId, capability, decision: "deny",
   773	          reason: `Approval ${approved.id} has invalid expiry metadata; refusing corrupt authority`,
   774	          matchedRuleId: "invalid-approval-expiry", policyRevision, bindingKey,
   775	        };
   776	      }
   777	
   778	      if (approved?.status === "approved" && approvalExpiryState(approved.expiresAt) === "valid") {
   779	        // Try to consume it
   780	        const consumed = await store.consumeApproved(approved.id, bindingKey, {
   781	          workerId: coordinationContext.workerId,
   782	          workerAttempt: coordinationContext.workerAttempt,
   783	        }, invocation);
   784	        if (consumed.consumed) {
   785	          return { requestId, capability, decision: "allow", reason: "Approved by prior exact binding", approvalId: approved.id, matchedRuleId: "exact-binding-approved", policyRevision, approvalConsumed: true };
   786	        }
   787	        // The claim lost a race: the record was claimed between the read above
   788	        // and this attempt. Reporting `ask` would mint a replacement for an
   789	        // approval that may already be executing, so this is an unverifiable
   790	        // state and is denied. Silence is never success.
   791	        return {
   792	          requestId,
   793	          capability,
   794	          decision: "deny",
   795	          reason: `Approval ${approved.id} could not be claimed (already consumed or raced); refusing to re-issue authority`,
   796	          matchedRuleId: "binding-claim-lost",
   797	          policyRevision,
   798	          bindingKey,
   799	        };
   800	      }
   801	
   802	      // Check for existing pending
   803	      const pending = store.findPendingByBindingKey(bindingKey);
   804	      if (pending) {
   805	        return { requestId, capability, decision: "ask", reason: `Pending approval: ${pending.id}`, approvalId: pending.id, matchedRuleId: "pending-approval", policyRevision, bindingKey, requestFingerprint: coordinationContext.requestFingerprint ?? capability };
   806	      }
   807	
   808	      // Create the pending approval with the COMPLETE canonical coordination
   809	      // binding, committed atomically inside the store's lock. The previous
   810	      // implementation created the record through the legacy `store.request()`
   811	      // (its own legacy binding) and then patched the returned object AFTER the
   812	      // commit, so the authoritative ledger/projection and the in-memory
   813	      // binding index never carried the coordination binding — reconciliation
   814	      // could never match. requestOrReusePending commits the coordination
   815	      // binding and de-dups in the same locked mutate (no check-then-create
   816	      // race between the findPendingByBindingKey above and this create).
   817	      const approval = await store.requestOrReusePending({
   818	        reason,
   819	        bindingKey,
   820	        requestFingerprint: coordinationContext.requestFingerprint ?? capability,
   821	        policyRevision,
   822	        capabilities: [capability],
   823	        ownershipClaims: coordinationContext.ownershipClaims ?? [],
   824	        coordinationRunId: coordinationContext.coordinationRunId,
   825	        workerId: coordinationContext.workerId,
   826	        workerAttempt: coordinationContext.workerAttempt,
   827	        sessionId,
   828	        agentId,
   829	        requestId,
   830	        invocation,
   831	      });
   832	      return { requestId, capability, decision: "ask", reason: `Pending approval: ${approval.id}`, approvalId: approval.id, matchedRuleId: "created-approval", policyRevision, bindingKey: approval.bindingKey, requestFingerprint: approval.requestFingerprint };
   833	    }
   834	
   835	    // Fallback to legacy behavior for non-coordination requests
   836	    // In "ask" mode, always create a fresh approval — don't reuse prior approvals.
   837	    // Prior-approval reuse only applies in "auto" (auto-approve) mode.
   838	    if (sessionMode !== "auto") {
   839	      // De-dup: if the same tool call has already been resolved (approved
   840	      // OR denied), honour that resolution. The agent loop re-executes the
   841	      // tool after waitForApproval returns "approved", which would otherwise
   842	      // create a SECOND approval for the same call — and the LLM never sees
   843	      // the resolved result, just another "Approval required" denial.
   844	      const prior = requestId ? store.findByRequestId?.(requestId) : undefined;
   845	      if (prior) {
   846	        if (prior.status === "approved") {
   847	          // Single-use by exact invocation. When the caller supplies an
   848	          // invocation identity, a mismatch — including a legacy record with NO
   849	          // fingerprint — must NOT authorize. Fall through and ask again so a
   850	          // fresh, exactly-bound approval is created. The capability-level path
   851	          // (no tool invocation) keeps its prior reuse behavior.
   852	          const expiryState = approvalExpiryState(prior.expiresAt);
   853	          if (expiryState === "invalid") {
   854	            return { requestId, capability, decision: "deny", reason: `Approval ${prior.id} has invalid expiry metadata; refusing corrupt authority`, approvalId: prior.id, matchedRuleId: "invalid-approval-expiry", policyRevision };
   855	          }
   856	          const bindingOk = invocation ? invocationMatches(prior, invocation) : true;
   857	          if (expiryState === "valid" && bindingOk) {
   858	            return { requestId, capability, decision: "allow", reason: `Already approved: ${prior.id}`, approvalId: prior.id, matchedRuleId: "prior-approval-approved", policyRevision };
   859	          }
   860	          // Expired or invocation-mismatched authority is not reused; create a fresh approval.
   861	        } else if (prior.status === "denied") {
   862	          return { requestId, capability, decision: "deny", reason: `Already denied: ${prior.id}`, approvalId: prior.id, matchedRuleId: "prior-approval-denied", policyRevision };
   863	        } else if (prior.status === "consumed") {
   864	          // A spent single-use approval. Distinguish a proven outcome from a
   865	          // crashed claim: `pending` means the process holding the claim never
   866	          // reported back, so classify it `unverified` and deny with an exact
   867	          // reason. Never re-authorize.
   868	          let outcome = prior.executionOutcome;
   869	          if (outcome === "pending") {
   870	            try {
   871	              const verdict = await (store as { markExecutionUnverified?: (id: string) => Promise<string> })
   872	                .markExecutionUnverified?.(prior.id);
   873	              if (verdict === "unverified") outcome = "unverified";
   874	            } catch {
   875	              // Classification is observability; the denial below stands either way.
   876	            }
   877	          }
   878	          const detail = outcome === "unverified" || outcome === "pending"
   879	            ? "its execution outcome is UNVERIFIED (the process holding the claim did not report back); the side effect is unknown"
   880	            : outcome === "succeeded"
   881	              ? "it already executed successfully"
   882	              : outcome === "failed"
   883	                ? "its execution already failed"
   884	                : outcome === "cancelled"
   885	                  ? "its execution was cancelled"
   886	                  : "it was already consumed";
   887	          return {
   888	            requestId,
   889	            capability,
   890	            decision: "deny",
   891	            reason: `Approval ${prior.id} is single-use and already consumed — ${detail}. Request a fresh approval for a new attempt.`,
   892	            approvalId: prior.id,
   893	            matchedRuleId: "prior-approval-consumed",
   894	            policyRevision,
   895	          };
   896	        } else if (prior.status === "pending") {
   897	          return { requestId, capability, decision: "ask", reason: `Pending approval: ${prior.id}`, approvalId: prior.id, matchedRuleId: "pending-approval", policyRevision };
   898	        }
   899	      }
   900	      // Create new pending approval, persisting the exact invocation binding
   901	      const approval = await store.request({ reason, capability, sessionId, agentId, requestId, invocation });
   902	      return { requestId, capability, decision: "ask", reason: `Pending approval: ${approval.id}`, approvalId: approval.id, matchedRuleId: "created-approval", policyRevision };
   903	    }
   904	
   905	    // Auto mode: check existing resolved approval
   906	    const resolved = store.findResolved({ capability });
   907	    if (resolved) {
   908	      if (resolved.status === "approved") {
   909	        return { requestId, capability, decision: "allow", reason: `Approved by prior approval: ${resolved.id}`, approvalId: resolved.id, policyRevision };
   910	      }
   911	      return { requestId, capability, decision: "deny", reason: `Prior approval was denied: ${resolved.id}`, approvalId: resolved.id, policyRevision };
   912	    }
   913	
   914	    // Check existing pending approval — reuse
   915	    const existing = store.findPending({ capability });
   916	    if (existing) {
   917	      return { requestId, capability, decision: "ask", reason: `Pending approval: ${existing.id}`, approvalId: existing.id, matchedRuleId: "pending-approval", policyRevision };
   918	    }
   919	
   920	    // Create new pending approval
   921	    const approval = await store.request({ reason, capability, sessionId, agentId });
   922	    return { requestId, capability, decision: "ask", reason: `Pending approval: ${approval.id}`, approvalId: approval.id, matchedRuleId: "created-approval", policyRevision };
   923	  }

   947	      violations: [],
   948	      enforcementMode,
   949	      recentViolationCount: 0,
   950	    };

  1087	  ): Promise<boolean> {

  1118	    toolName: string,
  1119	    argsHash: string,

  1132	  private async claimApproval(
  1133	    approvalId: string,
  1134	    // `InvocationIdentity` already owns this shape. Restating it inline had
  1135	    // already drifted from the copy in policy-gate.ts; one type means one rule.
  1136	    identity: InvocationIdentity,
  1137	  ): Promise<ExecuteResult | null> {
  1138	    const store = this.approvalStore;
  1139	    if (!store?.consumeApproved) {
  1140	      // A durable approval was cited but the store cannot atomically claim it.
  1141	      // Executing anyway would break single-use, so fail closed.
  1142	      return {
  1143	        kind: "denied",
  1144	        reason: `No approval store able to claim ${approvalId}; refusing to execute a single-use authorization`,
  1145	      };
  1146	    }
  1147	    try {
  1148	      const record = store.get?.(approvalId);
  1149	      if (!record?.bindingKey) {
  1150	        return { kind: "denied", reason: `Approval ${approvalId} not found; cannot authorize this execution` };
  1151	      }
  1152	      const result = await store.consumeApproved(approvalId, record.bindingKey, {}, { ...identity });
  1153	      if (!result?.consumed) {
  1154	        return {
  1155	          kind: "denied",
  1156	          reason: `Approval ${approvalId} could not be claimed (${result?.reason ?? "unknown"}); a fresh approval is required`,
  1157	        };
  1158	      }
  1159	      return null;
  1160	    } catch (err) {
  1161	      return {
  1162	        kind: "denied",
  1163	        reason: `Approval claim failed for ${approvalId}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`,
  1164	      };
  1165	    }
  1166	  }

  1168	  /**
  1169	   * Report the post-claim execution outcome. Best-effort by contract: a
  1170	   * persistence failure must never reclassify the tool result the model sees.
  1171	   * The store only accepts the transition from `pending`, so a duplicated
  1172	   * report cannot rewrite an already-resolved claim.
  1173	   */
  1174	  private async recordApprovalOutcome(
  1175	    approvalId: string,
  1176	    outcome: "succeeded" | "failed" | "cancelled",
  1177	  ): Promise<void> {
  1178	    try {
  1179	      await this.approvalStore?.recordExecutionOutcome?.(approvalId, outcome);
  1180	    } catch {
  1181	      // Observable via the durable `pending` state; never fatal to the call.
  1182	    }
  1183	  }
  1184	
  1185	  // ─── Ownership Gate ───────────────────────────────────────────
  1186	  // Runs for every tool call including continuation-resume.
  1187	  // Only mutates=true tools require ownership checks.
  1188	
  1189	  private async checkOwnershipGate(
  1190	    request: ToolCallRequest,
  1191	    toolName: string,
  1192	    args: Record<string, unknown>,
  1193	  ): Promise<ToolResult | null> {
  1194	    // A declared owned scope is enforced HERE, not only in PolicyGate.
  1195	    //
  1196	    // The continuation-resume branch deliberately skips PolicyGate (approval was
  1197	    // already verified by ContinuationManager), so `ownedPaths` would go
  1198	    // unchecked on that path: the registry lease below runs with
  1199	    // `autoAcquire: true`, which GRANTS coverage rather than enforcing it. A
  1200	    // scoped worker resuming a continuation could therefore write outside its
  1201	    // declared scope.
  1202	    //
  1203	    // The CHANNEL rule comes from the shared module, not from a copy here: the
  1204	    // first version of this block handled only enumerable targets, so a shell or
  1205	    // delegate channel slipped through the same way it did in PolicyGate.
  1206	    const ownedPaths = request.ownedPaths?.length ? request.ownedPaths : this.ownedPaths;
  1207	    if (ownedPaths?.length) {
  1208	      const { unscopableChannelDenial } = await import("../../coordination/ownership/owned-scope-channels.js");
  1209	      const capabilityId = this.toolRegistry?.lookupByName(toolName)?.policyKey ?? toolName;
  1210	      const unscopable = unscopableChannelDenial({
  1211	        capability: capabilityId,
  1212	        toolName,
  1213	        ownedPaths,
  1214	      });
  1215	      if (unscopable) {
  1216	        return { kind: "error", message: unscopable, retryable: false };
  1217	      }
  1218	    }
  1219	    if (ownedPaths?.length && this.workspacePathResolver) {
  1220	      const { extractMutationTargets } = await import("../../coordination/ownership/mutation-targets.js");
  1221	      const extraction = extractMutationTargets(toolName, args, this.workspacePathResolver);
  1222	      if (extraction.classification === "unknown-write") {
  1223	        return {
  1224	          kind: "error",
  1225	          message:
  1226	            `Cannot determine mutation targets for ${toolName} — a declared owned scope cannot be verified. ` +
  1227	            `Acquire an explicit lease covering the expected paths and retry.`,
  1228	          retryable: false,
  1229	        };
  1230	      }
  1231	      if (extraction.classification === "known-write") {
  1232	        const { isWithinOwnedScope } = await import("../../coordination/ownership/path-scope.js");
  1233	        const outside = extraction.targets
  1234	          .map((target) => target.path)
  1235	          .filter((path) => !isWithinOwnedScope(path, ownedPaths, this.root));
  1236	        if (outside.length > 0) {
  1237	          return {
  1238	            kind: "error",
  1239	            message: `Ownership check failed: ${outside.join(", ")} outside owned paths`,
  1240	            retryable: false,
  1241	          };
  1242	        }
  1243	      }
  1244	    }
  1245	
  1246	    // Skip if ownership is not wired
  1247	    if (!this.ownershipRegistry) return null;
  1248	    if (!this.workspacePathResolver) return null;
  1249	
  1250	    const { checkOwnershipGate: gate } = await import("../../coordination/ownership/ownership-gate.js");
  1251	    const capability = this.toolRegistry?.lookupByName(toolName);
  1252	    const mutates = capability?.mutates ?? false;
  1253	
  1254	    return await gate(
  1255	      {
  1256	        registry: this.ownershipRegistry,
  1257	        resolver: this.workspacePathResolver,
  1258	        autoAcquire: this.config.ownership?.autoAcquire ?? true,
  1259	      },
  1260	      request.agentId ?? "root",
  1261	      toolName,
  1262	      args,
  1263	      mutates,
  1264	    );
  1265	  }
  1266	}

  1273	  // retryability only when the caller has not already decided it.

  1275	  const msg = result.message.toLowerCase();

     1	/**
     2	 * approval-store-lock.ts — Cross-process lock for ApprovalStore.
     3	 *
     4	 * The primary backend is OS-managed: an exclusive advisory `flock` on a lock
     5	 * file (via the util-linux `flock` binary's file-descriptor form). The lock
     6	 * lives in the kernel, so it is released automatically when the holding process
     7	 * exits for any reason — including SIGKILL. There is no lock state to recover,
     8	 * no PID to probe, no age to compare, and no reclaim race: a killed daemon
     9	 * never stalls later mutations, and a live holder is never stolen on age.
    10	 *
    11	 * A fallback backend (atomic `mkdir` + PID liveness) is used only where no
    12	 * `flock` binary is available (macOS/Windows CI). It is fail-closed: a
    13	 * provably DEAD pid is reclaimed immediately; a provably ALIVE pid (signal-0
    14	 * succeeds, or EPERM) is never reclaimed; and an unprovable owner
    15	 * (invalid/missing pid, missing/malformed metadata) is never reclaimed by age,
    16	 * because age cannot establish owner death. An unprovable orphan on those
    17	 * platforms therefore requires explicit operator recovery — a documented
    18	 * limitation of the fallback only, never a license to steal a live lock.
    19	 */

    38	/** Lock backends. `flock` is OS-managed (auto-released on process death). */
    39	export type LockBackendName = "flock" | "mkdir";
    40	
    41	interface ApprovalLockBackend {
    42	  acquire(timeoutMs: number): Promise<boolean>;
    43	  release(): void;
    44	  isHeld(): boolean;
    45	}

    47	function lockDir(cwd: string): string {

    49	}

    51	function lockPath(cwd: string): string {
    52	  return join(lockDir(cwd), "approvals.lock");

    55	function sleep(ms: number): Promise<void> {
    56	  return new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

    59	// ─── Backend selection ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    60	
    61	let detectedBackend: LockBackendName | undefined;
    62	
    63	/**
    64	 * Choose the lock backend for this platform: OS-managed `flock` where the
    65	 * util-linux binary is present (Linux/BSD), the fail-closed `mkdir` lock
    66	 * otherwise (macOS, Windows). Detected once and cached; a per-instance
    67	 * `backend` option overrides it for tests.
    68	 */
    69	export function detectLockBackend(): LockBackendName {
    70	  if (detectedBackend !== undefined) return detectedBackend;
    71	  if (process.platform === "win32") {
    72	    detectedBackend = "mkdir";
    73	    return detectedBackend;
    74	  }
    75	  const probe = spawnSync("flock", ["--version"], { stdio: "ignore" });
    76	  detectedBackend = probe.error || probe.status !== 0 ? "mkdir" : "flock";
    77	  return detectedBackend;
    78	}
    79	
    80	// ─── OS-managed flock backend ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    81	
    82	/** The child fd slot used to hand our open fd to the `flock` binary. */
    83	const FLOCK_FD = 9;
    84	
    85	/**
    86	 * Open the lock target for the flock backend. Normally a regular file, created
    87	 * if absent. A leftover DIRECTORY at the lock path (an orphan from the pre-flock
    88	 * `mkdir` lock) is opened read-only instead: `flock` can lock a directory, so
    89	 * new-process mutual exclusion still holds rather than throwing EISDIR.
    90	 */
    91	function openLockFd(path: string): number {
    92	  try {
    93	    return openSync(path, "a+");
    94	  } catch (error) {
    95	    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "EISDIR") {
    96	      return openSync(path, "r");
    97	    }
    98	    throw error;
    99	  }
   100	}
   101	
   102	class FlockApprovalStoreLock implements ApprovalLockBackend {
   103	  private readonly path: string;
   104	  private fd: number | undefined;
   105	  private acquired = false;
   106	
   107	  constructor(cwd: string, overridePath?: string) {
   108	    this.path = overridePath ?? lockPath(cwd);
   109	  }
   110	
   111	  async acquire(timeoutMs = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS): Promise<boolean> {
   112	    if (this.acquired) return true;
   113	    mkdirSync(dirname(this.path), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
   114	
   115	    // One fd is opened and reused across non-blocking attempts. On success the
   116	    // fd stays open and IS the lock: the kernel holds an exclusive `flock` on
   117	    // the open file description until this fd is closed, so SIGKILL of this
   118	    // process closes it and releases the lock with no cleanup step.
   119	    const fd = openLockFd(this.path);
   120	    const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
   121	    try {
   122	      while (Date.now() < deadline) {
   123	        const code = await this.tryFlock(fd);
   124	        if (code === 0) {
   125	          // A contender may have opened a stale inode after the pathname was
   126	          // replaced. Never report acquisition of an unlinked lock target.
   127	          // This detects replacement before the check; it cannot prevent a
   128	          // privileged/external actor from unlinking the path afterward.
   129	          const held = fstatSync(fd);
   130	          const current = statSync(this.path);
   131	          if (held.dev !== current.dev || held.ino !== current.ino) {
   132	            return false;
   133	          }
   134	          this.fd = fd;
   135	          this.acquired = true;
   136	          return true;
   137	        }
   138	        await sleep(POLL_INTERVAL_MS);
   139	      }
   140	      return false;
   141	    } finally {
   142	      if (!this.acquired) {
   143	        try { closeSync(fd); } catch { /* already closed */ }
   144	      }
   145	    }
   146	  }
   147	
   148	  /**
   149	   * Ask the `flock` binary to take a non-blocking exclusive lock on our open
   150	   * fd. The child's fd 9 is a dup of the same open file description, so when
   151	   * `flock` exits (immediately) the lock is held by OUR fd, not the child's.
   152	   * Returns 0 when acquired, a non-zero exit code when contended, or null when
   153	   * the binary could not run at all.
   154	   */
   155	  private tryFlock(fd: number): Promise<number | null> {
   156	    return new Promise((resolve) => {
   157	      let settled = false;
   158	      const done = (code: number | null) => {
   159	        if (settled) return;
   160	        settled = true;
   161	        resolve(code);
   162	      };
   163	      const stdio = Array(FLOCK_FD).fill("ignore").concat([fd]);
   164	      const child = spawn("flock", ["-n", "-x", String(FLOCK_FD)], { stdio });
   165	      child.on("error", () => done(null));
   166	      child.on("exit", (code) => done(code));
   167	    });
   168	  }
   169	
   170	  release(): void {
   171	    if (!this.acquired) return;
   172	    this.acquired = false;
   173	    const fd = this.fd;
   174	    this.fd = undefined;
   175	    if (fd !== undefined) {
   176	      try { closeSync(fd); } catch { /* already closed */ }
   177	    }
   178	  }
   179	
   180	  isHeld(): boolean {
   181	    return this.acquired;
   182	  }
   183	}
   184	
   185	// ─── mkdir fallback backend ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
   186	
   187	class MkdirApprovalStoreLock implements ApprovalLockBackend {
   188	  private readonly path: string;
   189	  private readonly token: string;
   190	  private acquired = false;
   191	
   192	  constructor(cwd: string, overridePath?: string) {
   193	    this.path = overridePath ?? lockPath(cwd);
   194	    this.token = randomUUID();
   195	  }
   196	
   197	  async acquire(timeoutMs = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS): Promise<boolean> {
   198	    if (this.acquired) return true;
   199	    const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
   200	    mkdirSync(dirname(this.path), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
   201	
   202	    while (Date.now() < deadline) {
   203	      try {
   204	        mkdirSync(this.path);
   205	        writeFileSync(
   206	          join(this.path, "meta.json"),
   207	          JSON.stringify({ pid: process.pid, token: this.token, acquiredAt: new Date().toISOString() } as ApprovalLockMetadata),
   208	          "utf-8",
   209	        );
   210	        this.acquired = true;
   211	        return true;
   212	      } catch {
   213	        if (this.reclaimStaleLock()) continue;
   214	      }
   215	      await sleep(POLL_INTERVAL_MS);
   216	    }
   217	    return false;
   218	  }
   219	
   220	  release(): void {
   221	    if (!this.acquired) return;
   222	    try {
   223	      if (existsSync(this.path)) {
   224	        const metaPath = join(this.path, "meta.json");
   225	        if (existsSync(metaPath)) {
   226	          const saved = JSON.parse(readFileSync(metaPath, "utf-8")) as ApprovalLockMetadata;
   227	          if (saved.token === this.token) {
   228	            rmSync(this.path, { recursive: true, force: true });
   229	          }
   230	        }
   231	      }
   232	    } catch { /* best-effort */ }
   233	    this.acquired = false;
   234	  }
   235	
   236	  isHeld(): boolean {
   237	    return this.acquired;
   238	  }
   239	
   240	  /**
   241	   * Ownership-safe atomic reclaim of a stale lock.
   242	   *
   243	   * The staleness decision (`lockIsStale`) and the removal are two steps, so a
   244	   * check-then-remove race would let two contenders both observe a dead owner
   245	   * and both remove + re-acquire, entering their critical sections together.
   246	   * The rename closes it: exactly one contender wins the POSIX rename (the
   247	   * loser gets ENOENT and simply retries its own acquire), and the winner then
   248	   * re-verifies the frozen copy before destroying it — or restores it if the
   249	   * re-check proves a live owner the original read had not seen.
   250	   */
   251	  private reclaimStaleLock(): boolean {
   252	    if (!lockIsStale(this.path)) return false;
   253	
   254	    const tombstone = `${this.path}.stale-${randomUUID()}`;
   255	    try {
   256	      renameSync(this.path, tombstone);
   257	    } catch {
   258	      // Lost the race (another host reclaimed or the owner released), or the
   259	      // lock vanished between the staleness check and the rename.
   260	      return false;
   261	    }
   262	
   263	    if (lockIsStale(tombstone)) {
   264	      rmSync(tombstone, { recursive: true, force: true });
   265	      return true; // reclaimed — caller retries acquire
   266	    }
   267	
   268	    // The frozen copy proves a live owner: restore it rather than steal it.
   269	    try { renameSync(tombstone, this.path); } catch { /* best-effort */ }
   270	    return false;
   271	  }
   272	}
   273	
   274	/**
   275	 * A lock is stale only when its owner can no longer be holding it:
   276	 *
   277	 *  - a valid, provably DEAD PID (signal-0 → ESRCH) is stale immediately — no
   278	 *    age gate, so a daemon SIGKILLed inside `mutate()` is recovered right away;
   279	 *  - a valid, provably ALIVE PID (signal-0 succeeds, or fails with EPERM for a
   280	 *    process we cannot signal but that exists) is NEVER stale on age alone;
   281	 *  - an owner that cannot be proven — invalid/missing PID, or missing/malformed
   282	 *    metadata — is never reclaimed automatically. Age cannot establish owner
   283	 *    death, and reclaiming by age would let a paused live writer lose its lock.
   284	 *    Such orphans require explicit operator recovery.
   285	 */
   286	function lockIsStale(lockPath: string): boolean {
   287	  const metaPath = join(lockPath, "meta.json");
   288	  if (!existsSync(metaPath)) {
   289	    // No owner identity exists to validate. Even an old directory may belong
   290	    // to a live process paused between mkdir and metadata creation. Fail
   291	    // closed; an orphan requires explicit operator recovery, never an
   292	    // unsafe automatic steal.
   293	    return false;
   294	  }
   295	
   296	  let meta: ApprovalLockMetadata;
   297	  try {
   298	    meta = JSON.parse(readFileSync(metaPath, "utf-8")) as ApprovalLockMetadata;
   299	  } catch {
   300	    // An interrupted metadata write cannot prove that the writer is dead.
   301	    // Reclaim by age would allow a paused live writer to lose its lock.
   302	    return false;
   303	  }
   304	
   305	  const pid = meta.pid;
   306	  if (Number.isFinite(pid) && pid > 0) {
   307	    return !pidIsAlive(pid);
   308	  }
   309	
   310	  // Invalid PID cannot establish owner death. Never steal on elapsed time.
   311	  return false;
   312	}
   313	
   314	/**
   315	 * `process.kill(pid, 0)` is a portable existence probe: it sends nothing.
   316	 * A permission error still proves the process exists (it belongs to another
   317	 * user), so only "no such process" counts as dead.
   318	 */
   319	function pidIsAlive(pid: number): boolean {
   320	  try {
   321	    process.kill(pid, 0);
   322	    return true;
   323	  } catch (error) {
   324	    return (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "EPERM";
   325	  }
   326	}

   345	    this.backend.release();
   346	  }

   350	  }

    36	const JOURNAL_COMPACT_THRESHOLD = 500;
    37	
    38	/** Trusted host context supplied by the restricted worker port, never request metadata.
    39	 * Omitted scope is the existing privileged host path; an explicit empty scope
    40	 * permits only legacy records without worker or attempt attribution.
    41	 */
    42	export type ApprovalOutcomeScope = Readonly<{ workerId?: string; workerAttempt?: number }>;
    43	
    44	/** Check every recorded binding; consumption can attribute an unbound request. */
    45	function outcomeScopeMatches(record: ApprovalRecord, scope: ApprovalOutcomeScope): boolean {
    46	  return (!record.workerId || record.workerId === scope.workerId)
    47	    && (!record.consumedByWorkerId || record.consumedByWorkerId === scope.workerId)
    48	    && (record.workerAttempt === undefined || record.workerAttempt === scope.workerAttempt)
    49	    && (record.consumedAttempt === undefined || record.consumedAttempt === scope.workerAttempt);
    50	}
    51	
    52	// Abort mutate() before pruning, ledger append, or projection writes on denial.
    53	const OUTCOME_SCOPE_DENIED = Symbol("approval outcome scope denied");
    54	
    55	export type ApprovalRequestInput = {
   180	    const isTerminal = (s: ApprovalRecord["status"]): boolean =>
   181	      s === "denied" || s === "consumed" || s === "expired" || s === "revoked" || s === "invalidated";
   182	    const terminal = this.approvals.filter((r) => isTerminal(r.status));
   183	    if (terminal.length <= this.maxTerminalRecords) return false;
   184	    // createdAt is ISO-8601, so lexicographic order is chronological.
   185	    terminal.sort((a, b) => a.createdAt.localeCompare(b.createdAt));
   186	    const drop = new Set(terminal.slice(0, terminal.length - this.maxTerminalRecords).map((r) => r.id));
   187	    this.approvals = this.approvals.filter((r) => !drop.has(r.id));
   188	    return true;
   189	  }
   190	
   191	  /**
   192	   * Load approvals — LEDGER first (R2.5 authority). In-memory state is
   193	   * rebuilt from the latest ledger fact per approval; the JSON projection
   194	   * (snapshot + journal) is consulted only for legacy records with zero
   195	   * ledger facts. Groups remain projection-only. Ledger db errors THROW —
   196	   * an authoritative store is never masked by a JSON fallback.
   197	   */
   198	  async load(): Promise<void> {
   199	    let latest: ReturnType<ReturnType<typeof getSharedLedger>["readLatestByEntityType"]>;
   200	    try {
   201	      const ledger = getSharedLedger(this.cwd);
   202	      latest = ledger.readLatestByEntityType("approval");
   203	    } catch (err) {
   204	      // Counted AND rethrown: a broken authoritative store must be visible.
   205	      this.ledgerCounters.failures += 1;
   206	      this.ledgerCounters.lastError = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
   207	      throw err;
   208	    }
   209	    const fromLedger = new Map<string, ApprovalRecord>();
   210	    const removedIds = new Set<string>();
   211	    for (const event of latest) {
   212	      if (event.eventType === "approval.removed") {
   213	        removedIds.add(event.entityId);
   214	        continue;
   215	      }
   216	      const payload = event.payload as { approval?: ApprovalRecord } | null;
   217	      if (!payload?.approval) {
   218	        throw new Error(`approval ledger event for ${event.entityId} missing approval payload`);
   219	      }
   220	      fromLedger.set(event.entityId, payload.approval);
   221	    }
   222	
   223	    // Projection view (snapshot + journal replay) for legacy facts + groups.
   224	    const projectionRecords: ApprovalRecord[] = [];
   225	    this.groups = [];
   226	    if (existsSync(this.filePath)) {
   227	      try {
   228	        const raw = await readFile(this.filePath, "utf-8");
   229	        const parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
   230	        if (Array.isArray(parsed)) {
   231	          for (const r of parsed as any[]) {
   232	            projectionRecords.push(normalizeApprovalRecord(r, { defaultPolicyRevision: "legacy", now: new Date() }));
   233	          }
   234	        } else {
   235	          const data = parsed as { approvals?: any[]; groups?: ApprovalGroup[] };
   236	          for (const r of data.approvals ?? []) {
   237	            projectionRecords.push(normalizeApprovalRecord(r, { defaultPolicyRevision: "legacy", now: new Date() }));
   238	          }
   239	          this.groups = data.groups ?? [];
   240	        }
   241	      } catch {
   242	        // corrupt snapshot — journal replay below may still contribute
   243	      }
   244	    }
   245	    for (const record of await this.readJournal()) {
   246	      const idx = projectionRecords.findIndex((a) => a.id === record.id);
   247	      if (idx >= 0) projectionRecords[idx] = record;
   248	      else projectionRecords.push(record);
   249	    }
   250	
   251	    // Merge: ledger wins over projection; tombstones suppress projection
   252	    // copies; zero-fact legacy records survive untouched.
   253	    const merged = new Map<string, ApprovalRecord>();
   254	    for (const r of projectionRecords) {
   255	      if (removedIds.has(r.id) || fromLedger.has(r.id)) continue;
   256	      merged.set(r.id, r);
   257	    }
   258	    for (const [id, r] of fromLedger) {
   259	      if (!removedIds.has(id)) merged.set(id, r);
   260	    }
   261	    this.approvals = [...merged.values()];
   262	    this.rebuildIndexes();
   263	  }
   264	
   265	  /** Read + normalize journal records (append-only delta since last compact). */
   295	  async save(): Promise<void> {
   296	    await this.saveAtomic();
   297	  }
   298	
   299	  /**
   300	   * Emit a lifecycle event to the EventLog — best-effort (Option-3 convention):
   301	   * the append happens after the durable mutation succeeds, so a failure must
   302	   * not change the store method's contract. Fire-and-forget, matching the
   303	   * repo's established `.catch(() => {})` pattern on hot paths.
   304	   */
   305	  private emit(type: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>, sessionId?: string): void {
   306	    const append = this.eventLog?.append({ sessionId: sessionId ?? "unknown", actor: "policy", type, payload });
   307	    if (append) {
   308	      append.catch(() => {});  // fire-and-forget (Option-3 convention)
   309	      this.pendingAppends.push(append);
   310	    }
   311	  }
   312	
   313	  /** Await all in-flight fire-and-forget appends so a subsequent read is
   314	   *  deterministic. Production callers never need this (the appends are
   315	   *  intentionally non-fatal); it exists so tests can assert the emitted
   316	   *  lifecycle events without racing the async append. */
   317	  async flushEvents(): Promise<void> {
   318	    const pending = this.pendingAppends.splice(0);
   319	    await Promise.all(pending);
   320	  }
   321	
   322	  /** Compact: write the full snapshot atomically, then clear the journal. */
   323	  private async saveAtomic(): Promise<void> {
   324	    const dir = join(this.filePath, "..");
   325	    if (!existsSync(dir)) {
   326	      await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
   327	    }
   328	    const token = randomUUID().slice(0, 8);
   329	    const tmpPath = `${this.filePath}.tmp.${token}`;
   330	    const state = { approvals: this.approvals, groups: this.groups ?? [] };
   331	    await writeFile(tmpPath, JSON.stringify(state, null, 2), { encoding: "utf-8", mode: 0o600, flag: "wx" });
   332	    await renameFile(tmpPath, this.filePath);
   333	    // Snapshot now includes every journal record — drop the delta.
   334	    await rm(this.journalPath, { force: true }).catch(() => {});
   335	  }
   336	
   337	  /**
   338	   * R2.5 append one approval fact — THE COMMIT (ledger is authoritative).
   339	   * Failure is counted, then THROWN: an unavailable authoritative store must
   340	   * never leave a JSON-only mutation behind.
   341	   */
   342	  private appendApprovalFact(record: ApprovalRecord, kind: "created" | "updated"): void {
   343	    const expected = currentEntityVersion(this.cwd, this.ledgerCounters, record.id);
   344	    appendFact(this.cwd, this.ledgerCounters, {
   345	      eventType: kind === "created" && expected === 0 ? "approval.created" : "approval.updated",
   346	      entityType: "approval",
   347	      entityId: record.id,
   348	      payload: { approval: record },
   349	      correlationId: record.id,
   350	      sessionId: record.sessionId,
   351	      agentId: record.agentId,
   352	      actor: { type: "system", id: "approval-store" },
   353	      occurredAt: new Date().toISOString(),
   354	      expectedVersion: expected,
   355	      errorLabel: "approval ledger",
   356	    });
   357	  }
   358	
   359	  /** R2.5 append a removal tombstone (prune or delete) — the commit. Throws on failure. */
   360	  private appendApprovalRemoved(id: string): void {
   361	    appendFact(this.cwd, this.ledgerCounters, {
   362	      eventType: "approval.removed",
   363	      entityType: "approval",
   364	      entityId: id,
   365	      payload: { removed: true },
   366	      correlationId: id,
   367	      actor: { type: "system", id: "approval-store" },
   368	      occurredAt: new Date().toISOString(),
   369	      errorLabel: "approval ledger",
   370	    });
   371	  }
   372	
   373	  /** Observable authority health (R2: failures must never be silent). */
   374	  ledgerStatus(): { appends: number; failures: number; projectionFailures: number; lastError?: string; lastProjectionError?: string } {
   375	    const c = this.ledgerCounters;
   376	    return {
   377	      appends: c.appends,
   378	      failures: c.failures,
   379	      projectionFailures: this.projectionFailures,
   380	      ...(c.lastError !== undefined ? { lastError: c.lastError } : {}),
   381	      ...(this.lastProjectionError !== undefined ? { lastProjectionError: this.lastProjectionError } : {}),
   382	    };
   383	  }
   384	
   385	  /**
   386	   * Acquire the per-file lock, load fresh, run a mutation, then persist.
   387	   * Pure additions append to the journal (no snapshot rewrite); updates,
   388	   * deletions, or retention pruning compact the snapshot (#703).
   389	   */
   390	  async mutate<T>(fn: (approvals: ApprovalRecord[]) => T | Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
   391	    return serializeStoreMutation(this.filePath, async () => {
   392	      const lock = new ApprovalStoreLock(this.cwd);
   393	      const acquired = await lock.acquire();
   394	      if (!acquired) throw new Error("Could not acquire approval lock");
   395	      try {
   396	        await this.load();
   397	        const before = new Map<string, string>();
   398	        for (const r of this.approvals) before.set(r.id, JSON.stringify(r));
   399	
   400	        const result = await fn(this.approvals);
   401	
   402	        // Classify the diff: additions vs updates/deletions.
   403	        const added: ApprovalRecord[] = [];
   404	        let mutatedExisting = false;
   405	        for (const r of this.approvals) {
   406	          const prior = before.get(r.id);
   407	          if (prior === undefined) added.push(r);
   408	          else if (prior !== JSON.stringify(r)) mutatedExisting = true;
   409	        }
   410	        const afterIds = new Set(this.approvals.map((r) => r.id));
   411	        for (const id of before.keys()) {
   412	          if (!afterIds.has(id)) { mutatedExisting = true; break; }
   413	        }
   414	
   415	        const pruned = this.pruneTerminal();
   416	        this.rebuildIndexes();
   417	
   418	        // R2.5 authority: the ledger append IS the commit — it runs BEFORE the
   419	        // projection and throws on failure (no JSON-only state can exist).
   420	        const finalIds = new Set(this.approvals.map((r) => r.id));
   421	        for (const r of this.approvals) {
   422	          const prior = before.get(r.id);
   423	          if (prior === undefined) this.appendApprovalFact(r, "created");
   424	          else if (prior !== JSON.stringify(r)) this.appendApprovalFact(r, "updated");
   425	        }
   426	        for (const id of before.keys()) {
   427	          if (!finalIds.has(id)) this.appendApprovalRemoved(id);
   428	        }
   429	
   430	        // Projection second: failure tolerated and counted — the ledger holds
   431	        // the truth and reconciliation reports projection drift for rebuild.
   432	        try {
   433	          if (!mutatedExisting && !pruned && added.length > 0 && existsSync(this.filePath)) {
   434	            // Append-only fast path: no unrelated history rewritten. (The first
   435	            // write compacts so `approvals.json` exists for external readers.)
   436	            await this.appendJournal(added);
   437	            const journalLines = await this.journalLineCount();
   438	            if (journalLines >= JOURNAL_COMPACT_THRESHOLD) {
   439	              await this.saveAtomic();
   440	            }
   441	          } else {
   442	            await this.saveAtomic();
   443	          }
   444	        } catch (err) {
   445	          this.projectionFailures += 1;
   446	          this.lastProjectionError = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
   447	        }
   448	
   449	        return result;
   450	      } finally {
   451	        lock.release();
   452	      }
   453	    });
   454	  }
   455	
   735	    evidence: RemoteDecisionEvidence,
   736	    decisionReason?: string,
   737	  ): Promise<ApprovalRecord | null> {
   738	    return this.resolveInternal(id, status, decisionReason, evidence);
   739	  }
   740	
   741	  private async resolveInternal(
   742	    id: string,
   743	    status: "approved" | "denied",
   744	    decisionReason: string | undefined,
   745	    evidence: RemoteDecisionEvidence | undefined,
   746	  ): Promise<ApprovalRecord | null> {
   747	    const resolved = await this.mutate((approvals) => {
   748	      const record = approvals.find(a => a.id === id);
   749	      if (!record || record.status !== "pending") { return record ?? null; }
   750	      record.status = status;
   751	      record.decidedAt = new Date().toISOString();
   752	      record.decisionReason = decisionReason;
   753	      if (evidence !== undefined) record.remoteDecisionEvidence = evidence;
   754	      return { ...record } as ApprovalRecord;
   755	    });
   756	
   757	    // Emit events after lock is released
   758	    if (resolved && resolved.status === status) {
   759	      this.emit(APPROVAL_EVENT_TYPES.RESOLVED, {
   760	        approvalId: id,
   761	        coordinationRunId: resolved.coordinationRunId,
   762	        workerId: resolved.workerId,
   763	        agentId: resolved.agentId,
   764	        capabilities: resolved.capabilities,
   765	        bindingKey: resolved.bindingKey,
   766	        policyRevision: resolved.policyRevision,
   767	        status,
   768	        reason: decisionReason,
   769	        timestamp: resolved.decidedAt,
   770	      }, resolved.sessionId);
   771	      this.auditStore?.append({
   772	        action: status === "approved" ? "approval.approved" : "approval.denied",
   773	        actor: "user",
   774	        details: { approvalId: id, reason: decisionReason },
   775	      }).catch(() => {});
   776	    }
   777	    return resolved;
   778	  }

   780	  /** List all approvals, newest first. IDs break timestamp ties, matching the
   781	   * precedence order `consumeApproved` and the binding index apply, so a caller
   782	   * that takes the first exact-binding match cannot select a different record
   783	   * than the store's own authority check. */
   784	  list(): ApprovalRecord[] {
   785	    // createdAt is ISO-8601: lexicographic order is chronological.
   786	    return [...this.approvals]
   787	      .sort((a, b) => b.createdAt.localeCompare(a.createdAt) || b.id.localeCompare(a.id));
   788	  }
   789	
   790	  /** List pending approvals only. */
   791	  listPending(): ApprovalRecord[] {
   792	    return this.list().filter(a => a.status === "pending");
   793	  }

   795	  /** Get a single approval by ID — O(1) via index (#703). */
   796	  get(id: string): ApprovalRecord | undefined {
   797	    return this.byId.get(id);
   798	  }
   799	
   800	  /**
   801	   * Find the most recent approval for a given requestId (typically the
   802	   * toolCallId). Returns the latest record regardless of status — callers
   803	   * inspect `.status` to decide how to proceed. This is the de-dup hook:
   804	   * when the agent loop re-executes the same tool call after approval,
   805	   * the policy gate uses this to recognise the prior resolution instead
   806	   * of creating a duplicate approval record.
   807	   */
   808	  findByRequestId(requestId: string): ApprovalRecord | undefined {
   809	    let latest: ApprovalRecord | undefined;
   810	    for (const a of this.approvals) {
   811	      if (a.requestId !== requestId) continue;
   812	      if (!latest || a.createdAt > latest.createdAt) latest = a;
   813	    }
   814	    return latest;
   815	  }
   816	
   817	  /** Find an approval record by exact binding key — O(1) via index (#703). */
   818	  findExact(bindingKey: string): ApprovalRecord | undefined {
   819	    return this.byBindingKey.get(bindingKey)?.[0];
   820	  }
   821	
   822	  /**
   823	   * Record what happened after a claim (`succeeded` | `failed` | `cancelled`).
   824	   *
   825	   * Best-effort by contract: the tool result must never be reclassified because
   826	   * outcome persistence failed, so callers ignore the boolean. Only the first
   827	   * terminal transition wins — a stale or duplicated report cannot rewrite a
   828	   * claim that another execution already resolved.
   829	   */
   830	  async recordExecutionOutcome(
   831	    id: string,
   832	    outcome: "succeeded" | "failed" | "cancelled",
   833	    scope?: ApprovalOutcomeScope,
   834	  ): Promise<boolean> {
   835	    const trustedScope = scope === undefined ? undefined : { ...scope };
   836	    let recorded = false;
   837	    let sessionId: string | undefined;
   838	    await this.mutate((approvals) => {
   839	      const r = approvals.find(a => a.id === id);
   840	      if (!r) return;
   841	      if (trustedScope && !outcomeScopeMatches(r, trustedScope)) throw OUTCOME_SCOPE_DENIED;
   842	      if (r.status !== "consumed") return;
   843	      if (r.executionOutcome !== "pending") return;
   844	      r.executionOutcome = outcome;
   845	      r.executionOutcomeAt = new Date().toISOString();
   846	      sessionId = r.sessionId;
   847	      recorded = true;
   848	    }).catch((error: unknown) => {
   849	      if (error !== OUTCOME_SCOPE_DENIED) throw error;
   850	    });
   851	    if (recorded) {
   852	      const type = outcome === "succeeded"
   853	        ? APPROVAL_EVENT_TYPES.EXECUTION_SUCCEEDED
   854	        : outcome === "cancelled"
   855	          ? APPROVAL_EVENT_TYPES.EXECUTION_CANCELLED
   856	          : APPROVAL_EVENT_TYPES.EXECUTION_FAILED;
   857	      this.emit(type, { approvalId: id, outcome }, sessionId);
   858	    }
   859	    return recorded;
   860	  }
   861	
   862	  /**
   863	   * Classify a `pending` claim as `unverified`: the process that held it is
   864	   * gone, so the side effect is unknown. Terminal and fail-closed — the
   865	   * approval is never reissued by this transition.
   866	   *
   867	   * Returns the record's current state so a caller can name the exact reason.
   868	   */
   869	  async markExecutionUnverified(
   870	    id: string,
   871	    scope?: ApprovalOutcomeScope,
   872	  ): Promise<"unverified" | "terminal" | "missing"> {
   873	    const trustedScope = scope === undefined ? undefined : { ...scope };
   874	    let verdict: "unverified" | "terminal" | "missing" = "missing";
   875	    let sessionId: string | undefined;
   876	    await this.mutate((approvals) => {
   877	      const r = approvals.find(a => a.id === id);
   878	      if (!r) { verdict = "missing"; return; }
   879	      if (trustedScope && !outcomeScopeMatches(r, trustedScope)) throw OUTCOME_SCOPE_DENIED;
   880	      if (r.status !== "consumed") { verdict = "terminal"; return; }
   881	      if (r.executionOutcome === "unverified") { verdict = "unverified"; return; }
   882	      if (r.executionOutcome !== "pending") { verdict = "terminal"; return; }
   883	      r.executionOutcome = "unverified";
   884	      r.executionOutcomeAt = new Date().toISOString();
   885	      sessionId = r.sessionId;
   886	      verdict = "unverified";
   887	    }).catch((error: unknown) => {
   888	      if (error !== OUTCOME_SCOPE_DENIED) throw error;
   889	    });
   890	    // `verdict` is assigned inside the mutate() closure, so TS narrows it to the
   891	    // initial literal here. Re-assert the declared union before comparing.
   892	    const finalVerdict = verdict as "unverified" | "terminal" | "missing";
   893	    if (finalVerdict === "unverified") {
   894	      this.emit(APPROVAL_EVENT_TYPES.EXECUTION_UNVERIFIED, { approvalId: id }, sessionId);
   895	    }
   896	    return finalVerdict;
   897	  }
   898	
   899	  /**
   900	   * Consumed approvals whose execution outcome is not a proven terminal result.
   901	   *
   902	   * `unverified` means a replay already observed a dead claim. `pending` may
   903	   * still be in flight, or may be a crash that nothing has replayed yet — both
   904	   * are reported so an operator can inspect them without a wall-clock sweep.
   905	   */
   906	  listUncertainConsumptions(): ApprovalRecord[] {
   907	    return this.list().filter(
   908	      a => a.status === "consumed"
   909	        && (a.executionOutcome === "pending" || a.executionOutcome === "unverified"),
   910	    );
   911	  }

   913	  /** Find a pending approval by binding key — O(1) bucket lookup (#703). */
   914	  findPendingByBindingKey(bindingKey: string): ApprovalRecord | undefined {
   915	    const latest = this.byBindingKey.get(bindingKey)?.[0];
   916	    return latest?.status === "pending" ? latest : undefined;
   917	  }

   919	  /**
   920	   * Force a fresh load from disk and return an approval by ID.
   921	   * Unlike get() which may return stale in-memory state, this
   922	   * reloads the store first to guarantee fresh data.
   923	   */
   924	  async loadFresh(approvalId: string): Promise<ApprovalRecord | undefined> {
   925	    await this.load();
   926	    return this.byId.get(approvalId);
   927	  }

   929	  /** Recovery authority: no legacy JSON/journal fallback and no cached view. */
   930	  loadCommitted(approvalId: string): ApprovalRecord | undefined {
   931	    const event = getSharedLedger(this.cwd).readLatestByEntityType("approval")
   932	      .find(fact => fact.entityId === approvalId);
   933	    if (!event || event.eventType === "approval.removed") return undefined;
   934	    const payload = event.payload as { approval?: ApprovalRecord } | null;
   935	    if (!payload?.approval || payload.approval.id !== approvalId) {
   936	      throw new Error(`approval ledger event for ${approvalId} missing matching approval payload`);
   937	    }
   938	    return payload.approval;
   939	  }

   943	   * Reloads from disk to ensure the in-memory state is current.
   944	   */
   945	  async findExactFresh(bindingKey: string): Promise<ApprovalRecord | undefined> {
   946	    await this.load();
   947	    return this.byBindingKey.get(bindingKey)?.[0];
   948	  }
