   950	  /**
  1020	   */
  1021	  async consumeApproved(
  1022	    id: string,
  1023	    expectedBindingKey: string,
  1024	    consumer: { workerId?: string; workerAttempt?: number; now?: Date; requireWorkerBinding?: boolean },
  1025	    expectedInvocation?: InvocationIdentity,
  1026	  ): Promise<ConsumeResult> {
  1027	    let result: ConsumeResult = { consumed: false, reason: "not found" };
  1028	    await this.mutate((approvals) => {
  1029	      const r = approvals.find(a => a.id === id);
  1030	      if (!r) { result = { consumed: false, reason: "not found" }; return; }
  1031	      if (r.status !== "approved") { result = { consumed: false, reason: `status is ${r.status}` }; return; }
  1032	      const now = consumer.now ?? new Date();
  1033	      const expiryState = approvalExpiryState(r.expiresAt, now);
  1034	      if (expiryState === "invalid") { result = { consumed: false, reason: "invalid expiry" }; return; }
  1035	      if (expiryState === "expired") { result = { consumed: false, reason: "expired" }; return; }
  1036	      if (r.bindingKey !== expectedBindingKey) { result = { consumed: false, reason: "binding key mismatch" }; return; }
  1037	      // Re-check precedence against the locked ledger, not the caller's earlier
  1038	      // selection. IDs cannot establish authority between simultaneous decisions.
  1039	      const createdAt = Date.parse(r.createdAt);
  1040	      const competingTimes = approvals.filter(a => a.id !== r.id && a.bindingKey === expectedBindingKey &&
  1041	        a.invocationFingerprint === r.invocationFingerprint && a.workerId === r.workerId &&
  1042	        a.workerAttempt === r.workerAttempt && a.coordinationRunId === r.coordinationRunId)
  1043	        .map(a => Date.parse(a.createdAt));
  1044	      if (!Number.isFinite(createdAt) || competingTimes.some(time => !Number.isFinite(time))) {
  1045	        result = { consumed: false, reason: "invalid approval decision timestamp" }; return;
  1046	      }
  1047	      if (competingTimes.some(time => time === createdAt)) {
  1048	        result = { consumed: false, reason: "ambiguous approval decision timestamp" }; return;
  1049	      }
  1050	      if (competingTimes.some(time => time > createdAt)) {
  1051	        result = { consumed: false, reason: "superseded by a newer exact decision" }; return;
  1052	      }
  1053	      // Restricted worker ports must not claim legacy/unbound records. Check
  1054	      // against the freshly reloaded record while holding the store lock.
  1055	      if (consumer.requireWorkerBinding && (!r.workerId || r.workerId !== consumer.workerId ||
  1056	          (consumer.workerAttempt !== undefined && r.workerAttempt !== consumer.workerAttempt))) {
  1057	        result = { consumed: false, reason: "worker scope mismatch" }; return;
  1058	      }
  1059	      // Worker-bound authority requires explicit, matching execution identity.
  1060	      // A binding key alone must never authorize a different worker or attempt.
  1061	      if (r.workerId && r.workerId !== consumer.workerId) {
  1062	        result = { consumed: false, reason: "worker mismatch" }; return;
  1063	      }
  1064	      if (r.workerAttempt !== undefined && r.workerAttempt !== consumer.workerAttempt) {
  1065	        result = { consumed: false, reason: "worker attempt mismatch" }; return;
  1066	      }
  1067	      // Invocation-bound records require a current invocation even if the
  1068	      // caller omits it. Explicit legacy unbound records remain single-use.
  1069	      if ((r.invocationFingerprint || expectedInvocation) &&
  1070	          (!expectedInvocation || !invocationMatches(r, expectedInvocation))) {
  1071	        result = { consumed: false, reason: "invocation mismatch" }; return;
  1072	      }
  1073	      r.status = "consumed";
  1074	      r.consumedAt = (consumer.now ?? new Date()).toISOString();
  1075	      r.consumedByWorkerId = consumer.workerId;
  1076	      r.consumedAttempt = consumer.workerAttempt;
  1077	      // The claim is durable; execution follows and reports its own outcome.
  1078	      // A crash in between leaves this `pending`, which a later replay
  1079	      // classifies as `unverified` rather than silently reissuing authority.
  1080	      r.executionOutcome = "pending";
  1081	      r.executionOutcomeAt = r.consumedAt;
  1082	      result = { consumed: true, record: { ...r } };
  1083	    });
  1084	    // `result` is assigned inside the mutate() closure, so TS narrows it to the
  1085	    // initial `{ consumed: false }` variant here. Re-assert the declared type.
  1086	    const consumeOutcome = result as ConsumeResult;
  1087	    if (consumeOutcome.consumed && consumeOutcome.record) {
  1088	      this.emit(APPROVAL_EVENT_TYPES.CONSUMED, { approvalId: consumeOutcome.record.id }, consumeOutcome.record.sessionId);
  1089	    }
  1090	    return result;
  1091	  }

   334	  /**
   335	   * Execute a tool call, emitting exactly one terminal tool span per PHYSICAL
   336	   * tool call when tracing is enabled and the request carries a runId that
   337	   * resolves to an active run (R2, design §21, §22 exactly-once).
   338	   *
   339	   * The span is not begun until after dispatch confirms the tool actually ran:
   340	   * `dispatch` can return an early, non-executing `denied` — most importantly
   341	   * the approval-gated first attempt (`reason` starts with "Approval required")
   342	   * that `handleToolCall` re-executes for real. Starting a span for that pause
   343	   * would burn a spurious second terminal span (branded `error`) on a normal
   344	   * approval wait. So we resolve the run up front (needed to end a span on the
   345	   * throw path too), snapshot the pre-repair args + entry time, and only start
   346	   * + end the span once dispatch has actually executed. Exactly one terminal
   347	   * span across success / error-result / throw / timeout / cancellation; zero
   348	   * span work when tracing is disabled, runId absent, or run unknown.
   349	   */

     1	/**
     2	 * policy-loader.ts — Load PolicyRules from disk or fall back to defaults.
     3	 *
     4	 * Reads .alix/policies/*.json and validates each rule.
     5	 * Falls back to built-in defaults when no policy files exist.
     6	 */
     7	
     8	import { readdir, readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
     9	import { join } from "node:path";
    10	import { existsSync } from "node:fs";
    11	import type { PolicyRule } from "./policy-rule.js";
    12	import { validatePolicyRule } from "./policy-rule.js";
    13	import { RuleEvaluator } from "./rule-evaluator.js";
    14	import { defaultPolicyRules } from "./default-policies.js";
    15	
    16	/** Load PolicyRule[] from disk or return defaults. */
    17	export async function loadPolicyRules(cwd: string): Promise<PolicyRule[]> {
    18	  const policiesDir = join(cwd, ".alix", "policies");
    19	  if (!existsSync(policiesDir)) {
    20	    return defaultPolicyRules();
    21	  }
    22	
    23	  const files = await readdir(policiesDir);
    24	  const jsonFiles = files.filter(f => f.endsWith(".json"));
    25	  if (jsonFiles.length === 0) {
    26	    return defaultPolicyRules();
    27	  }
    28	
    29	  const rules: PolicyRule[] = [];
    30	  const seenIds = new Set<string>();
    31	
    32	  for (const f of jsonFiles) {
    33	    try {
    34	      const raw = await readFile(join(policiesDir, f), "utf-8");
    35	      const parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
    36	
    37	      // Single rule or array
    38	      const items: unknown[] = Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : [parsed];
    39	
    40	      for (const item of items) {
    41	        const rule = item as PolicyRule;
    42	        const validation = validatePolicyRule(rule);
    43	        if (!validation.valid) {
    44	          console.warn(`Skipping invalid policy rule in ${f}: ${validation.errors.join("; ")}`);
    45	          continue;
    46	        }
    47	        if (seenIds.has(rule.id)) {
    48	          console.warn(`Skipping duplicate policy rule ID: ${rule.id} in ${f}`);
    49	          continue;
    50	        }
    51	        seenIds.add(rule.id);
    52	        rules.push(rule);
    53	      }
    54	    } catch (err) {
    55	      console.warn(`Skipping invalid policy file ${f}: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`);
    56	    }
    57	  }
    58	
    59	  return rules.length > 0 ? rules : defaultPolicyRules();
    60	}
    61	
    62	/** Convenience: load rules and wrap in a RuleEvaluator. */
    63	export async function loadRuleEvaluator(cwd: string): Promise<RuleEvaluator> {
    64	  const rules = await loadPolicyRules(cwd);
    65	  return new RuleEvaluator(rules);
    66	}

    59	## 4. Independence was obtainable, and I was wrong that it was not
    60	
    61	I originally wrote here that independence was absent because no second party could
    62	produce it. That was too strong. This repository already had precedent —
    63	model-independent review by a different model family, on a pinned commit, with the
    64	prompt and verbatim output committed — and it was used for Gate B.
    65	
    66	So it was used here too (§9). The reviewer returned **NO**.
    67	
    68	The lesson is worth stating plainly: independence was not a formality to be
    69	satisfied after the tests were green. It was the step that revealed the tests were
    70	green without establishing their controls. Had it been treated as available from
    71	the start, the record would never have claimed 5/5.
    72	
    73	## 5. Two validator decisions worth stating
    74	
    75	**Exit `3`, not `0`.** A sound author-only record exits `3`. If it exited `0`, a CI
    76	step would read "the record validates" as "Gate E closed".
    77	
    78	**And a third the review had to teach me (D10).** That distinction only covered the
    79	author-only path: a well-formed record with one `partial` clause returned `ok: true`
    80	and `HOLD`, and exited **0** from the `ok` branch. A HOLD read as a pass. HOLD now
    81	always exits non-zero, and `independence.qualifier` must cite an existing artifact
    82	that names the qualifier (D9) — a record can no longer declare its own independence
    83	from free text.
    84	
    85	**`pathBase` is required.** The record declares whether its citations resolve beside
    86	the record file or from the repository root. Both are legitimate; guessing is not.
    87	A silent default either rejects valid citations or accepts nonexistent ones, and
    88	either way the path check becomes decorative. (Both Gate B's and Gate F's validators
    89	learned this the same way — by failing on a real record.)
    90

   106	## 6.1 Suite repair found while verifying this record
   107	
   108	Running the full suite to confirm the record's numbers surfaced 20 failures that
   109	had nothing to do with Gate E, and they were **pre-existing**: both suites fail
   110	identically at parent commit `ea863a25` in a clean worktree.
   111	
   112	The cause was a fixture defect, not a product defect. Two fixtures configured model
   113	tiers under `subagents.<tier>`, but `createModelResolver` reads `config.models[tier]`.
   114	So `getRoleModel` threw "Subagent tier is unconfigured" and every assertion
   115	downstream of `spawn()` observed that error instead of the behaviour it was written
   116	to check.
   117	
   118	Type-checking could not catch it: §2.8.1/§2.8.4 made `subagents.<tier>` a
   119	loader-derived compatibility projection — genuinely part of the type, never
   120	persisted, never the source. The fixtures kept the projection and lost the source.
   121	
   122	| Suite | Before | After |
   123	|---|---|---|
   124	| `subagent-manager.test.ts` | 3/19 | **19/19** |
   125	| `subagent-worker-executor.test.ts` | 9/13 | **13/13** |
   126	
   127	Node lane after repair: **8915 pass, 0 fail**. Both are recorded in the Gate E
   128	record under `suiteRepair`. They are **not** Gate E evidence — the five clauses cite
   129	different files — but a suite reporting 20 failures cannot be read as green, so the
   130	repair is written down rather than left implicit.
   131	
   132	Two tests were *cancelled*, not failed, by resource contention in the parallel run:
   133	`cli-discover.test.js` spent 48 minutes under contention and passes in 11s
   134	standalone, and `ContextCompiler.warm()` timed out at 120s but passes in 2s

    19	const DEFAULT_GLOB_LIMIT = 500;

    22	function clampLimit(value: number | undefined, fallback: number): number {
    23	  if (typeof value !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(value) || value <= 0) return fallback;
    24	  return Math.min(Math.floor(value), MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT);
    25	}

    27	function escapeRegExp(text: string): string {
    28	  return text.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&");
    29	}
    30	
    31	/**
    32	 * Strip a leading inline-flags group (e.g. `(?i)`, `(?-i)`) from a pattern and
    33	 * fold it into the `caseSensitive` flag. JavaScript regexes do not support
    34	 * inline flags, so without this `(?i)TODO` is an invalid pattern and would be
    35	 * silently treated as a literal (returning no matches). Returns the cleaned
    36	 * pattern and the effective case sensitivity.
    37	 */
    38	function stripInlineFlags(
    39	  pattern: string,
    40	  caseSensitive: boolean | undefined,
    41	): { pattern: string; caseSensitive: boolean } {
    42	  let cs = caseSensitive === true;
    43	  let p = pattern;
    44	  const m = /^\(\?([a-z]*)(?:-([a-z]+))?\)/.exec(p);
    45	  if (m) {
    46	    const on = m[1] ?? "";
    47	    const off = m[2] ?? "";
    48	    if (on.includes("i")) cs = false;
    49	    if (off.includes("i")) cs = true;
    50	    p = p.slice(m[0].length);
    51	  }
    52	  return { pattern: p, caseSensitive: cs };
    53	}

    55	/**
    56	 * Walk workspace files (relative paths), skipping ignored directories and
    57	 * gitignored paths. Sequential and bounded by the caller's early exit.
    58	 */
    59	export async function* walkWorkspaceFiles(
    60	  root: string,
    61	  ignorePatterns: string[],
    62	  subdir?: string,
    63	): AsyncGenerator<string> {
    64	  const resolvedRoot = resolve(root);
    65	  const start = subdir ? resolve(resolvedRoot, subdir) : resolvedRoot;
    66	  // Fail closed for a scope that escapes the workspace.
    67	  const relStart = relative(resolvedRoot, start);
    68	  if (relativeIsOutside(relStart)) return;
    69	  async function* walk(dir: string): AsyncGenerator<string> {
    70	    let entries;
    71	    try {
    72	      entries = await readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true });
    73	    } catch {
    74	      return;
    75	    }
    76	    for (const entry of entries) {
    77	      const full = join(dir, entry.name);
    78	      const rel = relative(resolvedRoot, full).split(sep).join("/");
    79	      if (entry.isDirectory()) {
    80	        if (IGNORED_DIRS.has(entry.name)) continue;
    81	        if (isIgnoredPath(rel, ignorePatterns)) continue;
    82	        yield* walk(full);
    83	      } else if (entry.isFile()) {
    84	        if (isIgnoredPath(rel, ignorePatterns)) continue;
    85	        yield rel;
    86	      }
    87	    }
    88	  }
    89	  yield* walk(start);
    90	}
    91	
    92	/** Stream a file's lines; returns early for binary-looking content (NUL byte). */
    93	async function* readLinesStreaming(path: string): AsyncGenerator<{ lineNumber: number; line: string }> {
    94	  const stream = createReadStream(path, { encoding: "utf-8" });
    95	  const rl = createInterface({ input: stream, crlfDelay: Infinity });
    96	  let lineNumber = 0;
    97	  try {
    98	    for await (const line of rl) {
    99	      lineNumber++;
   100	      if (lineNumber === 1 && line.includes("\u0000")) return; // binary file
   101	      yield { lineNumber, line };
   102	    }
   103	  } finally {
   104	    rl.close();
   105	    stream.destroy();
   106	  }
   107	}

   109	export type GrepSearchArgs = {
   110	  root: string;
   111	  pattern: string;
   112	  caseSensitive?: boolean;
   113	  include?: string[];
   114	  headLimit?: number;
   115	  path?: string;
   116	};
   117	
   118	/**
   119	 * Content search across the workspace (#719). Regex by default (falls back
   120	 * to a literal match for invalid regexes), bounded by headLimit.
   121	 */
   122	export async function grepSearch(args: GrepSearchArgs): Promise<ToolResult> {
   123	  const { root } = args;
   124	  const headLimit = clampLimit(args.headLimit, DEFAULT_GREP_LIMIT);
   125	  const normalized = stripInlineFlags(args.pattern, args.caseSensitive);
   126	  const pattern = normalized.pattern;
   127	  const flags = normalized.caseSensitive ? "" : "i";
   128	  let matcher: RegExp;
   129	  try {
   130	    matcher = new RegExp(pattern, flags);
   131	  } catch {
   132	    matcher = new RegExp(escapeRegExp(pattern), flags);
   133	  }
   134	  const include = args.include?.filter(Boolean) ?? [];
   135	  const ignorePatterns = loadGitignore(root);
   136	  const matches: FileMatch[] = [];
   137	
   138	  for await (const rel of walkWorkspaceFiles(root, ignorePatterns, args.path)) {
   139	    if (include.length > 0 && !include.some((g) => minimatch(rel, g, { dot: true }))) continue;
   140	    try {
   141	      for await (const { lineNumber, line } of readLinesStreaming(join(root, rel))) {
   142	        if (matcher.test(line)) {
   143	          matches.push({ path: rel, lineNumber, line });
   144	          if (matches.length >= headLimit) return { kind: "success", matches };
   145	        }
   146	      }
   147	    } catch {
   148	      // skip unreadable files
   149	    }
   150	  }
   151	  return { kind: "success", matches };
   152	}

     1	/**
     2	 * pre-r032-non-bypass.vitest.ts — PRE-R032 non-bypass demonstration.
     3	 *
     4	 * WHAT THIS PROVES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT
     5	 *
     6	 * PRE-R032 requires a demonstration that supervision never bypasses existing
     7	 * authorization. No supervision/eligibility engine is implemented, so there is
     8	 * no feature to test for bypass — and asserting "it works" would be testing code
     9	 * that does not exist.
    10	 *
    11	 * What CAN be proven today, and is proven here, is the structural half: the
    12	 * authorization controls an eligibility layer would have to route through are
    13	 * themselves authoritative, and nothing consults an eligibility record to widen
    14	 * a decision. That makes the future bypass surface small and named.
    15	 *
    16	 * This is a parity table, not a spot check: expected outcomes are declared for
    17	 * every direction (deny stays deny, allow is not invented, consumed cannot be
    18	 * reused, scope still decides) so a regression in any one direction fails.
    19	 *
    20	 * @module
    21	 */
    22	
    23	import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";
    24	import { mkdtempSync, rmSync } from "node:fs";

    33	}

    36	describe("authorization is not authority-by-adjacency", () => {

    40	    // The full declared outcome table, not just the new case: a permissive mode
    41	    // must not convert a hard deny in ANY direction.

    51	      } as never);

    80	  it("no source module consults an eligibility record to widen a decision", async () => {
    81	    // The future bypass would look like: policy says deny, then something reads
    82	    // an eligibility/promotion record and returns allow. Nothing may do that.
    83	    const { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } = await import("node:fs");
    84	    const { join } = await import("node:path");
    85	    const walk = (dir: string): string[] => {
    86	      const out: string[] = [];
    87	      for (const entry of readdirSync(dir)) {
    88	        const full = join(dir, entry);
    89	        if (statSync(full).isDirectory()) out.push(...walk(full));
    90	        else if (full.endsWith(".ts")) out.push(full);
    91	      }
    92	      return out;
    93	    };
    94	
    95	    const gateSource = readFileSync(
    96	      join(process.cwd(), "src/governance/policy/policy-gate.ts"),
    97	      "utf-8",
    98	    );
    99	    // The gate itself must not know about eligibility at all. If it ever does,
   100	    // this test should be replaced by a real parity table over that coupling
   101	    // rather than deleted.
   102	    expect(gateSource).not.toMatch(/eligibility/i);
   103	
   104	    // Scan the WHOLE policy tree and actually populate `offenders`.
   105	    //
   106	    // This array was declared and asserted empty without ever being filled, so
   107	    // the assertion could not fail: the walker ran only for a length sanity
   108	    // check (Gate E review, vacuous assertion #3). A scan that cannot report a
   109	    // hit is not a scan.
   110	    // One scanner, used by both the assertion and its own negative test.
   111	    const offenders = scanEligibilityWidening(join(process.cwd(), "src/governance/policy"));
   112	    const scanned = walk(join(process.cwd(), "src/governance/policy"));
   113	    // Sanity: the walker works, so an empty `offenders` is a real negative.
   114	    expect(scanned.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
   115	    expect(offenders).toEqual([]);
   116	  });
   117	});

   148	describe("approvals cannot be minted, widened or reused", () => {

   165	    const { readFileSync } = await import("node:fs");

   167	      join(process.cwd(), "src/governance/approvals/approval-store.ts"),
   168	      "utf-8",
   169	    );
   170	    // Each guard is a refusal that must exist independently: removing any one
   171	    // would let a stale or foreign approval authorize an invocation.
   172	    for (const guard of [
   173	      /status !== "approved"/,

   175	      /expiryState === "invalid"/,
   176	      /expiryState === "expired"/,

   179	    ]) {

   212	// ── The scanners themselves must be able to report a hit ──────────────────
   213	//
   214	// Gate E review, vacuous assertions #3-#5: three source-text scans asserted a
   215	// clean result while being unable to produce a dirty one. The pattern is
   216	// identical each time — a scan whose failure path is never exercised reads as
   217	// coverage. These tests exercise the failure path directly.
   218	describe("source scanners can detect what they claim to forbid", () => {
   219	  it("the eligibility scan would flag a decision-widening read", () => {
   220	    // Calls the SAME predicate the real scan uses. The earlier version
   221	    // re-implemented the regex here, so the copy could pass while the scanner
   222	    // drifted — it proved the copy worked, not the guard.
   223	    expect(eligibilityWideningPattern("const e = eligibility.read(); return decision;")).toBe(true);
   224	    expect(eligibilityWideningPattern("const decision = allow;")).toBe(false);
   225	    expect(eligibilityWideningPattern("// eligibility is documented elsewhere")).toBe(false);
   226	  });
   227	
   228	  it("the consumed-status writer count would catch a second writer", () => {
   229	    expect(countConsumedWriters('this.status = "consumed";')).toBe(1);
   230	    expect(countConsumedWriters('this.status = "consumed"; other.status = "consumed";')).toBe(2);
   231	    // Object.assign-style writes are invisible to this scan — a real limitation,
   232	    // recorded rather than papered over.
   233	    expect(countConsumedWriters('Object.assign(r, { status: "consumed" });')).toBe(0);
   234	  });
   235	
   236	  it("the required-guard scan reports a deleted guard", () => {
   237	    const all = [
   238	      'if (r.status !== "approved") {}',
   239	      'const expiryState = approvalExpiryState(r.expiresAt, now);',
   240	      'if (expiryState === "invalid") {}',
   241	      'if (expiryState === "expired") {}',
   242	      'if (r.bindingKey !== expectedBindingKey) {}',
   243	      'invocationMatches(x)',
   244	    ].join(" ");
   245	    expect(missingApprovalGuards(all)).toEqual([]);
   246	    const withoutOne = all.replace('if (r.bindingKey !== expectedBindingKey) {}', "");
   247	    expect(missingApprovalGuards(withoutOne)).toHaveLength(1);
   248	  });

     2	 * approval-consumed-propagation.test.ts — pins the consumption hand-off.
     3	 *
     4	 * The coordination exact-binding branch consumes the approval INSIDE the gate
     5	 * and reports `approvalConsumed: true`. The executor must trust that flag and
     6	 * NOT claim again, or a legitimate worker is denied by a double-consume. This
     7	 * suite pins the flag's whole journey:
     8	 *
     9	 *   PolicyGateDecision.approvalConsumed
    10	 *     → ExecutionDecision.allowed.approvalConsumed
    11	 *       → the executor's claim guard.

    14	 * its fix commit.
    15	 */

     1	/**
     2	 * path-scope.ts — Deterministic path scope overlap detection.
     3	 *
     4	 * Uses constrained PathScope (root + recursive) instead of heuristic
     5	 * minimatch intersection. Two operations:
     6	 *
     7	 * 1. `pathScopesOverlap(a, b)` — SYMMETRIC. Returns true if there exists
     8	 *    any real path that falls under both scopes.
     9	 *
    10	 * 2. `scopeContains(scope, target)` — DIRECTIONAL. Returns true if the
    11	 *    scope covers the specific target path.
    12	 */
    13	
    14	import { resolve, relative, normalize } from "node:path";
    15	import { relativeIsOutside } from "../../runtime-state/runtime/workspace-path.js";
    16	import type { PathScope } from "./ownership-types.js";
    17	
    18	/**
    19	 * Check whether two path scopes overlap (SYMMETRIC).
    20	 */
    21	export function pathScopesOverlap(a: PathScope, b: PathScope): boolean {
    22	  if (a.root === b.root) return true;
    23	
    24	  // A is recursive and B's root sits inside A
    25	  if (a.recursive && isInside(a.root, b.root)) return true;
    26	
    27	  // B is recursive and A's root sits inside B
    28	  if (b.recursive && isInside(b.root, a.root)) return true;
    29	
    30	  return false;
    31	}
    32	
    33	/**
    34	 * Check whether a scope contains a specific target path (DIRECTIONAL).
    35	 */
    36	export function scopeContains(scope: PathScope, targetPath: string): boolean {
    37	  const target = normalize(targetPath);
    38	
    39	  if (target === scope.root) return true;
    40	  if (!scope.recursive) return false;
    41	
    42	  return isInside(scope.root, target);
    43	}
    44	
    45	/**
    46	 * Alias for scopeContains — kept for compatibility.
    47	 */
    48	export function pathInScope(scope: PathScope, targetPath: string): boolean {
    49	  return scopeContains(scope, targetPath);
    50	}
    51	
    52	/**
    53	 * Normalize a raw pattern into a PathScope.
    54	 *
    55	 * Accepted patterns (constrained for M0.75):
    56	 *   src/runtime          → { root: "/abs/src/runtime", recursive: false }
    57	 *   src/runtime-state/runtime/         → { root: "/abs/src/runtime", recursive: true }
    58	 *   src/runtime-state/runtime/**       → { root: "/abs/src/runtime", recursive: true }
    59	 *   /absolute/path       → { root: "/absolute/path", recursive: false }
    60	 *   src/runtime-state/runtime/executor.ts → { root: "/abs/src/runtime-state/runtime/executor.ts", recursive: false }
    61	 *
    62	 * Rejected:
    63	 *   src/../              — segment traversal
    64	 *   empty string
    65	 *   /outside/workspace   — absolute paths outside workspace root
    66	 */
    67	export function normalizePathScope(pattern: string, cwd: string, workspaceRoot?: string): PathScope {
    68	  const trimmed = pattern.trim();
    69	
    70	  // Reject empty/blank scopes
    71	  if (!trimmed) {
    72	    throw new Error("Path scope must not be empty");
    73	  }
    74	
    75	  // Normalize backslashes (platform support)
    76	  const normalized = trimmed.replace(/\\/g, "/");
    77	
    78	  // Reject .. path segments (not substring ".." — src/foo..bar is valid)
    79	  const segments = normalized.split("/").filter(Boolean);
    80	  if (segments.some(s => s === "..")) {
    81	    throw new Error(`Path scope must not contain ".." traversal: ${trimmed}`);
    82	  }
    83	
    84	  // Reject unsupported wildcards: *, ?, {}, []
    85	  // Allow only /** as a suffix
    86	  const stripped = normalized.replace(/\/\*\*$/, "");
    87	  if (/[*?[\]{}]/.test(stripped)) {
    88	    throw new Error(`Unsupported wildcard pattern: ${trimmed}. Accepted: path, path/, path/**`);
    89	  }
    90	
    91	  // Determine if recursive
    92	  const isRecursive = normalized.endsWith("/**") || normalized.endsWith("/");
    93	
    94	  // Strip /** suffix to get root directory
    95	  let root = normalized
    96	    .replace(/\/\*\*$/, "")
    97	    .replace(/\/$/, "");
    98	
    99	  // Resolve relative paths against cwd
   100	  const absolute = resolve(cwd, root);
   101	
   102	  // Reject absolute paths outside workspace
   103	  if (workspaceRoot && !isInside(workspaceRoot, absolute)) {
   104	    throw new Error(`Path scope ${trimmed} resolves outside workspace (${workspaceRoot})`);
   105	  }
   106	
   107	  return {
   108	    kind: "path" as const,
   109	    root: absolute,
   110	    recursive: isRecursive,
   111	  };
   112	}
   113	
   114	function isInside(parent: string, child: string): boolean {
   115	  // Same path is inside (allows workspace root as scope)
   116	  if (parent === child) return true;
   117	  const rel = relative(parent, child);
   118	  return rel !== "" && !relativeIsOutside(rel);
   119	}
   120	
   121	/** Get a display-friendly scope string. */
   122	export function formatScope(scope: PathScope): string {
   123	  return scope.recursive ? `${scope.root}/**` : scope.root;
   124	}

   126	// ─── Owned-write scopes (single authority) ─────────────────────────────
   127	
   128	/**
   129	 * True when an owned-path entry is a workspace-wide grant: `.`, or a pattern
   130	 * whose every non-empty segment is `*` or `**`.
   131	 *
   132	 * This is a RULE, not an enumeration. An enumerated list of spellings was
   133	 * incomplete — several multi-star forms fell through to the reject branch, and
   134	 * only a future edit would have added them. Deriving it means a spelling nobody
   135	 * thought of still resolves to the workspace rather than to nothing.
   136	 *
   137	 * The rule must be a strict SUPERSET of any list it replaces. An earlier
   138	 * version split on the separator and demanded every segment be a star, which
   139	 * silently narrowed the grant: the dot-slash spellings (dot-slash-star and
   140	 * dot-slash-globstar-slash-star) were both workspace-wide and began denying.
   141	 * A leading dot-slash and a leading slash are cosmetic, so both are stripped
   142	 * before the segments are examined — treating them as scope is the bug.
   143	 */
   144	function isWorkspaceWideGrant(normalized: string): boolean {
   145	  const trimmed = normalized.trim();
   146	  if (trimmed === "." || trimmed === "./" || trimmed === "/") return true;
   147	  // Strip cosmetic prefixes and suffixes — a leading dot-slash, a leading
   148	  // slash, and any trailing slashes. All of them mean the same workspace-wide
   149	  // grant. Anything left that is not a star segment (a real directory name)
   150	  // makes this an ordinary scoped path instead.
   151	  const bare = trimmed
   152	    .replace(/^\.\//, "")
   153	    .replace(/^\/+|\/+$/g, "");
   154	  return bare.length > 0 && bare.split("/").every(segment => segment === "*" || segment === "**");
   155	}
   156	
   157	/**
   158	 * Reduce an owned-path entry to the absolute directory prefix it authorizes,
   159	 * or `undefined` when the entry cannot be reduced safely.
   160	 *
   161	 * Accepts a path, a directory (`docs/`), a recursive scope (`docs/**`), or a
   162	 * workspace-wide grant (see {@link isWorkspaceWideGrant}). Fails closed on `..` traversal and on
   163	 * wildcards it cannot interpret — an uninterpretable grant authorizes nothing
   164	 * rather than everything.
   165	 */
   166	export function resolveOwnedScopePrefix(raw: string, cwd: string): string | undefined {
   167	  const normalized = raw.trim().replace(/\\/g, "/");
   168	  if (normalized.length === 0) return undefined;
   169	  // Fail closed on Windows drive spellings on every platform: on Windows they
   170	  // can name locations outside the workspace, and on POSIX they would otherwise
   171	  // create surprising literal `C:` entries under the workspace.
   172	  if (/^[A-Za-z]:(?:[\/]|$)/.test(normalized)) return undefined;
   173	  // `resolve` normalizes a trailing separator, so a cwd of "/tmp/" cannot
   174	  // silently disable a workspace-wide grant.
   175	  if (isWorkspaceWideGrant(normalized)) return resolve(cwd);
   176	
   177	  const stripped = normalized
   178	    .replace(/\/\*\*$/, "")
   179	    .replace(/\*\*\/$/, "")
   180	    .replace(/\/+$/, "");
   181	  if (stripped.length === 0) return resolve(cwd);
   182	
   183	  const segments = stripped.split("/").filter(Boolean);
   184	  if (segments.some(segment => segment === "..")) return undefined;
   185	  if (/[*?[\]{}]/.test(stripped)) return undefined;
   186	  const absolute = resolve(cwd, stripped);
   187	  // An owned entry that resolves OUTSIDE the workspace is not an owned scope —
   188	  // the sibling `normalizePathScope` rejects the same case, and silently
   189	  // authorizing `/etc` because a worker wrote it in `ownedPaths` would be a
   190	  // privilege escalation dressed as a convenience.
   191	  const rel = relative(resolve(cwd), absolute);
   192	  if (relativeIsOutside(rel)) return undefined;
   193	  return absolute;
   194	}
   195	
   196	/**
   197	 * True when `resolvedTarget` sits inside one of the caller's owned scopes.
   198	 * The single ownership matcher: the policy gate and the file router MUST both
   199	 * call this, or one of them will authorize (or deny) something the other
   200	 * disagrees with.
   201	 */
   202	export function isWithinOwnedScope(
   203	  resolvedTarget: string,
   204	  ownedPaths: readonly string[],
   205	  cwd: string,
   206	): boolean {
   207	  return ownedPaths.some(raw => {
   208	    const prefix = resolveOwnedScopePrefix(raw, cwd);
   209	    return prefix !== undefined && isInside(prefix, resolvedTarget);
   210	  });
   211	}

   213	// ─── Planning-side claim overlap ───────────────────────────────────────
   214	
   215	export type RawOwnershipClaim = { path: string; recursive: boolean };
   216	
   217	/**
   218	 * True when two workspace-relative planning claims can both cover some path.
   219	 * The planner's overlap question lives HERE (one matcher module) so planning
   220	 * serialization, lease conflicts, and runtime authorization cannot drift into
   221	 * three disagreeing answers. `path === "."` is the workspace-wide claim.
   222	 * Inputs are workspace-relative strings as captured by the planner; absolute
   223	 * or `..` shapes are rejected at claim-capture time, not here.
   224	 */
   225	export function claimScopesOverlap(a: RawOwnershipClaim, b: RawOwnershipClaim): boolean {
   226	  const contains = (claim: RawOwnershipClaim, path: string): boolean =>
   227	    claim.path === "." || claim.path === path || (claim.recursive && path.startsWith(`${claim.path}/`));
   228	  return contains(a, b.path) || contains(b, a.path);
   229	}

   389	  private pruneUnlocked(opts?: { olderThanDays?: number }): number {
   390	    const cutoff = Date.now() - ((opts?.olderThanDays ?? HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS) * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000);
   391	    const before = this.records.length;
   392	    this.records = this.records.filter(r => {
   393	      if (r.status === "active" && !this.isExpired(r)) return true;
   394	      const t = r.expiredAt ?? r.revokedAt ?? r.releasedAt ?? r.expiresAt;
   395	      return new Date(t).getTime() >= cutoff;
   396	    });
   397	    const removed = before - this.records.length;
   398	    if (removed > 0) this.markChanged();
   399	    return removed;
   400	  }

   117	  private checkPath(rawPath: string): ToolResult | null {
   118	    const result = this.pathResolver.check(rawPath);
   119	    if (!result.insideWorkspace || !this.pathResolver.isCanonicalInWorkspace(result.absolute)) {

   798	  try {
   799	    for (const { owned, path, allowed } of cases) {
   800	      const router = new FileToolRouter("/tmp");
   801	      const result = await router.execute({
   802	        toolCallId: "1",
   803	        name: "file.create",
   804	        args: { path, content: "x" },
   805	        ...(owned ? { ownedPaths: owned } : {}),
   806	      });
   807	      assert.strictEqual(result.kind, allowed ? "success" : "error", `${JSON.stringify(owned)} -> ${path}`);
   808	      const written = await readFile(resolve("/tmp", path), "utf8").then(() => true, () => false);
   809	      assert.strictEqual(written, allowed, `${JSON.stringify(owned)} -> ${path} must ${allowed ? "" : "not "}be written`);
   810	    }
   811	  } finally {
   812	    await rm(`/tmp/${ws}`, { recursive: true, force: true });
   813	    await rm(`/tmp/outside-${process.pid}.txt`, { force: true });
   814	  }
   815	});

    18	/**
    19	 * Resolve a tool name that may be misspelled or unknown.
    20	 * Uses fuzzy search to find the closest match in the MCP tool index.
    21	 */
    22	type SessionState = {
    23	  created: Set<string>;
    24	  deleted: Set<string>;
    25	  changed: Set<string>;
    26	  fatalErrors: string[];
    27	  pendingScopeExpansion: boolean;
    28	};
    29	
    30	/**
    31	 * Build a human-readable summary of session state changes.
    32	 */
    33	export function buildStateSummary(state: SessionState): string {
    34	  const parts: string[] = [];
    35	  if (state.created.size) parts.push(`Created: ${[...state.created].join(", ")}`);
    36	  if (state.changed.size) parts.push(`Changed: ${[...state.changed].join(", ")}`);
    37	  if (state.deleted.size) parts.push(`Deleted: ${[...state.deleted].join(", ")}`);
    38	  if (state.fatalErrors.length) parts.push(`FATAL: ${state.fatalErrors.join("; ")}`);
    39	  return parts.length ? `[Session Digest] ${parts.join(". ")}.` : "";
    40	}

    42	/**
    43	 * Generate tool description for patch format based on policy.
    44	 */
    45	export function patchFormatDescription(policy: EditFormatPolicy): string {
    46	  const preferred = policy.preferred;
    47	  const alternate = preferred === "search_replace" ? "structured_patch" : "search_replace";
    48	  return `Patch format. Preferred: ${preferred}. Use ${preferred} unless the user explicitly asks for ${alternate}. unified_diff is also accepted and auto-detected. Do not use full_file for existing files. Full-file rewrite policy: ${policy.fullFileRewrite}. For small edits to existing files prefer search_replace (exact original block, no hash needed); use structured_patch for large rewrites with a correct preimageHash.`;
    49	}
    50	
    51	/**
    52	 * Generate tool description for patch text based on preferred format.
    53	 */
    54	export function patchTextDescription(preferred: EditFormatPolicy["preferred"]): string {
    55	  if (preferred === "structured_patch") {
    56	    return `The patch content. Preferred structured_patch format is a JSON object: {"version":1,"files":[{"path":"src/file.ts","operation":"modify","preimageHash":"<sha256 hex of the CURRENT file content>","content":"<full new content>"}]}. preimageHash must be the exact sha256 of the file as it exists now (read the file first; compute it with sha256sum) — a literal placeholder never validates. For small edits prefer search_replace with the exact original block instead (no hash needed). unified_diff is also accepted and auto-detected.`;
    57	  }
    58	  if (preferred === "unified_diff") {
    59	    return "The patch content. Preferred unified_diff format is a standard git diff: --- a/<file> / +++ b/<file> / @@ hunk headers. search_replace and structured_patch are also accepted.";
    60	  }
    61	  return "The patch content. Preferred search_replace format:\n<<<<<<< SEARCH path=<file>\n<original>\n=======\n<replacement>\n>>>>>>> REPLACE\nunified_diff is also accepted and auto-detected.";
    62	}

    87	  // ═══ Internal load/save (only inside withLock) ═══════════════════
    88	
    89	  private reloadFromDisk(): boolean {
    90	    try {
    91	      const raw = readFileSync(this.storagePath, "utf-8");
    92	      const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as Partial<OwnershipStore>;
    93	      if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== "object" || parsed.version !== STORE_VERSION ||
    94	          !Array.isArray(parsed.records) || !Number.isInteger(parsed.revision) || (parsed.revision ?? -1) < 0) {
    95	        this.records = [];
    96	        this.revision = 0;
    97	        return false;
    98	      }
    99	      const validModes = new Set(["exclusive-write", "shared-read", "review-only"]);
   100	      const validStatuses = new Set(["active", "released", "expired", "revoked"]);
   101	      const validRecord = (record: OwnershipRecord): boolean =>
   102	        !!record &&
   103	        typeof record.id === "string" && record.id.length > 0 &&
   104	        typeof record.agentId === "string" && record.agentId.length > 0 &&
   105	        record.scope?.kind === "path" && typeof record.scope.root === "string" &&
   106	        typeof record.scope.recursive === "boolean" &&
   107	        validModes.has(record.mode) && validStatuses.has(record.status) &&
   108	        typeof record.acquiredAt === "string" && !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(record.acquiredAt)) &&
   109	        typeof record.expiresAt === "string" && !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(record.expiresAt));
   110	      if (!parsed.records.every(record => validRecord(record as OwnershipRecord))) {
   111	        this.records = [];
   112	        this.revision = 0;
   113	        return false;
   114	      }
   115	      this.records = parsed.records.map(r => ({
   116	        ...r,
   117	        status: (r.status === "active" && this.isExpired(r)) ? ("expired" as const) : r.status,
   118	      }));
   119	      this.revision = parsed.revision as number;
   120	      return true;
   121	    } catch (err) {
   122	      if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "ENOENT") {
   123	        this.records = [];
   124	        this.revision = 0;
   125	        return true;
   126	      }
   127	      this.records = [];
   128	      this.revision = 0;
   129	      return false;
   130	    }
   131	  }
   132	
   133	  private applyExpiration(): void {
   134	    const now = new Date().toISOString();
   135	    for (const r of this.records) {
   136	      if (r.status === "active" && this.isExpired(r)) {
   137	        r.status = "expired";
   138	        r.expiredAt = now;
   139	        this.changed = true;
   140	        this.queueEvent("ownership.expired", { recordId: r.id, agentId: r.agentId });
   141	      }
   142	    }
   143	  }
   144	
   145	  private persistIfChanged(): void {
   146	    if (!this.changed) return;
   147	    this.revision++;
   148	    const store: OwnershipStore = { version: STORE_VERSION, revision: this.revision, records: this.records };
   149	    mkdirSync(dirname(this.storagePath), { recursive: true });
   150	    const tmp = this.storagePath + ".tmp";
   151	    writeFileSync(tmp, JSON.stringify(store, null, 2), "utf-8");
   152	    renameSync(tmp, this.storagePath);
   153	  }
   154	
   155	  /**
   156	   * Execute fn inside lock. On failure: clear pending events, reload,
   157	   * rethrow. Events emitted after lock release.
   158	   */
   159	  private async withLock<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T | null> {
   160	    const acquired = await this.lock.acquire();
   161	    if (!acquired) {
   162	      await this.emitEvents([{ event: OWNERSHIP_EVENT_TYPES.LOCK_FAILED, data: { reason: "timeout" } }]);
   163	      return null;
   164	    }
   165	    let events: Array<{ event: string; data: Record<string, unknown> }> = [];
   166	    try {
   167	      if (!this.reloadFromDisk()) {
   168	        events = [{ event: OWNERSHIP_EVENT_TYPES.STATE_INVALID, data: { reason: "unreadable_or_malformed" } }];
   169	        return null;
   170	      }
   171	      this.applyExpiration();
   172	      this.changed = false;
   173	      const result = await fn();
   174	      this.persistIfChanged();
   175	      events = this.takePendingEvents();
   176	      return result;
   177	    } catch (err) {
   178	      this.pendingEvents = [];
   179	      this.reloadFromDisk();
   180	      throw err;

     1	/**
     2	 * approval-crash-recovery.test.ts — R1.5 crash-after-consume contract.
     3	 *
     4	 * Consumption and execution cannot be one transaction across a process
     5	 * boundary, so a crash between them is a real state. The contract pinned here:
     6	 *
     7	 *  - a claim is durable and marks the record `executionOutcome: "pending"`;
     8	 *  - a completed execution reports `succeeded` / `failed` / `cancelled`;
     9	 *  - a replay that observes a `pending` claim classifies it `unverified` and
    10	 *    DENIES — the side effect is unknown, so authority is never reissued and
    11	 *    the invocation is never retried automatically;
    12	 *  - uncertainty is listable for an operator without any wall-clock sweep.
    13	 *
    14	 * Every assertion reads real record state and real file effects, not just the
    15	 * returned verdict.
    16	 */
    17

    45	async function makeFixture(label: string): Promise<Fixture> {
    46	  const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), `alix-crash-${label}-`));
    47	  mkdirSync(join(root, ".alix", "approvals"), { recursive: true });
    48	  const log = new EventLog(join(root, ".alix", "sessions", "test"));
    49	  await log.init();
    50	  const store = new ApprovalStore(root, { eventLog: log });
    51	  await store.load();
    52	
    53	  const config = structuredClone(DEFAULT_CONFIG);
    54	  config.permissions.sessionMode = "ask";
    55	  config.permissions.tools = { "shell.run": "ask", "file.read": "ask", "file.create": "ask" };
    56	
    57	  const executor = createToolExecutor({ config, log, root, approvalStore: store });
    58	  return { root, log, store, config, executor, cleanup: () => rmSync(root, { recursive: true, force: true }) };
    59	}

    61	function effectCount(root: string): number {
    62	  if (!existsSync(join(root, "effects.txt"))) return 0;
    63	  return readFileSync(join(root, "effects.txt"), "utf8").trim().split("\n").filter(Boolean).length;
    64	}

    67	  f: Fixture,

    91	      const claim = await f.store.consumeApproved(record.id, record.bindingKey, {}, record.invocation);

   101	      assert.equal(after?.status, "consumed");

    17	  test(`D9 SIGKILL ${point}: persisted claim cannot authorize replay`, { timeout: 30000 }, async () => {
    18	    const cwd = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'alix-d9-sigkill-'));
    19	    let child: ReturnType<typeof spawn> | undefined;
    20	    try {
    21	      const store = new ApprovalStore(cwd); await store.load();
    22	      const record = await store.requestOrReusePending({
    23	        reason: 'SIGKILL durability', bindingKey: 'd9-key', requestFingerprint: 'd9-fp',
    24	        policyRevision: 'd9-rev', capabilities: ['file.create'], workerId: 'd9-worker', workerAttempt: 1,
    25	      });
    26	      await store.resolve(record.id, 'approved');
    27	      closeAllSharedLedgers();
    28	      const marker = join(cwd, 'checkpoint');
    29	      const effect = join(cwd, 'effect.txt');
    30	      const code = `
    31	        import { writeFile, appendFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
    32	        import { ApprovalStore } from ${JSON.stringify(storeUrl)};
    33	        const [cwd, id, marker, effect, point] = process.argv.slice(1);
    34	        const store = new ApprovalStore(cwd); await store.load();
    35	        const claim = await store.consumeApproved(id, 'd9-key', {workerId:'d9-worker', workerAttempt:1});
    36	        if (!claim.consumed) process.exit(3);
    37	        if (point === 'after-consume') {
    38	          await writeFile(marker, 'claimed');
    39	        } else {
    40	          await appendFile(effect, 'sentinel\\n');
    41	          await writeFile(marker, 'effect-applied');
    42	        }
    43	        setInterval(() => {}, 1000);
    44	      `;
    45	      child = spawn(process.execPath, ['--input-type=module', '-e', code, cwd, record.id, marker, effect, point], { stdio: 'pipe' });
    46	      let stderr = '';
    47	      child.stderr?.on('data', chunk => { stderr += String(chunk); });
    48	      let ready = false;
    49	      for (let i = 0; i < 150; i++) {
    50	        try { await readFile(marker); ready = true; break; } catch { /* wait */ }
    51	        if (child.exitCode !== null) break;
    52	        await sleep(100);
    53	      }
    54	      assert.ok(ready, `child never reached checkpoint: ${stderr}`);
    55	      const exited = new Promise<{signal: NodeJS.Signals | null}>((resolve, reject) => {
    56	        child!.once('exit', (_code, signal) => resolve({signal}));
    57	        child!.once('error', reject);
    58	      });
    59	      assert.equal(child.kill('SIGKILL'), true);
    60	      assert.equal((await exited).signal, 'SIGKILL');
    61	      child = undefined;
    62	      closeAllSharedLedgers();
    63	      const restarted = new ApprovalStore(cwd); await restarted.load();
    64	      assert.equal(restarted.get(record.id)?.status, 'consumed');
    65	      assert.equal(restarted.get(record.id)?.executionOutcome, 'pending');
    66	      assert.equal((await restarted.consumeApproved(record.id, 'd9-key', {workerId:'d9-worker', workerAttempt:1})).consumed, false);
    67	      assert.equal(await restarted.markExecutionUnverified(record.id), 'unverified');
    68	      await restarted.load();
    69	      assert.equal(restarted.get(record.id)?.executionOutcome, 'unverified');
    70	      const observed = await readFile(effect, 'utf8').catch(() => '');
    71	      assert.deepEqual(observed ? observed.trimEnd().split(String.fromCharCode(10)) : [], point === "after-effect" ? ["sentinel"] : []);
    72	      assert.equal((await restarted.consumeApproved(record.id, 'd9-key', {workerId:'d9-worker', workerAttempt:1})).consumed, false);
    73	      assert.equal(await readFile(effect, 'utf8').catch(() => ''), observed);
    74	    } finally {
    75	      if (child && child.exitCode === null) child.kill('SIGKILL');
    76	      closeAllSharedLedgers();
    77	      await rm(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true });
    78	    }
    79	  });

   384	/**
   385	 * `alix_shell_run` is withheld from read-only scopes. Arbitrary command
   386	 * execution can mutate the workspace (`rm`, `sed -i`, a test suite writing
   387	 * fixtures), so offering it would reopen the hole `--read-only` exists to
   388	 * close. This is a containment boundary, not a scoping accident.
   389	 *
   390	 * The measured cost: a read-only objective that must actually RUN something
   391	 * ("run pnpm typecheck:unused and report whether it passes") is unsatisfiable,
   392	 * because the only tool that could run it is not offered. Cohort
   393	 * `t3d-2026-09-28-c` hit this on 6 of 8 verification-shaped scopes.
   394	 *
   395	 * That scope is *recorded* rather than silently absorbed: `deriveSurfaceGaps`
   396	 * classifies it `absent-upstream`, and the loop now injects an explicit
   397	 * limitation notice so the model reports the constraint instead of quietly
   398	 * substituting a weaker method. Verification-shaped work that genuinely needs
   399	 * execution belongs on the `shellTask` route (per-call `ask`-gated), not here.
   400	 */
   401	export const READ_ONLY_EXCLUDED_TOOL_NAMES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(["alix_shell_run"]);
   402	
   403	/**
   404	 * The single derivation of the read-only offer surface, used by both
   405	 * `agent-loop.ts` and `session/setup.ts`. Two hand-built copies of this filter
   406	 * is how `verify.claim` ended up offered in one route and withheld in the
   407	 * other; the set is now the only place the answer lives.
   408	 */
   409	export function buildReadOnlyToolFilter(extra: Iterable<string> = []): Set<string> {
   410	  const filter = new Set(READ_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES);
   411	  for (const name of READ_ONLY_EXCLUDED_TOOL_NAMES) filter.delete(name);
   412	  for (const name of extra) filter.add(name);
   413	  return filter;
   414	}

    69	async function handleList(stores: ApprovalStore[], args: string[]): Promise<void> {
    70	  const showAll = args.includes("--all");
    71	  const jsonMode = args.includes("--json");
    72	  const runFilter = args.find(a => a.startsWith("--run="))?.split("=")[1];
    73	
    74	  const seen = new Set<string>();
    75	  let approvals = stores
    76	    .flatMap((s) => s.list())
    77	    .filter((a) => (seen.has(a.id) ? false : (seen.add(a.id), true)));
    78	  if (!showAll) approvals = approvals.filter(a => a.status === "pending");
    79	  if (runFilter) approvals = approvals.filter(a => a.coordinationRunId === runFilter);
    80	
    81	  if (jsonMode) {
    82	    console.log(JSON.stringify(approvals, null, 2));
    83	    return;
    84	  }
    85	
    86	  if (approvals.length === 0) {
    87	    console.log("No approvals found.");
    88	    return;
    89	  }
    90	
    91	  for (const a of approvals) {
    92	    console.log(
    93	      `${a.id.padEnd(30)} ${a.status.padEnd(12)} ${(a.capabilities ?? []).join(",").padEnd(20)} ${a.coordinationRunId ?? ""}`
    94	    );
    95	  }
    96	}
    97	
    98	async function handleShow(store: ApprovalStore, args: string[]): Promise<void> {
    99	  const id = args[0];
   100	  if (!id) { console.error("Usage: alix approval show <id>"); process.exit(1); }
   101	  const record = store.get(id);
   102	  if (!record) { console.error(`Approval not found: ${id}`); process.exit(1); }
   103	  console.log(JSON.stringify(record, null, 2));
   104	}
   105	
   106	async function handleResolve(store: ApprovalStore, args: string[], status: "approved" | "denied"): Promise<void> {
   107	  const id = args[0];
   108	  if (!id) { console.error(`Usage: alix approval ${status} <id> [--reason "..."]`); process.exit(1); }
   109	  const reason = args.find(a => a.startsWith("--reason="))?.split("=").slice(1).join("=");
   110	  const record = await store.resolve(id, status, reason);
   111	  if (!record) { console.error(`Approval not found or cannot be resolved: ${id}`); process.exit(1); }
   112	  console.log(`${status.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + status.slice(1)}: ${id}`);
   113	}
   114	
   115	async function handleRevoke(store: ApprovalStore, args: string[]): Promise<void> {
   116	  const id = args[0];
   117	  const reasonArg = args.find(a => a.startsWith("--reason="));
   118	  if (!id || !reasonArg) { console.error("Usage: alix approval revoke <id> --reason=\"...\""); process.exit(1); }
   119	  const reason = reasonArg.split("=").slice(1).join("=");
   120	  const record = await store.revoke(id, { actor: "cli", reason });
   121	  if (!record) { console.error(`Approval not found or cannot be revoked: ${id}`); process.exit(1); }
   122	  console.log(`Revoked: ${id}`);
   123	}
   124	
   125	async function handleExpire(stores: ApprovalStore[], _args: string[]): Promise<void> {
   126	  let count = 0;
   127	  for (const store of stores) count += (await store.expireDue(new Date())).length;
   128	  console.log(`Expired ${count} approval(s).`);
   129	}

    34	      goalPrompt: 'write owned.txt', requiredCapabilities: ['file.create'], attempt: 1,

    36	      status: 'blocked', blockReason: 'approval_required', approvalId: approval.id });

    44	function host(cwd: string, approvalId: string, point: string) {
    45	  const child = spawn(process.execPath, [fileURLToPath(new URL('../fixtures/d9-resumer-crash-child.js', import.meta.url)), cwd, approvalId, point], {
    46	    cwd, env: { PATH: process.env.PATH, HOME: cwd, XDG_CONFIG_HOME: join(cwd, '.config') },
    47	    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe', 'ipc'],
    48	  });
    49	  let stderr = '', observed = false;
    50	  child.stdout!.on('data', data => { stderr += String(data); });
    51	  child.stderr!.on('data', data => { stderr += String(data); });
    52	  const exited = new Promise<{ code: number | null; signal: NodeJS.Signals | null }>((resolve, reject) => {
    53	    child.once('error', reject); child.once('exit', (code, signal) => resolve({ code, signal }));
    54	  });
    55	  const ready = new Promise<number>((resolve, reject) => {
    56	    const timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`No ${point} checkpoint: ${stderr}`)), 20_000);
    57	    child.on('message', message => {
    58	      const data = message as { checkpoint: string; pid: number };
    59	      if (data.checkpoint === (point === 'recover' ? 'recovered' : point)) {
    60	        observed = true; clearTimeout(timer); resolve(data.pid);
    61	      }
    62	    });
    63	    void exited.then(result => { clearTimeout(timer); if (!observed) reject(new Error(`Host exited before ${point}: ${JSON.stringify(result)} ${stderr}`)); }, error => { clearTimeout(timer); reject(error); });
    64	  });
    65	  return { child, exited, ready };
    66	}
    67	
    68	async function snapshot(cwd: string, f: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof seed>>) {
    69	  closeAllSharedLedgers();
    70	  const approvals = new ApprovalStore(cwd); await approvals.load();
    71	  const conts = new ContinuationStore(cwd); await conts.load();

    73	    approval: approvals.loadCommitted(f.approvalId)!,

    75	    continuation: conts.findByApprovalId(f.approvalId),

    77	    entries: await readFile(join(cwd, 'router-entries.jsonl'), 'utf8').catch(error => { if (error.code === 'ENOENT') return ''; throw error; }),
    78	    mtime: await stat(join(cwd, 'owned.txt')).then(s => s.mtimeMs, error => { if (error.code === 'ENOENT') return null; throw error; }),
    79	  };
    80	}

     1	/**
     2	 * workspace-path.ts — Central file-path safety resolver.
     3	 *
     4	 * All file tools, patch operations, and policy checks should resolve
     5	 * paths through this single resolver instead of duplicating logic.
     6	 */
     7	
     8	import { existsSync, realpathSync } from "node:fs";
     9	import { dirname, isAbsolute, relative, resolve, sep } from "node:path";
    10	import { homedir } from "node:os";
    11	
    12	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    13	// Types
    14	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    15	
    16	export type ResolvedPath = {
    17	  absolute: string;
    18	  insideWorkspace: boolean;
    19	  protected: boolean;
    20	  sensitive: boolean;
    21	  reason?: string;
    22	};
    23	
    24	function relativeIsInside(rel: string): boolean {
    25	  return rel === "" || !relativeIsOutside(rel);
    26	}
    27	
    28	/**
    29	 * True when a `relative(root, target)` result escapes `root` — the single
    30	 * lexical containment predicate. `""` (same dir) and in-tree paths are inside;
    31	 * only `..`, `../…`, or an absolute remainder escape. Shared by
    32	 * `WorkspacePathResolver` and the router/patch/coordination backstops so the
    33	 * rule is not re-implemented per site.
    34	 */
    35	export function relativeIsOutside(rel: string): boolean {
    36	  return rel === ".." || rel.startsWith(`..${sep}`) || isAbsolute(rel);
    37	}
    38	
    39	export function isCanonicalPathWithinWorkspace(workspaceRoot: string, targetPath: string): boolean {
    40	  const resolvedRoot = resolve(workspaceRoot);
    41	  if (!existsSync(resolvedRoot)) {
    42	    const rel = relative(resolvedRoot, resolve(targetPath));
    43	    return relativeIsInside(rel);
    44	  }
    45	  const canonicalRoot = realpathSync.native(resolvedRoot);
    46	  let existing = resolve(targetPath);
    47	  while (!existsSync(existing)) {
    48	    const parent = dirname(existing);
    49	    if (parent === existing) return false;
    50	    existing = parent;
    51	  }
    52	  const canonicalExisting = realpathSync.native(existing);
    53	  const rel = relative(canonicalRoot, canonicalExisting);
    54	  return relativeIsInside(rel);
    55	}

    57	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    58	// Sensitive path patterns
    59	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    60	
    61	const SENSITIVE_PATTERNS = [
    62	  /(^|\/)\.ssh($|\/)/,
    63	  /(^|\/)\.gnupg($|\/)/,
    64	  /(^|\/)\..*rc($|\/)/,
    65	  /(^|\/)\.env(\..*)?$/,
    66	  /(^|\/)known_hosts$/,
    67	  /(^|\/)id_rsa/,
    68	  /(^|\/)id_ed25519/,
    69	  /(^|\/)\.alix($|\/)/,
    70	  /(^|\/)\.git($|\/)/,
    71	];
    72	
    73	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    74	// Resolver
    75	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    76	
    77	export class WorkspacePathResolver {
    78	  constructor(
    79	    private readonly workspaceRoot: string,
    80	    private readonly protectedPaths: string[] = [],
    81	  ) {}
    82	
    83	  resolve(rawPath: string): string {
    84	    if (isAbsolute(rawPath)) return rawPath;
    85	    if (rawPath.startsWith("~")) return resolve(homedir(), rawPath.replace(/^~/, homedir()));
    86	    return resolve(this.workspaceRoot, rawPath);
    87	  }
    88	
    89	  isInWorkspace(absolutePath: string): boolean {
    90	    const rel = relative(resolve(this.workspaceRoot), resolve(absolutePath));
    91	    return relativeIsInside(rel);
    92	  }
    93	
    94	  /** Reject lexical escapes and symlink traversal outside the workspace. */
    95	  isCanonicalInWorkspace(absolutePath: string): boolean {
    96	    return isCanonicalPathWithinWorkspace(this.workspaceRoot, absolutePath);
    97	  }
    98	
    99	  isProtected(absolutePath: string): boolean {
   100	    const workspacePath = relative(resolve(this.workspaceRoot), resolve(absolutePath));
   101	    for (const pattern of this.protectedPaths) {
   102	      if (this.matchesPattern(absolutePath, pattern)) return true;
   103	      if (this.matchesPattern(workspacePath, pattern)) return true;
   104	    }
   105	    return false;
   106	  }
   107	
   108	  isSensitive(absolutePath: string): boolean {
   109	    return SENSITIVE_PATTERNS.some((re) => re.test(absolutePath.replaceAll("\\", "/")));
   110	  }
   111	
   112	  check(rawPath: string): ResolvedPath {
   113	    const absolute = this.resolve(rawPath);
   114	    const sensitive = this.isSensitive(absolute);
   115	    const insideWorkspace = this.isInWorkspace(absolute);
   116	    const protected_ = this.isProtected(absolute);
   117	
   118	    if (sensitive) {
   119	      return { absolute, insideWorkspace, protected: protected_, sensitive, reason: "Path matches a sensitive system pattern" };
   120	    }
   121	    if (protected_ && insideWorkspace) {
   122	      return { absolute, insideWorkspace, protected: true, sensitive: false, reason: "Path matches a protected pattern" };
   123	    }
   124	    return { absolute, insideWorkspace, protected: false, sensitive: false };
   125	  }
   126	
   127	  isTraversalSafe(rawPath: string): boolean {
   128	    if (rawPath.startsWith("..")) return false;
   129	    if (isAbsolute(rawPath)) return this.isInWorkspace(rawPath);
   130	    if (rawPath.includes("../")) return false;
   131	    if (rawPath.startsWith("~")) return false;
   132	    if (rawPath.startsWith("$")) return false;
   133	    return true;
   134	  }
   135	
   136	  private matchesPattern(path: string, pattern: string): boolean {
   137	    path = path.replaceAll("\\", "/");
   138	    pattern = pattern.replaceAll("\\", "/");
   139	    if (pattern.endsWith("/**")) {
   140	      const prefix = pattern.slice(0, -3);
   141	      return path === prefix || path.startsWith(prefix + "/");
   142	    }
   143	    if (pattern.endsWith(".*")) {
   144	      return path === pattern.slice(0, -2) || path.startsWith(pattern.slice(0, -1));
   145	    }
   146	    return path === pattern;
   147	  }
   148	}
     1	/**
     2	 * mutation-targets.ts — Extract file system mutation targets from tool args.
     3	 *
     4	 * Uses WorkspacePathResolver.check() for proper path resolution and
     5	 * workspace safety validation. Returns classification + targets.
     6	 *
     7	 * Classifications:
     8	 * - "known-write":   targets were successfully identified
     9	 * - "unknown-write": tool is mutates=true but targets cannot be determined (fail closed)
    10	 * - "no-write":      tool does not mutate files (read-only shell commands, etc.)
    11	 */
    12	
    13	import type { WorkspacePathResolver } from "../../runtime-state/runtime/workspace-path.js";
    14	
    15	// Shell commands known to be read-only (no file mutation)
    16	// Only truly read-only commands belong here. Tools that can write
    17	// files (git, npm, npx, node, tsc, etc.) are intentionally excluded
    18	// so they go through ownership enforcement.
    19	const READ_ONLY_COMMANDS = new Set([
    20	  "ls", "cat", "head", "tail", "grep", "find", "echo", "pwd", "which",
    21	]);
    22	
    23	export type MutationClassification = "known-write" | "unknown-write" | "no-write";
    24	
    25	export type MutationTarget = {
    26	  /** The resolved, absolute path */
    27	  path: string;
    28	  /** How this path was found in the args */
    29	  origin: "single" | "source" | "destination" | "header" | "shell" | "glob";
    30	  /** Whether we're confident this is a write target */
    31	  confident: boolean;
    32	};
    33	
    34	export type MutationExtraction = {
    35	  classification: MutationClassification;
    36	  targets: MutationTarget[];
    37	};
    38	
    39	/**
    40	 * Extract all file mutation targets from tool arguments.
    41	 */
    42	export function extractMutationTargets(
    43	  toolName: string,
    44	  args: Record<string, unknown>,
    45	  resolver: WorkspacePathResolver,
    46	): MutationExtraction {
    47	  const targets: MutationTarget[] = [];
    48	
    49	  switch (toolName) {
    50	    case "file.create":
    51	    case "file.delete": {
    52	      const path = asString(args.path);
    53	      if (path) {
    54	        const resolved = resolver.check(path);
    55	        if (resolved.insideWorkspace && !resolved.sensitive && !resolved.protected) {
    56	          targets.push({ path: resolved.absolute, origin: "single", confident: true });
    57	        }
    58	      }
    59	      if (targets.length === 0) return { classification: "unknown-write", targets: [] };
    60	      return { classification: "known-write", targets };
    61	    }
    62	
    63	    case "file.rename":
    64	    case "file.copy": {
    65	      const source = asString(args.source);
    66	      const dest = asString(args.destination);
    67	      // Both source and dest are required for rename/copy
    68	      if (!source || !dest) return { classification: "unknown-write", targets: [] };
    69	      const sResolved = resolver.check(source);
    70	      const dResolved = resolver.check(dest);
    71	      if (
    72	        !sResolved.insideWorkspace || sResolved.sensitive || sResolved.protected ||
    73	        !dResolved.insideWorkspace || dResolved.sensitive || dResolved.protected
    74	      ) {
    75	        return { classification: "unknown-write", targets: [] };
    76	      }
    77	      targets.push({ path: sResolved.absolute, origin: "source", confident: true });
    78	      targets.push({ path: dResolved.absolute, origin: "destination", confident: true });
    79	      return { classification: "known-write", targets };
    80	    }
    81	
    82	    case "patch.apply": {
    83	      // Real patch tool args: root, format, patchText
    84	      const patchText = asString(args.patchText);
    85	      const root = asString(args.root);
    86	      if (patchText && root) {
    87	        const headerPaths = extractPatchPaths(patchText, resolver, root);
    88	        targets.push(...headerPaths);
    89	      }
    90	      if (targets.length === 0) return { classification: "unknown-write", targets: [] };
    91	      return { classification: "known-write", targets };
    92	    }
    93	
    94	    case "shell.run": {
    95	      const command = asString(args.command);
    96	      if (!command) return { classification: "unknown-write", targets: [] };
    97	
    98	      // Known read-only commands -> no-write
    99	      const cmdName = command.trim().split(/\s+/)[0] ?? "";
   100	      if (READ_ONLY_COMMANDS.has(cmdName)) {
   101	        return { classification: "no-write", targets: [] };
   102	      }
   103	
   104	      // For M0.75: unknown shell commands are unknown-write.
   105	      // Future: integrate full shell command path extraction.
   106	      return { classification: "unknown-write", targets: [] };
   107	    }
   108	
   109	    default: {
   110	      // Generic tool: try known path fields
   111	      const path = asString(args.path);
   112	      if (path) {
   113	        const resolved = resolver.check(path);
   114	        if (resolved.insideWorkspace) {
   115	          targets.push({ path: resolved.absolute, origin: "single", confident: false });
   116	        }
   117	      }
   118	      const root = asString(args.root);
   119	      if (root) {
   120	        const resolved = resolver.check(root);
   121	        if (resolved.insideWorkspace) {
   122	          targets.push({ path: resolved.absolute, origin: "glob", confident: false });
   123	        }
   124	      }
   125	      return { classification: targets.length > 0 ? "known-write" : "unknown-write", targets };
   126	    }
   127	  }
   128	}
   129	
   130	/** Extract file paths from unified diff patch headers. */
   131	function extractPatchPaths(
   132	  patchText: string,
   133	  resolver: WorkspacePathResolver,
   134	  _root: string,
   135	): MutationTarget[] {
   136	  const targets: MutationTarget[] = [];
   137	  // Match unified diff headers: --- a/path  and  +++ b/path
   138	  const headerRe = /^[+-]{3}\s+(?:[ab]\/)?(.+)$/gm;
   139	  const seen = new Set<string>();
   140	  let match;
   141	  while ((match = headerRe.exec(patchText)) !== null) {
   142	    const rawPath = match[1].trim();
   143	    if (!rawPath || seen.has(rawPath)) continue;
   144	    seen.add(rawPath);
   145	    const resolved = resolver.check(rawPath);
   146	    if (resolved.insideWorkspace) {
   147	      targets.push({ path: resolved.absolute, origin: "header", confident: true });
   148	    }
   149	  }
   150	  return targets;
   151	}
   152	
   153	function asString(v: unknown): string | undefined {
   154	  if (typeof v === "string") return v;
   155	  if (typeof v === "number") return String(v);
   156	  return undefined;
   157	}

    60	  /**
    61	   * Evaluate one execution request through the full authorization pipeline.
    62	   *
    63	   * Pipeline:
    64	   *   1. Policy evaluation—delegate to PolicyGate
    65	   *   2. Approval lifecycle - delegated to PolicyGate handleAskDecision()
    66	   *   3. Ownership gate—verify mutation targets are covered
    67	   *   4. Audit emission—one canonical record
    68	   */
    69	  async evaluate(request: ExecutionDecisionRequest): Promise<ExecutionDecision> {
    70	    const { policyGate, ownershipGateConfig, auditStore, eventLog } = this.deps;
    71	    const agentId = request.agentId ?? "alix";
    72	
    73	    // ── Step 1: Trusted coordination identity ───────────────────
    74	    // A coordination worker's identity is minted by the scheduler. A malformed
    75	    // or partial identity is denied here so it can never degrade to the legacy
    76	    // (non-coordination) approval path and produce an unmatchable binding.
    77	    const coordinationClass = classifyCoordinationIdentity(request.coordination);
    78	    if (coordinationClass === "invalid") {
    79	      const finalDecision = decisionDenied(
    80	        "Malformed coordination execution identity",
    81	        { policyRuleId: "coordination-identity-invalid" },
    82	      );
    83	      await this.emitAudit(auditStore, eventLog, request, finalDecision, {});
    84	      return finalDecision;
    85	    }
    86	    const coordination = coordinationClass === "valid" ? request.coordination : undefined;
    87	
    88	    // ── Step 2: Policy evaluation ───────────────────────────────
    89	    const policyDecision = request.toolName
    90	      ? await policyGate.evaluateToolCall({
    91	          requestId: request.requestId,
    92	          toolName: request.toolName,
    93	          capability: request.capability,
    94	          args: request.args ?? {},
    95	          cwd: request.cwd,
    96	          sessionMode: request.sessionMode,
    97	          ownedPaths: request.ownedPaths,
    98	          sessionId: request.sessionId,
    99	          agentId: request.agentId,
   100	          source: request.source === "agent" ? "tool" : request.source,
   101	          ...(coordination ? {
   102	            coordinationRunId: coordination.coordinationRunId,
   103	            workerId: coordination.workerId,
   104	            workerAttempt: coordination.workerAttempt,
   105	            ownershipClaims: coordination.ownershipClaims,
   106	            requestFingerprint: coordination.requestFingerprint,
   107	          } : {}),
   108	        })
   109	      : await policyGate.evaluateCapability({
   110	          requestId: request.requestId,
   111	          capability: request.capability,
   112	          sessionMode: request.sessionMode,
   113	          nodeId: request.nodeId,
   114	          graphId: request.graphId,
   115	          sessionId: request.sessionId,
   116	          agentId: request.agentId,
   117	          source: request.source === "agent" ? "tool" : request.source,
   118	          ...(coordination ? {
   119	            coordinationRunId: coordination.coordinationRunId,
   120	            workerId: coordination.workerId,
   121	            workerAttempt: coordination.workerAttempt,
   122	            ownershipClaims: coordination.ownershipClaims,
   123	            requestFingerprint: coordination.requestFingerprint,
   124	          } : {}),
   125	        });
   126	
   127	    // Short-circuit deny
   128	    if (policyDecision.decision === "deny") {
   129	      const finalDecision = decisionDenied(policyDecision.reason, {
   130	        policyRuleId: policyDecision.matchedRuleId,
   131	      });
   132	      await this.emitAudit(auditStore, eventLog, request, finalDecision, { policyDecision });
   133	      return finalDecision;
   134	    }
   135	
   136	    // ── Step 3: Approval lifecycle ───────────────────────────────
   137	    if (policyDecision.decision === "ask") {
   138	      // approval_required — return the approvalId and reason from PolicyGate
   139	      const finalDecision = decisionApprovalRequired(
   140	        policyDecision.approvalId ?? "unknown",
   141	        policyDecision.reason,
   142	        { policyRuleId: policyDecision.matchedRuleId, bindingKey: policyDecision.bindingKey, requestFingerprint: policyDecision.requestFingerprint },
   143	      );
   144	      await this.emitAudit(auditStore, eventLog, request, finalDecision, { policyDecision });
   145	      return finalDecision;
   146	    }
   147	
   148	    // ── Step 4: Ownership gate ───────────────────────────────────
   149	    // Determines mutability from the tool registry's authoritative `mutates` flag,
   150	    // covering any tool registered as mutating (including MCP, custom tools, etc.).
   151	    if (ownershipGateConfig && request.toolName && request.args && this.deps.toolRegistry) {
   152	      const cap = this.deps.toolRegistry.lookupByName(request.toolName);
   153	      const mutatesCap = cap?.mutates ?? false;
   154	      if (mutatesCap) {
   155	        const ownershipResult = await checkOwnershipGate(
   156	          ownershipGateConfig,
   157	          agentId,
   158	          request.toolName,
   159	          request.args,
   160	          true, // mutates
   161	        );
   162	        if (ownershipResult !== null) {
   163	          const errMsg = ownershipResult.kind === "error" ? ownershipResult.message : "Ownership check failed";
   164	          const finalDecision = decisionDenied(
   165	            `Ownership check failed: ${errMsg}`,
   166	            { policyRuleId: "ownership-gate" },
   167	          );
   168	          await this.emitAudit(auditStore, eventLog, request, finalDecision, { policyDecision, ownershipResult });
   169	          return finalDecision;
   170	        }
   171	      }
   172	    }
   173	
   174	    // ── Step 5: Allowed ─────────────────────────────────────────
   175	    const finalDecision = decisionAllowed({
   176	      policyRuleId: policyDecision.matchedRuleId,
   177	      approvalId: policyDecision.approvalId,
   178	      approvalConsumed: policyDecision.approvalConsumed,
   179	    });
   180	    await this.emitAudit(auditStore, eventLog, request, finalDecision, { policyDecision });
   181	    return finalDecision;
   182	  }

   184	  private async emitAudit(
   185	    auditStore: AuditStore | undefined,
   186	    eventLog: EventLog | undefined,
   187	    request: ExecutionDecisionRequest,
   188	    decision: ExecutionDecision,
   189	    _extras: { policyDecision?: unknown; ownershipResult?: unknown },
   190	  ): Promise<void> {
   191	    // Narrow the discriminated union for field access — no `as any` casts
   192	    let reason: string | undefined;
   193	    let policyRuleId: string | undefined;
   194	    let approvalId: string | undefined;
   195	    switch (decision.status) {
   196	      case "allowed":
   197	        policyRuleId = decision.policyRuleId;
   198	        approvalId = decision.approvalId;

   200	      case "denied":
   201	        reason = decision.reason;
   202	        policyRuleId = decision.policyRuleId;
   203	        approvalId = decision.approvalId;
   204	        break;
   205	      case "approval_required":
   206	        approvalId = decision.approvalId;
   207	        reason = decision.reason;
   208	        policyRuleId = decision.policyRuleId;
   209	        break;
   210	    }
   211	    const action = `authorization.${decision.status}` as "authorization.allowed" | "authorization.denied" | "authorization.approval_required";
   212	
   213	    const auditPromise = auditStore?.append({
   214	      action,
   215	      actor: "system",
   216	      details: {
   217	        requestId: request.requestId,
   218	        capability: request.capability,
   219	        toolName: request.toolName,
   220	        agentId: request.agentId,
   221	        source: request.source,
   222	        sessionId: request.sessionId,
   223	        decision: decision.status,
   224	        reason,
   225	        policyRuleId,
