   546	  async evaluateCapability(request: CapabilityPolicyRequest): Promise<PolicyGateDecision> {
   547	    const policyRevision = computePolicyRevision(this.config);
   548	
   549	    const toolDecision = this.config.permissions.tools?.[request.capability];
   550	
   551	    if (toolDecision) {
   552	      const effective = applySessionMode(toolDecision, request.sessionMode);
   553	      if (effective === "allow") {
   554	        return { requestId: request.requestId, capability: request.capability, decision: "allow", reason: `Allowed by tool policy (mode: ${request.sessionMode})`, matchedRuleId: `tool-policy-${request.capability}`, policyRevision };
   555	      }
   556	      if (effective === "deny") {
   557	        return { requestId: request.requestId, capability: request.capability, decision: "deny", reason: `Denied by tool policy (mode: ${request.sessionMode})`, matchedRuleId: `tool-policy-${request.capability}`, policyRevision };
   558	      }
   559	    }
   560	
   561	    const defaultDecision = applySessionMode(this.config.permissions.default ?? "ask", request.sessionMode);
   562	    if (defaultDecision === "allow") {
   563	      return { requestId: request.requestId, capability: request.capability, decision: "allow", reason: "Allowed by default policy", matchedRuleId: "default-policy", policyRevision };
   564	    }
   565	    if (defaultDecision === "deny") {
   566	      return { requestId: request.requestId, capability: request.capability, decision: "deny", reason: "Denied by default policy", matchedRuleId: "default-policy", policyRevision };
   567	    }
   568	
   569	    // Pending-approval reuse (#687): consecutive capability asks for the same
   570	    // capability must share one pending approval instead of duplicating it —
   571	    // the same reuse the tool path gets via RuntimeGate. Scoped to
   572	    // non-coordination asks only: coordination asks carry an exact binding key
   573	    // and reuse through handleAskDecision, where a capability-wide match
   574	    // would wrongly merge distinct bindings.
   575	    let capAskDecision: PolicyGateDecision;
   576	    const existingPending = !request.coordinationRunId
   577	      ? this.deps.approvalStore?.findPending({ capability: request.capability })
   578	      : undefined;
   579	    if (existingPending) {
   580	      capAskDecision = {
   581	        requestId: request.requestId,
   582	        capability: request.capability,
   583	        decision: "ask",
   584	        reason: `Pending approval: ${existingPending.id}`,
   585	        approvalId: existingPending.id,
   586	        matchedRuleId: "pending-approval",
   587	        policyRevision,
   588	      };
   589	    } else {
   590	      capAskDecision = await this.handleAskDecision(
   591	        request.requestId,
   592	        request.capability,
   593	        request.sessionMode,
   594	        `Requires approval for capability: ${request.capability}`,
   595	        request.sessionId,
   596	        request.agentId,
   597	        request.coordinationRunId ? {
   598	          coordinationRunId: request.coordinationRunId,
   599	          workerId: request.workerId,
   600	          workerAttempt: request.workerAttempt,
   601	          ownershipClaims: request.ownershipClaims,
   602	          requestFingerprint: request.requestFingerprint,
   603	        } : undefined,
   604	      );
   605	    }
   716	    // Tool-level authorization boundary for an ISOLATED worker process.
   717	    //
   718	    // A subagent runs as its own OS process, so it cannot receive the parent's
   719	    // in-memory ApprovalStore. It therefore opens its own instance against the
   720	    // SAME authoritative workspace (`projectRoot` is the cwd the parent spawned
   721	    // us in — never a guessed or config-derived path), and recognises itself
   722	    // through a RESTRICTED port that can request, observe and consume approvals
   723	    // but cannot record a decision. That is deliberate: without the port a
   724	    // worker could call `resolve()` on its own request and grant itself any
   725	    // capability.
   726	    //
   727	    // Fail closed: if the ledger cannot be opened or loaded, no port is wired
   728	    // and gated tool calls stay denied exactly as before — an inaccessible
   729	    // approval store must never become implicit permission.
   730	    let approvalPort: WorkerApprovalPort | undefined;
   731	    try {
   732	      const { openWorkerApprovalPort } = await import("../governance/approvals/worker-approval-port.js");
   733	      approvalPort = await openWorkerApprovalPort(projectRoot, {
   734	        eventLog, workerId: taskId, workerAttempt: coordinationRunId ? workerAttempt : undefined,
   735	      });
   736	    } catch (err) {
   737	      // Readable, actionable evidence — never a silent downgrade.
   738	      try {
   739	        await eventLog.append({
   740	          actor: "subagent",
   741	          type: "subagent.approval_store_unavailable",
   742	          sessionId,
   743	          payload: { error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) },
   744	        });
   745	      } catch { /* telemetry is best-effort; the denial below is the contract */ }
   746	      approvalPort = undefined;
   747	    }
   748	
   749	    const executor = createToolExecutor({
   750	      config,
   751	      log: eventLog,
   752	      root: projectRoot,
   753	      mcpManager: mcpManager ?? undefined,
   754	      editFormatPolicy: buildEditFormatPolicy({ provider: effectiveProvider, preferred: provider.editFormatPreference }),
   755	      ownedPaths: mode === "write" ? ownedPaths : undefined,
   756	      // Without a resolver the executor's owned-scope checks are INERT: it
   757	      // constructs a private resolver but never assigns it, so
   758	      // `this.workspacePathResolver` stays undefined and the declared scope is
   759	      // silently unenforced on the continuation and ownership paths. Supplying
   760	      // it here is what makes `ownedPaths` actually mean something in a worker.
   761	      workspacePathResolver: new WorkspacePathResolver(
   762	        projectRoot,
   763	        config.permissions?.protectedPaths ?? [],
   764	      ),
   765	      // The port is passed as-is: `createToolExecutor` takes `approvalStore:
   766	      // unknown` and the facade enforces the narrowing at runtime by throwing if
   767	      // a decision method ever becomes reachable. The earlier `as never` cast
   768	      // suppressed type checking for no benefit and implied the port needed
   769	      // widening, which is the opposite of its purpose.
   770	      ...(approvalPort ? { approvalStore: approvalPort } : {}),
   771	      ...(coordinationRunId && workerAttempt !== undefined ? {
   772	        coordinationContext: {
   773	          coordinationRunId, workerId: taskId, workerAttempt,
   774	          ownershipClaims: coordinationOwnershipClaims,
   775	        },
   776	      } : {}),

     1	/**
     2	 * source-scanners.ts — the source-text scanners `pre-r032-non-bypass` asserts on.
     3	 *
     4	 * WHY THIS IS A MODULE
     5	 *
     6	 * The first version of those tests asserted a clean result while being unable to
     7	 * produce a dirty one: `offenders` was declared and never populated, and the
     8	 * "would this catch a bad input?" cases re-implemented the regex inline next to
     9	 * the real one. That is the worst shape for a guard test — the copy passes while
    10	 * the scanner drifts, so the test proves the copy works, not the guard.
    11	 *
    12	 * Keeping the scan here means the test calls the SAME function the assertions
    13	 * use, so exercising the failure path is exercising the real path.
    14	 */
    15	
    16	import { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
    17	import { join } from "node:path";
    18	
    19	/** Files under `root` whose content reads an eligibility/promotion record AND decides. */
    20	export function scanEligibilityWidening(root: string): string[] {
    21	  const offenders: string[] = [];
    22	  for (const file of walkTypeScript(root)) {
    23	    const body = readFileSync(file, "utf-8");
    24	    if (eligibilityWideningPattern(body)) offenders.push(file);
    25	  }
    26	  return offenders;
    27	}
    28	
    29	/**
    30	 * The pattern itself, exported so a test can prove it matches.
    31	 *
    32	 * Requires BOTH an eligibility reference and decision logic: a file that merely
    33	 * mentions eligibility is not the bypass this guard exists for.
    34	 */
    35	export function eligibilityWideningPattern(body: string): boolean {
    36	  return /eligibility/i.test(body) && /decision/i.test(body);
    37	}
    38	
    39	/** Count `status = "consumed"` assignments — the single-writer invariant. */
    40	export function countConsumedWriters(source: string): number {
    41	  return (source.match(/\.status\s*=\s*"consumed"/g) ?? []).length;
    42	}
    43	
    44	/**
    45	 * Guards that must each be present, independently, in the approval store.
    46	 *
    47	 * Removing any one would let a stale or foreign approval authorize an
    48	 * invocation, so the check is per-guard and not a single combined test.
    49	 */
    50	export const REQUIRED_APPROVAL_GUARDS: readonly RegExp[] = [
    51	  /status !== "approved"/,
    52	  /approvalExpiryState\(r\.expiresAt, now\)/,
    53	  /expiryState === "invalid"/,
    54	  /expiryState === "expired"/,
    55	  /bindingKey !== expectedBindingKey/,
    56	  /invocationMatches/,
    57	];
    58	
    59	/** Which required guards are absent from `source`. Empty = all present. */
    60	export function missingApprovalGuards(source: string): string[] {
    61	  return REQUIRED_APPROVAL_GUARDS.filter((guard) => !guard.test(source)).map(String);
    62	}
    63	
    64	function walkTypeScript(dir: string): string[] {
    65	  const out: string[] = [];
    66	  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir)) {
    67	    const full = join(dir, entry);
    68	    if (statSync(full).isDirectory()) out.push(...walkTypeScript(full));
    69	    else if (full.endsWith(".ts")) out.push(full);
    70	  }
    71	  return out;
    72	}

    18	async function checkpoint(name: string): Promise<void> {
    19	  if (point !== name) return;
    20	  process.send!({ checkpoint: name, pid: process.pid });
    21	  setInterval(() => {}, 1000);
    22	  await new Promise<never>(() => {});
    23	}

    25	const updateRun = CoordinationStore.prototype.updateRun;
    26	let parkedRecovery = false;
    27	CoordinationStore.prototype.updateRun = async function (...args) {
    28	  if (point === 'recover-before-lock' && !parkedRecovery) {
    29	    parkedRecovery = true;
    30	    await new Promise<void>(resolve => {
    31	      process.once('message', () => resolve());
    32	      process.send!({ checkpoint: 'recover-before-lock', pid: process.pid });
    33	    });
    34	  }
    35	  return updateRun.apply(this, args);
    36	};

    40	  await remove.apply(this, args);

    44	ApprovalStore.prototype.consumeApproved = async function (...args) {
    45	  const result = await consume.apply(this, args);
    46	  if (result.consumed) await checkpoint('after-consume');
    47	  return result;
    48	};

    54	  const result = await execute.apply(this, args);
    55	  if (result.kind !== 'success') throw new Error(`Real file router failed: ${JSON.stringify(result)}`);
    56	  await checkpoint('after-effect');
    57	  return result;
    58	};
    59	const outcome = ApprovalStore.prototype.recordExecutionOutcome;
    60	ApprovalStore.prototype.recordExecutionOutcome = async function (...args) {
    61	  const result = await outcome.apply(this, args);
    62	  if (result && args[1] === 'succeeded') await checkpoint('after-receipt');
    63	  return result;
    64	};

    11	function request(effect: string): ToolCallRequest {
    12	  return { toolCallId: 'sigkill', name: 'shell.run', args: { command: `printf applied > ${JSON.stringify(effect)}` } };
    13	}

    15	function runCrashChild(cwd: string, effect: string): Promise<{ code: number | null; signal: NodeJS.Signals | null }> {
    16	  const moduleUrl = new URL('../../src/capabilities/tools/effect-journal.js', import.meta.url).href;
    17	  const code = `
    18	    import { writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
    19	    import { executeWithEffectJournal } from ${JSON.stringify(moduleUrl)};
    20	    const [cwd,effect] = process.argv.slice(1);
    21	    const request = { toolCallId:'child', name:'shell.run', args:{ command:'printf applied > '+JSON.stringify(effect) } };
    22	    await executeWithEffectJournal(cwd, request, async () => { await writeFile(effect, 'applied'); return {kind:'success',output:'ok'}; }, {
    23	      onPoint(point) { if (point === 'after_adapter') process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGKILL'); }
    24	    });
    25	  `;
    26	  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    27	    const child = spawn(process.execPath, ['--input-type=module', '-e', code, cwd, effect], { stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'] });
    28	    let stderr = '';
    29	    child.stderr.on('data', (d) => { stderr += d; });
    30	    child.on('error', reject);
    31	    child.on('close', (exitCode, signal) => {
    32	      if (exitCode !== null && exitCode !== 0) reject(new Error(`child exit ${exitCode}: ${stderr}`));
    33	      else resolve({ code: exitCode, signal });
    34	    });
    35	  });
    36	}

     1	/**
     2	 * gate-e-qualification-record.test.mjs — pins the Gate E qualification contract.
     3	 *
     4	 * Gate E has never had a record to check, so the failure modes worth pinning are
     5	 * the ones that would let a record *look* complete:
     6	 *   - four of five clauses recorded, read as "nearly done"
     7	 *   - a test file counted as a qualified control
     8	 *   - a clause with no negative case, i.e. a positive assertion standing in for
     9	 *     the regression the control exists to prevent
    10	 *   - declared gaps quietly omitted rather than declared
    11	 *   - author-only coverage labelled as qualification, dropping "independently"
    12	 *
    13	 * The last one is the whole gate. `QUALIFIED-AUTHOR-ONLY` exists so the honest
    14	 * ceiling has a name and cannot be rounded up.
    15	 */

     1	/**
     2	 * capability-map.ts -- Tool → capability mapping.
     3	 *
     4	 * Two responsibilities:
     5	 *
     6	 *  1. `legacyCapabilityToCanonical` — the centralized canonicalizer for
     7	 *     config-facing policy keys. This is the ONLY place legacy policy keys are
     8	 *     canonicalized to capability ids, including keys no current tool produces
     9	 *     (git.commit → repo.write, shell.readonly → shell.exec, ...). KEEP AS-IS.
    10	 *
    11	 *  2. Port-derived tool → capability views (`inferCapability`,
    12	 *     `canonicalCapabilityOf`) and capability predicates
    13	 *     (`isReadonlyCapability`, `requiresApproval`). These are DERIVED from the
    14	 *     canonical `ToolCapabilityRegistry` port — never independently maintained.
    15	 *     The single `mcp.*` registry wildcard entry
    16	 *     covers the dynamic `mcp.<server>.<tool>` family: any tool name beginning
    17	 *     with "mcp." maps to the `mcp.invoke` capability.
    18	 */
    19	
    20	import { createToolCapabilityRegistry } from "./tool-registry.js";
    21	import type {
    22	  ToolCapabilityEntry,
    23	  ToolCapabilityRegistry,
    24	} from "../../runtime-state/contracts/tool-capability-registry.js";
    25	
    26	const LEGACY_TO_CANONICAL: Record<string, string> = {
    27	  "file.read": "filesystem.read",
    28	  "file.write": "filesystem.write",
    29	  "file.search": "filesystem.search",
    30	  "file.delete": "filesystem.write",
    31	  "shell.run": "shell.exec",
    32	  "shell.readonly": "shell.exec",
    33	  "git.diff": "repo.read",
    34	  "git.commit": "repo.write",
    35	  "git.push": "repo.write",
    36	  "network.fetch": "network.fetch",
    37	  "secret.read": "secret.read",
    38	  "browser.open": "browser.open",
    39	  "patch.apply": "patch.apply",
    40	  "delegate": "agent.delegate",
    41	  "task.complete": "task.complete",
    42	  "web.search": "web.search",
    43	  "web.fetch": "web.fetch",
    44	  "mcp.invoke": "mcp.invoke",
    45	  "tool.invoke": "tool.invoke",
    46	  "verify.claim": "decision.claim-verification",
    47	};
    48	
    49	export function legacyCapabilityToCanonical(legacy: string): string {
    50	  return LEGACY_TO_CANONICAL[legacy] ?? legacy;
    51	}
    52	
    53	const capabilityCatalog = createToolCapabilityRegistry();
    54	
    55	/**
    56	 * Resolve an executor name through the canonical catalogue, including the
    57	 * dynamic MCP family. A dynamic `mcp.<server>.<tool>` name intentionally has
    58	 * no static registry row: it resolves through the port's single `mcp.*`
    59	 * entry, so the dynamic surface cannot carry a second policy vocabulary.
    60	 */
    61	export function resolveCataloguedExecutor(
    62	  catalog: ToolCapabilityRegistry,
    63	  executorName: string,
    64	): ToolCapabilityEntry | undefined {
    65	  if (executorName.startsWith("mcp.")) return catalog.resolve("mcp.*");
    66	  return catalog.resolve(executorName);
    67	}
    68	
    69	/** Fallback vocabulary when the catalogue has no row (never a second taxonomy). */
    70	function uncataloguedFallback(toolName: string): string {
    71	  return toolName.startsWith("mcp.") ? "mcp.invoke" : "tool.invoke";
    72	}
    73	
    74	/**
    75	 * Map a tool name to its config-facing policy key.
    76	 *
    77	 * Exactly reproduces the historical executor/policy-gate `inferCapability`
    78	 * behavior: `mcp.<...>` → `"mcp.invoke"`; a known registry tool → its
    79	 * `policyKey`; otherwise `"tool.invoke"`.
    80	 */
    81	export function inferCapability(toolName: string): string {
    82	  return resolveCataloguedExecutor(capabilityCatalog, toolName)?.policyKey
    83	    ?? uncataloguedFallback(toolName);
    84	}
    85	
    86	/**
    87	 * Map a tool name to its canonical capability id.
    88	 *
    89	 * `mcp.<...>` → `"mcp.invoke"`; a known registry tool → its `capabilityId`;
    90	 * otherwise `"tool.invoke"`. This replaces the
    91	 * `legacyCapabilityToCanonical(inferCapability(name))` composition at call
    92	 * sites (the canonicalizer is for config keys, not tool names).
    93	 */
    94	export function canonicalCapabilityOf(toolName: string): string {
    95	  return resolveCataloguedExecutor(capabilityCatalog, toolName)?.capabilityId
    96	    ?? uncataloguedFallback(toolName);
    97	}
    98	
    99	/** True when no tool for the capability mutates state (registry-derived). */
   100	export function isReadonlyCapability(capabilityId: string): boolean {
   101	  return !capabilityCatalog.list().some(t => t.capabilityId === capabilityId && t.mutates);
   102	}
   103	
   104	/**
   105	 * True when every tool for the capability carries non-low risk
   106	 * (registry-derived).
   107	 *
   108	 * NOTE: signature changed from the legacy `(capability, policy)` form — the
   109	 * only consumer was the unit test, which built a `PolicyConfig`. It is now a
   110	 * pure registry predicate over the canonical taxonomy.
   111	 */
   112	export function requiresApproval(capabilityId: string): boolean {
   113	  return capabilityCatalog
   114	    .list()
   115	    .filter(t => t.capabilityId === capabilityId)
   116	    .every(t => t.risk !== "low");
   117	}

     8	import { test } from 'node:test';
     9	import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
    10	import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';

    16	
    17	const childScript = fileURLToPath(new URL('../fixtures/d9-approval-lock-child.js', import.meta.url));
    18	const LOCK_DIR = ['.alix', 'approvals', 'approvals.lock'];
    19	const metaPath = (cwd: string) => join(cwd, ...LOCK_DIR, 'meta.json');
    20	
    21	type Message = { event: string; pid: number; acquired?: boolean };
    22	
    23	function host(cwd: string, mode: string, budget?: number, backend?: 'flock' | 'mkdir') {
    24	  const child = spawn(process.execPath, [childScript, cwd, mode, String(budget ?? ''), backend ?? ''], {
    25	    cwd, env: { PATH: process.env.PATH, HOME: cwd }, stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe', 'ipc'],
    26	  });
    27	  const messages: Message[] = [];
    28	  let output = '';
    29	  child.stdout!.on('data', d => { output += String(d); });
    30	  child.stderr!.on('data', d => { output += String(d); });
    31	  child.on('message', m => messages.push(m as Message));
    32	  const exited = new Promise<{ code: number | null; signal: NodeJS.Signals | null }>((resolve, reject) => {
    33	    child.once('error', reject);
    34	    child.once('exit', (code, signal) => resolve({ code, signal }));
    35	  });
    36	  async function wait(event: string, timeoutMs = 15_000): Promise<Message> {
    37	    const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
    38	    while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    39	      const m = messages.find(m => m.event === event);
    40	      if (m) { assert.equal(m.pid, child.pid); return m; }
    41	      if (child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null) throw new Error(`Host died before ${event}: ${output}`);
    42	      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 10));
    43	    }
    44	    throw new Error(`Host timeout at ${event}: ${output}`);
    45	  }
    46	  return { child, wait, exited,
    47	    go: () => child.send({ release: true }),
    48	    stop: () => child.kill('SIGSTOP'),
    49	    cont: () => child.kill('SIGCONT'),
    50	    kill: () => child.kill('SIGKILL') };
    51	}
    52	
    53	async function workspace() {
    54	  return mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'aplock-proc-'));
    55	}
    56	async function cleanup(cwd: string, hosts: ReturnType<typeof host>[]) {
    57	  for (const h of hosts) if (h.child.exitCode === null && h.child.signalCode === null) h.child.kill('SIGKILL');
    58	  for (const h of hosts) await h.exited.catch(() => {});
    59	  await rm(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true });
    60	}
    61	
    62	test('a paused (SIGSTOP) holder keeps its lock — a contender never steals it', { timeout: 30_000 }, async () => {
    63	  const cwd = await workspace();
    64	  const hosts: ReturnType<typeof host>[] = [];
    65	  try {
    66	    const holder = host(cwd, 'hold'); hosts.push(holder);
    67	    const held = await holder.wait('held');
    68	    assert.equal(held.acquired, true);
    69	
    70	    // Freeze the holder mid-hold. SIGSTOP does not close its fd, so the
    71	    // kernel keeps the flock. A contender must observe the lock held — never
    72	    // steal it on any timer.
    73	    holder.stop();
    74	    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 200));
    75	    const contender = new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd);
    76	    assert.equal(await contender.acquire(400), false, 'a paused live owner must not be stolen');
    77	
    78	    // Resume, release, and the lock is genuinely free.
    79	    holder.cont();
    80	    holder.go(); await holder.wait('released');
    81	    assert.equal(await contender.acquire(2_000), true);
    82	    contender.release();
    83	  } finally { await cleanup(cwd, hosts); }
    84	});
    85	
    86	test('a SIGKILLed holder releases immediately; a successor needs no stale recovery', { timeout: 30_000 }, async () => {
    87	  const cwd = await workspace();
    88	  const hosts: ReturnType<typeof host>[] = [];
    89	  try {
    90	    const holder = host(cwd, 'hold'); hosts.push(holder);
    91	    const held = await holder.wait('held');
    92	    assert.equal(held.acquired, true);
    93	
    94	    holder.kill();
    95	    assert.deepEqual(await holder.exited, { code: null, signal: 'SIGKILL' });
    96	
    97	    const started = Date.now();
    98	    const successor = new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd);
    99	    assert.equal(await successor.acquire(2_000), true, 'the OS must release the lock on SIGKILL');
   100	    assert.ok(Date.now() - started < 1_000, 'recovery must not wait for any age or reclaim step');
   101	    successor.release();
   102	  } finally { await cleanup(cwd, hosts); }
   103	});
   104	
   105	test('concurrent contenders never overlap inside the critical section', { timeout: 30_000 }, async () => {
   106	  const cwd = await workspace();
   107	  const hosts: ReturnType<typeof host>[] = [];
   108	  try {
   109	    const count = 6;
   110	    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) hosts.push(host(cwd, 'mutate'));
   111	    await Promise.all(hosts.map(h => h.wait('mutate-acquired')));
   112	    await Promise.all(hosts.map(h => h.wait('mutated')));
   113	    for (const h of hosts) assert.deepEqual(await h.exited, { code: 0, signal: null });
   114	    const value = parseInt((await readFile(join(cwd, 'counter.txt'), 'utf8')).trim(), 10);
   115	    assert.equal(value, count, 'mutual exclusion must serialize the read-modify-write');
   116	  } finally { await cleanup(cwd, hosts); }
   117	});
   118	
   119	test('a daemon restart acquires immediately with no stale-lock recovery', { timeout: 30_000 }, async () => {
   120	  const cwd = await workspace();
   121	  const hosts: ReturnType<typeof host>[] = [];
   122	  try {
   123	    // First daemon acquires and is killed without releasing.
   124	    const daemon = host(cwd, 'hold'); hosts.push(daemon);
   125	    assert.equal((await daemon.wait('held')).acquired, true);
   126	    daemon.kill();
   127	    assert.deepEqual(await daemon.exited, { code: null, signal: 'SIGKILL' });
   128	
   129	    // A restarted daemon must acquire immediately — there is no orphan lock
   130	    // state to detect, probe, or reclaim.
   131	    const restarted = host(cwd, 'hold'); hosts.push(restarted);
   132	    const held = await restarted.wait('held', 3_000);
   133	    assert.equal(held.acquired, true, 'the restarted daemon must acquire without recovery');
   134	    restarted.go(); await restarted.wait('released');
   135	  } finally { await cleanup(cwd, hosts); }
   136	});
   137	
   138	test('mkdir fallback: a dead owner is reclaimed immediately, and concurrent reclaimers never double-steal', { timeout: 30_000 }, async () => {
   139	  const cwd = await workspace();
   140	  const hosts: ReturnType<typeof host>[] = [];
   141	  try {
   142	    // Seed a stale mkdir lock: a valid, dead PID with a recent timestamp.
   143	    const lockDir = join(cwd, ...LOCK_DIR);
   144	    await mkdir(lockDir, { recursive: true });
   145	    await writeFile(join(lockDir, 'meta.json'), JSON.stringify({
   146	      pid: 2 ** 30, token: 'dead-owner', acquiredAt: new Date().toISOString(),
   147	    }));
   148	    const count = 6;
   149	    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) hosts.push(host(cwd, 'mutate', undefined, 'mkdir'));
   150	    await Promise.all(hosts.map(h => h.wait('mutate-acquired')));
   151	    await Promise.all(hosts.map(h => h.wait('mutated')));
   152	    for (const h of hosts) assert.deepEqual(await h.exited, { code: 0, signal: null });
   153	    const value = parseInt((await readFile(join(cwd, 'counter.txt'), 'utf8')).trim(), 10);
   154	    assert.equal(value, count, 'an atomic reclaim must not let two hosts both enter the critical section');
   155	  } finally { await cleanup(cwd, hosts); }
   156	});
   157	
   158	test('mkdir fallback: a metadata-less lock is never stolen by age', { timeout: 30_000 }, async () => {
   159	  const cwd = await workspace();
   160	  const hosts: ReturnType<typeof host>[] = [];
   161	  try {
   162	    const lockDir = join(cwd, ...LOCK_DIR);
   163	    await mkdir(lockDir, { recursive: true });
   164	    assert.equal(await new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd, { backend: 'mkdir' }).acquire(200), false);
   165	    const old = new Date(Date.now() - 70_000);
   166	    await utimes(lockDir, old, old);
   167	    const successor = new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd, { backend: 'mkdir' });
   168	    assert.equal(await successor.acquire(250), false, 'age cannot prove an owner is dead');
   169	    successor.release();
   170	  } finally { await cleanup(cwd, hosts); }
   171	});
     1	/**
     2	 * approval-store-lock.test.ts — In-process tests for the per-file lock.
     3	 *
     4	 * Covers the OS-managed `flock` backend (the production default) and the
     5	 * `mkdir` fallback. Real OS-process liveness and mutual-exclusion cases live
     6	 * in tests/security/approval-lock-liveness.test.ts.
     7	 */
     8	
     9	import { describe, it, beforeEach, afterEach } from "node:test";
    10	import assert from "node:assert/strict";
    11	import { mkdtempSync, rmSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, utimesSync } from "node:fs";
    12	import { join } from "node:path";
    13	import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
    14	import { ApprovalStoreLock, detectLockBackend } from "../../src/governance/approvals/approval-store-lock.js";
    15	
    16	const LOCK_DIR = [".alix", "approvals", "approvals.lock"];
    17	const STALE_LOCK_MS = 60_000;
    18	
    19	function lockPath(cwd: string): string { return join(cwd, ...LOCK_DIR); }
    20	function metaPath(cwd: string): string { return join(cwd, ...LOCK_DIR, "meta.json"); }
    21	
    22	/** Backdate a directory's mtime so its age exceeds the stale ceiling. */
    23	function backdate(lockDir: string): void {
    24	  const old = new Date(Date.now() - STALE_LOCK_MS - 5_000);
    25	  utimesSync(lockDir, old, old);
    26	}
    27	
    28	function readMeta(cwd: string): { pid: number; token: string; acquiredAt: string } {
    29	  return JSON.parse(readFileSync(metaPath(cwd), "utf-8"));
    30	}
    31	
    32	describe("ApprovalStoreLock (flock backend)", () => {
    33	  let cwd: string;
    34	  beforeEach(() => { cwd = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "aplock-flock-")); });
    35	  afterEach(() => { rmSync(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true }); });
    36	
    37	  it("is the selected backend on this platform", () => {
    38	    // The flock tests below only run meaningfully where flock is present; the
    39	    // fallback cases are covered by the mkdir describe block instead.
    40	    assert.equal(typeof detectLockBackend(), "string");
    41	  });
    42	
    43	  it("acquires and releases", async () => {
    44	    const lock = new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd);
    45	    assert.equal(await lock.acquire(500), true);
    46	    assert.equal(lock.isHeld(), true);
    47	    lock.release();
    48	    assert.equal(lock.isHeld(), false);
    49	  });
    50	
    51	  it("blocks a second acquisition while held", async () => {
    52	    const lock1 = new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd);
    53	    const lock2 = new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd);
    54	    assert.equal(await lock1.acquire(500), true);
    55	    assert.equal(await lock2.acquire(200), false);
    56	    lock1.release();
    57	    lock2.release();
    58	  });
    59	
    60	  it("acquires again after release", async () => {
    61	    const lock = new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd);
    62	    assert.equal(await lock.acquire(500), true);
    63	    lock.release();
    64	    assert.equal(await lock.acquire(500), true);
    65	    lock.release();
    66	  });
    67	
    68	  it("releasing frees the lock for a successor", async () => {
    69	    const lock1 = new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd);
    70	    assert.equal(await lock1.acquire(500), true);
    71	    lock1.release();
    72	    const lock2 = new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd);
    73	    assert.equal(await lock2.acquire(500), true);
    74	    lock2.release();
    75	  });
    76	
    77	  it("leaves no lock state that blocks a fresh instance after release", async () => {
    78	    const lock = new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd);
    79	    assert.equal(await lock.acquire(500), true);
    80	    lock.release();
    81	    // A fresh process's lock must be immediately acquirable — the OS released
    82	    // the advisory lock on release, so no stale-state recovery is needed.
    83	    const successor = new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd);
    84	    assert.equal(await successor.acquire(500), true);
    85	    successor.release();
    86	  });
    87	
    88	  it("rejects an acquired lock if its pathname was replaced while waiting", async () => {
    89	    const original = new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd);
    90	    assert.equal(await original.acquire(500), true);
    91	    const contender = new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd);
    92	    const pending = contender.acquire(450);
    93	    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 100));
    94	    rmSync(lockPath(cwd), { force: true });
    95	    writeFileSync(lockPath(cwd), "replacement", "utf8");
    96	    original.release();
    97	    assert.equal(await pending, false, "a contender on an unlinked inode must not report success");
    98	    contender.release();
    99	  });
   100	
   101	  it("locks a leftover directory from the pre-flock mkdir lock without throwing", async () => {
   102	    // A legacy mkdir-lock orphan leaves a DIRECTORY at the lock path. flock can
   103	    // lock a directory, so acquisition must succeed rather than throw EISDIR.
   104	    mkdirSync(lockPath(cwd), { recursive: true });
   105	    const lock = new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd);
   106	    assert.equal(await lock.acquire(500), true, "a legacy directory target must not break the flock lock");
   107	    lock.release();
   108	  });
   109	});
   110	
   111	describe("ApprovalStoreLock (mkdir fallback)", () => {
   112	  let cwd: string;
   113	  beforeEach(() => { cwd = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "aplock-mkdir-")); });
   114	  afterEach(() => { rmSync(cwd, { recursive: true, force: true }); });
   115	
   116	  const mkdirLock = () => new ApprovalStoreLock(cwd, { backend: "mkdir" });
   117	
   118	  it("acquires and releases", async () => {
   119	    const lock = mkdirLock();
   120	    assert.equal(await lock.acquire(500), true);
   121	    lock.release();
   122	    assert.equal(lock.isHeld(), false);
   123	  });
   124	
   125	  it("blocks second acquisition", async () => {
   126	    const lock1 = mkdirLock();
   127	    const lock2 = mkdirLock();
   128	    assert.equal(await lock1.acquire(500), true);
   129	    assert.equal(await lock2.acquire(200), false);
   130	    lock1.release();
   131	    lock2.release();
   132	  });
   133	
   134	  it("acquires again after release", async () => {
   135	    const lock = mkdirLock();
   136	    assert.equal(await lock.acquire(500), true);
   137	    lock.release();
   138	    assert.equal(await lock.acquire(500), true);
   139	    lock.release();
   140	  });
   141	
   142	  /**
   143	   * A daemon SIGKILLed inside a mutation leaves a lock directory behind with a
   144	   * valid, dead PID. A dead owner is proof enough, immediately — no age gate.
   145	   */
   146	  it("breaks a lock whose owning process is dead, without waiting for the age ceiling", async () => {
   147	    const held = mkdirLock();
   148	    assert.equal(await held.acquire(500), true);
   149	    // Simulate the owner dying: rewrite the metadata with a PID that cannot
   150	    // exist, keeping `acquiredAt` recent so only liveness can justify a break.
   151	    const meta = readMeta(cwd);
   152	    writeFileSync(metaPath(cwd), JSON.stringify({ ...meta, pid: 2 ** 30 }), "utf-8");
   153	
   154	    const started = Date.now();
   155	    const successor = mkdirLock();
   156	    assert.equal(await successor.acquire(2_000), true, "a dead owner must not hold the lock");
   157	    assert.ok(Date.now() - started < 1_000, "recovery must not wait for the age ceiling");
   158	    successor.release();
   159	  });
   160	
   161	  /**
   162	   * A live holder whose critical section outlives the stale ceiling keeps its
   163	   * lock: age alone must NEVER steal a lock whose owner is provably alive.
   164	   */
   165	  it("does not break a lock past the age ceiling while its PID is alive", async () => {
   166	    const held = mkdirLock();
   167	    assert.equal(await held.acquire(500), true);
   168	    // This process's own PID is alive; only the timestamp is aged out.
   169	    const meta = readMeta(cwd);
   170	    writeFileSync(metaPath(cwd), JSON.stringify({ ...meta, acquiredAt: new Date(Date.now() - 120_000).toISOString() }), "utf-8");
   171	    const successor = mkdirLock();
   172	    assert.equal(await successor.acquire(300), false, "a provably-alive owner must not be stolen on age alone");
   173	    held.release();
   174	    successor.release();
   175	  });
   176	
   177	  it("still respects a live owner's recent lock", async () => {
   178	    const held = mkdirLock();
   179	    assert.equal(await held.acquire(500), true);
   180	    const contender = mkdirLock();
   181	    assert.equal(await contender.acquire(200), false);
   182	    held.release();
   183	    contender.release();
   184	  });
   185	
   186	  /**
   187	   * A missing/invalid `pid` must not be an immediate theft, and age cannot
   188	   * establish owner death, so it is never reclaimed automatically.
   189	   */
   190	  for (const pid of [undefined, 0, -1, NaN] as const) {
   191	    it(`does not break a lock with an invalid pid (${String(pid)})`, async () => {
   192	      const held = mkdirLock();
   193	      assert.equal(await held.acquire(500), true);
   194	      const meta = readMeta(cwd);
   195	      writeFileSync(metaPath(cwd), JSON.stringify({ ...meta, pid }), "utf-8");
   196	      const successor = mkdirLock();
   197	      assert.equal(await successor.acquire(200), false, "an invalid pid must not be stolen");
   198	      held.release();
   199	      successor.release();
   200	    });
   201	  }
   202	
   203	  it("never steals an invalid-pid lock based on age", async () => {
   204	    const held = mkdirLock();
   205	    assert.equal(await held.acquire(500), true);
   206	    const meta = readMeta(cwd);
   207	    writeFileSync(metaPath(cwd), JSON.stringify({ token: meta.token, acquiredAt: new Date(Date.now() - 120_000).toISOString() }), "utf-8");
   208	    const successor = mkdirLock();
   209	    assert.equal(await successor.acquire(250), false, "elapsed time cannot establish that an unprovable owner died");
   210	    successor.release();
   280	});

   433	test('D10: the CLI reports failure for every HOLD, not just for invalid input', async () => {

   538	   * requestOrReusePending — Atomic lookup + insert inside a single mutate() call.
   539	   *
   540	   * If a pending approval with the same bindingKey already exists, returns it.
   541	   * Otherwise creates a new one via the same logic as requestBound.
   542	   *
   543	   * This eliminates the check-then-create race that requestBound() leaves to callers.
   544	   */
   545	  async requestOrReusePending(input: ApprovalRequestInput): Promise<ApprovalRecord> {
   546	    return this.mutate((approvals) => {
   547	      // Look for existing pending approval with the same binding key
   548	      const latest = approvals.filter(a => a.bindingKey === input.bindingKey)
   549	        .sort((a, b) => b.createdAt.localeCompare(a.createdAt) || b.id.localeCompare(a.id))[0];
   550	      const existing = latest?.status === "pending" ? latest : undefined;
   551	      if (existing) {
   552	        // The binding key is not a substitute for worker/attempt authority.
   553	        // Reject collisions rather than returning another worker's approval.
   554	        if (existing.workerId !== input.workerId || existing.workerAttempt !== input.workerAttempt ||
   555	            existing.coordinationRunId !== input.coordinationRunId || existing.sessionId !== input.sessionId) {
   556	          throw new Error("pending approval identity mismatch");
   557	        }
   558	        return { ...existing };
   559	      }

   564	        schemaVersion: "2.0",

   611	  /** Internal helper to create an approval record inside mutate(). */
   612	  private async createApprovalRecord(input: ApprovalRequestInput): Promise<ApprovalRecord> {
   865	   * approval is never reissued by this transition.
   866	   *
   867	   * Returns the record's current state so a caller can name the exact reason.
   868	   */
   869	  async markExecutionUnverified(
   870	    id: string,
   871	    scope?: ApprovalOutcomeScope,
   872	  ): Promise<"unverified" | "terminal" | "missing"> {
   873	    const trustedScope = scope === undefined ? undefined : { ...scope };
   874	    let verdict: "unverified" | "terminal" | "missing" = "missing";
   875	    let sessionId: string | undefined;
   876	    await this.mutate((approvals) => {
   877	      const r = approvals.find(a => a.id === id);
   878	      if (!r) { verdict = "missing"; return; }
   879	      if (trustedScope && !outcomeScopeMatches(r, trustedScope)) throw OUTCOME_SCOPE_DENIED;
   880	      if (r.status !== "consumed") { verdict = "terminal"; return; }
   881	      if (r.executionOutcome === "unverified") { verdict = "unverified"; return; }
   882	      if (r.executionOutcome !== "pending") { verdict = "terminal"; return; }
   883	      r.executionOutcome = "unverified";
   884	      r.executionOutcomeAt = new Date().toISOString();
   885	      sessionId = r.sessionId;
   886	      verdict = "unverified";
   887	    }).catch((error: unknown) => {
   888	      if (error !== OUTCOME_SCOPE_DENIED) throw error;
   889	    });
   890	    // `verdict` is assigned inside the mutate() closure, so TS narrows it to the
   891	    // initial literal here. Re-assert the declared union before comparing.
   892	    const finalVerdict = verdict as "unverified" | "terminal" | "missing";
   893	    if (finalVerdict === "unverified") {
   894	      this.emit(APPROVAL_EVENT_TYPES.EXECUTION_UNVERIFIED, { approvalId: id }, sessionId);
   895	    }
   896	    return finalVerdict;
   897	  }

   247	  async acquire(req: AcquireRequest): Promise<AcquireResult> {
   248	    return (await this.withLock(async () => this.acquireUnlocked(req)))
   249	      ?? { acquired: false, conflict: { reason: "Ownership state unavailable or lock acquisition timed out", conflictingRecords: [] } };
   250	  }
   251	
   252	  async acquireMany(reqs: AcquireRequest[]): Promise<AcquireResult[]> {
   253	    return (await this.withLock(async () => {
   254	      // Check against existing persisted records
   255	      for (const r of reqs) {
   256	        const c = this.findConflicts(r.agentId, r.scope, r.mode);
   257	        if (!c.allowed) {
   258	          return reqs.map(() =>
   259	            ({ acquired: false, conflict: { reason: `Batch conflict: ${c.reason}`, conflictingRecords: c.conflictingRecords } }));
   260	        }
   261	      }
   262	      // Check intra-batch conflicts (same batch, different agents, overlapping scopes)
   263	      for (let i = 0; i < reqs.length; i++) {
   264	        for (let j = i + 1; j < reqs.length; j++) {
   265	          if (
   266	            reqs[i].agentId !== reqs[j].agentId &&
   267	            this.scopesOverlap(reqs[i].scope, reqs[j].scope) &&
   268	            modesConflict(reqs[i].mode, reqs[j].mode)
   269	          ) {
   270	            return reqs.map(() =>
   271	              ({ acquired: false, conflict: { reason: "Intra-batch conflict", conflictingRecords: [] } }));
   272	          }
   273	        }
   274	      }
   275	      return reqs.map(r => this.acquireUnlocked(r));
   276	    })) ?? reqs.map(() => ({ acquired: false, conflict: { reason: "Ownership state unavailable or lock acquisition timed out", conflictingRecords: [] } }));
   277	  }

DEFECTS

1. MAJOR — Child-process approval authority remains reachable.
src/governance/approvals/worker-approval-port.ts:119; src/agents/subagent-manager.ts:368; src/interfaces/cli/commands/approval.ts:55 and :110.
A child executing JavaScript can construct ApprovalStore(workspace), load it, and call resolve, revoke, or public mutate. The CLI similarly exposes approve/deny/revoke without authenticating a distinct worker principal. Environment filtering does not remove same-user filesystem authority. No singleton or passed full-store reference is needed.
Minimal fix: place decision authority behind authenticated parent-owned IPC/storage permissions inaccessible to workers, or explicitly narrow F8b to cooperative use of the facade. The latter does not satisfy the question’s unrestricted child-process claim.

2. MAJOR — Owned/protected-path checks do not constrain canonical destinations.
src/coordination/ownership/path-scope.ts:207–209; src/runtime-state/runtime/workspace-path.ts:39–54 and :112–124; src/capabilities/tools/tool-router.ts:118–128, :205 and :218.
Counterexample: ownedPaths=["owned/**"], with an existing directory symlink owned/link pointing to ../unowned. Creating owned/link/new.txt passes lexical ownership. Canonical workspace containment also passes because unowned remains inside the workspace. Node follows the parent symlink and creates unowned/new.txt.
An alias into an in-workspace protected directory similarly avoids lexical protection matching. The final-component symlink test does not cover this.
Minimal fix: enforce ownership and protection against canonical destinations, including existing ancestors of new files. Use a race-resistant write mechanism or reject symlink traversal.

3. MAJOR — Validator still manufactures independent qualification from unsupported claims.
benchmark/evidence/gate-e-qualification-record.mjs:102, :143–149, :166–176, :219, :233, :317 and :337–340.
Executed read-only probe: supplied an all-zero nonexistent commit, runner “IMAGINARY”, command “echo tests/policy/rule-evaluator.test.ts”, fabricated 999999/999999 counts, “x” negative cases, and rule-evaluator.ts as every clause’s evidence. Retained the existing qualifier reference to the previous rejecting review.
Result: ok:true, QUALIFIED-INDEPENDENT for both model-independent and declared-independent.
The validator checks command substrings, file existence/extensions, supplied arithmetic, and whether review text contains an identity. It does not verify execution, assertion semantics, review verdict, reviewed artifact, or independent authority.
Minimal fix: bind qualification to commit/build-bound execution receipts and an independently controlled review verdict covering those clauses and that artifact. Until then, describe this as structural record validation, not semantic qualification.

4. MAJOR — Execution logs are locally present but absent from the committed evidence set.
.gitignore:15; docs/prd/evidence/lean-01/D9-phase-f-req1-x86-64-qualification-2026-11-02.md:7; evidence/d9-x86-64-2026-11-02/SHA256SUMS:2–14.
git ls-files lists only RESULT.txt, SHA256SUMS and environment.txt in that directory. The 13 logs are ignored. Hashes cannot reconstruct missing files; a fresh checkout cannot inspect the claimed executions.
Minimal fix: retain the logs as tracked evidence or in an immutable, explicitly referenced archive.

5. MAJOR — Invalid policy can remove deny authority.
src/governance/policy/policy-loader.ts:43–45, :54–59.
An invalid deny rule/file is skipped; surviving permissive rules remain, or defaults replace the failed policy set.
Minimal fix: distinguish initial absence from malformed/unreadable configured authority and fail closed on the latter. Add malformed-deny plus matching-allow execution tests.
The ownership-registry half of old D8 has improved: ownership-registry.ts:167 rejects failed reloads; ownership-registry.test.ts:153–164 tests malformed-state denial.

6. MAJOR — mkdir lock recovery can temporarily remove a live successor’s lock.
src/governance/approvals/approval-store-lock.ts:252–269; approval-store.ts:343.
Source-derived interleaving: two reclaimers observe a dead lock. One replaces it and acquires a live lock. The delayed reclaimer renames that live successor away. Before restoration, a third contender acquires the vacant pathname. Restoration can fail and is ignored. Two critical sections can overlap.
The ledger version is obtained at append time, rather than retained from the state used to authorize consumption, so it does not reliably repair this interleaving.
Minimal fix: disable automatic fallback reclamation until it is ownership-safe, or use an OS-managed lock. Also make approved-to-consumed conditional on the version originally read.
This affects the fallback backend, not the reviewed Linux flock path. The concurrent fallback test at approval-lock-liveness.test.ts:138 does not force this interleaving.

7. MAJOR — Earlier ask branches conceal hard evasion denies.
src/governance/policy/policy-gate.ts:157–161 and :318–347.
Counterexamples: a command containing “sudo su -” and “passwd root” matches the earlier ask before the later deny. With an enabled whitelist and allowUnmatched:true, an unmatched download-and-execute command returns ask before evasion denial runs.
Explicit capability-deny precedence is fixed, but the gate does not apply deny-wins across these other rule families.
Minimal fix: evaluate mandatory denies before returning any ask, and select the strictest matching evasion result.
This proves deny-to-ask conversion; it does not, by itself, prove successful dispatch without approval.

8. MINOR — Coordination replay denies uncertainty without classifying it.
src/governance/policy/policy-gate.ts:758–767; tests/security/approval-consumed-propagation.test.ts:210–219.
The branch never calls markExecutionUnverified. A pending consumed coordination claim remains pending. The test checks consumed status, identity and record count but omits executionOutcome.
Minimal fix: classify pending consumption under the locked store operation, or explicitly document a narrower pending/unknown contract and stop claiming uniform unverified classification.

9. MAJOR — A later ownership denial can strand a preconsumed coordination approval.
src/governance/policy/policy-gate.ts:780–785; src/runtime-state/runtime/execution-authorization.ts:151–169; src/capabilities/tools/executor.ts:845.
The gate consumes first. A subsequent ownership conflict produces a denied execution decision. The executor therefore never reaches its allowed-decision receipt handling, leaving consumed/pending state despite no router execution.
Minimal fix: defer consumption until all authorization checks pass, or durably record a proven pre-dispatch rejection. Test denial, zero router calls, approval state and lease state together.

10. MINOR — Record text is stale and internally contradictory.
docs/audits/2026-10-24-gate-e-qualification.md:158 says the command exits 3; the actual read-only invocation exits 1/HOLD.
qualification-record.json:203–210 still lists D5/D7 as unfixed despite substantial current remediation, while its D9 closure claim exceeds what the validator establishes.
Minimal fix: update the record against a pinned re-review artifact without upgrading unresolved clauses.


VACUOUS ASSERTIONS

The following distinctions matter: some tests meaningfully verify a helper but remain vacuous for the larger control attributed to them.

1. Constructor enforcement remains untested.
tests/security/worker-approval-port.vitest.ts:266 and :286.
The tests invoke assertNoForbiddenDecisionMethods themselves. Deleting the constructor’s invocation at worker-approval-port.ts:211 leaves them passing.
The helper’s own throw behavior is now genuinely tested. Constructor integration is not.

2. “Another worker’s records” uses no foreign record.
tests/security/worker-approval-port.vitest.ts:200–206.
It creates worker B’s record, verifies B can find it, then queries a nonexistent binding. Remove visibility filtering: these assertions still pass.
The newer sibling-discovery test at :53–66 is meaningful and should replace this misleading evidence.

3. “Different process” and “across processes” are separate instances in one process.
worker-approval-port.vitest.ts:23–27, :146 and :160; legacy-approval-single-use.test.ts:139–145.
These do not prove OS-process isolation or cross-process locking. Removing the OS lock can leave them passing.
Real subprocess evidence now exists elsewhere; these particular assertions should not be presented as that evidence.

4. Source presence does not prove an operative guard.
tests/security/pre-r032-non-bypass.vitest.ts:149–181.
The writer count recognizes one assignment spelling. Object.assign is explicitly invisible at :233. Guard regexes remain satisfied by comments, dead code, or conditions whose rejection body was removed. Removing locking also leaves these assertions satisfied.
The additional scanner-helper tests do not establish execution enforcement.

5. “Missing authority is a pause” never asserts a pause.
tests/security/pre-r032-non-bypass.vitest.ts:187–208.
Only matchedRuleId is asserted. Returning allow with that same rule ID still passes.

6. “Continuation-resume path” never invokes continuation execution.
tests/ownership/ownership-gate.test.ts:143–157.
It calls checkOwnershipGate directly. Removing the executor’s continuation ownership call leaves it passing.

7. One purported executor ownership regression is stopped by missing approval first.
tests/executor.test.ts:391–416.
No approval backs the request. Removing ownership enforcement still produces denial and no file.
The later test at :472–521 improves this by requiring the owned-scope refusal reason. It meaningfully tests attribution/reachability, although its approval lacks invocation binding and therefore cannot establish the stronger claim that removing ownership would actually permit execution.

8. Protected-path parity proves decisions, not absence of effects.
tests/security/policy-protected-path-parity.vitest.ts:87–103 and :123–137.
A caller that ignores the deny and executes would leave these tests green. They are useful gate tests, insufficient dispatch/effect evidence.

9. “Fabricated run cannot qualify” rejects only a missing command.
benchmark/evidence/gate-e-qualification-record.test.mjs:375–386.
The asserted problem is “command is required.” Add an echo command containing the filename and fabricated counts pass, as the read-only probe demonstrated.

10. The accepted independent-review fixture contains no affirmative verdict.
benchmark/evidence/gate-e-qualification-record.test.mjs:337–351.
“Reviewer: … VERDICT: …” is enough for QUALIFIED-INDEPENDENT. No clearance, scope or artifact binding is asserted.

11. “Extras cannot re-admit command execution” never supplies command execution as an extra.
tests/run/read-only-tool-surface.vitest.ts:47–58.
buildReadOnlyToolFilter deletes exclusions before adding unrestricted extras at helpers.ts:409–413. Passing ["alix_shell_run"] re-adds it. The test’s supplied extras cannot expose this hole.
The default filter does exclude shell; it includes verify.claim at helpers.ts:381, contrary to the supplied root instruction’s description.


UNDECLARED GAPS

Beyond the five named F-gaps, material gaps include:

- Canonical ownership/protected-path enforcement through in-workspace symlink ancestors.
- Constructor-call integration coverage, despite meaningful helper-level guard tests.
- Validator acceptance of a rejecting review as affirmative qualification.
- Durable retention of execution logs and hashes identifying compiled build outputs.
- Deterministically scheduled fallback-lock reclamation races.
- Deny/ask precedence across whitelist and evasion rule families.
- Coordination ownership rejection after consumption and its resulting partial authority state.
- Uniform coordination replay classification.
- Read-only filter exclusions surviving caller-supplied extras.

The record already mentions unrestricted store access and malformed policy authority in its earlier findings/notFixed material. Those are acknowledged defects, although absent from declaredGaps; they should not be described as wholly undisclosed.

The record is honest about overall HOLD and the previous NO. Its detailed remediation inventory and Markdown evidence table are not current enough to certify today’s tree.

PARTIAL support for REQ 1; insufficient durable evidence for its full stated claim.

Locally, all 14 SHA256SUMS entries verify. The logs report 17 + 18 + 23 = 58 passing test cases and one skip. - The committed artifact set omits all execution logs.
- No compiled-output hash/build manifest identifies the executable files tested; build.log:2 records only the build command.
- Dot-reporter focused-vitest.log:10–11 retains aggregate counts rather than individual test identities.
- Checksums establish local file integrity, not independent execution provenance or native-versus-emulated execution.

The local files allow partial re-derivation. A fresh checkout cannot re-derive even the logged execution claims without obtaining the ignored logs. The report appropriately disclaims REQ 2 and broader durability certification at qualification.md:69–75.


VERDICT

NO.

Several remediations are real, particularly D1, evaluator deny-wins, unscopable-channel denial, coordination no-replacement replay, receipt propagation and worker identity enforcement. They do not establish all five clauses.

A direct disqualifier remains: the constructor-enforcement claim can survive deletion of worker-approval-port.ts:211 because its tests call the guard separately. More materially, same-user child authority, canonical scope escape, validator false qualification and incomplete durable evidence prevent acceptance.

An independent HUMAN qualifier must adjudicate the threat model and remaining gaps, obtain the complete retained logs and build identities, authorize and reproduce the source-derived counterexamples in a disposable environment, mutation-check the actual construction/dispatch boundaries, and issue an artifact-bound decision under separate authority. This read-only review did not execute those runtime checks.

This verdict may be cited as independent model criticism. It may not be cited as human independence, human qualification, or affirmative Gate E/Phase F clearance.

DEFECTS

1. MAJOR — Child-process approval authority remains reachable.
src/governance/approvals/worker-approval-port.ts:119; src/agents/subagent-manager.ts:368; src/interfaces/cli/commands/approval.ts:55 and :110.
A child executing JavaScript can construct ApprovalStore(workspace), load it, and call resolve, revoke, or public mutate. The CLI similarly exposes approve/deny/revoke without authenticating a distinct worker principal. Environment filtering does not remove same-user filesystem authority. No singleton or passed full-store reference is needed.
Minimal fix: place decision authority behind authenticated parent-owned IPC/storage permissions inaccessible to workers, or explicitly narrow F8b to cooperative use of the facade. The latter does not satisfy the question’s unrestricted child-process claim.

2. MAJOR — Owned/protected-path checks do not constrain canonical destinations.
src/coordination/ownership/path-scope.ts:207–209; src/runtime-state/runtime/workspace-path.ts:39–54 and :112–124; src/capabilities/tools/tool-router.ts:118–128, :205 and :218.
Counterexample: ownedPaths=["owned/**"], with an existing directory symlink owned/link pointing to ../unowned. Creating owned/link/new.txt passes lexical ownership. Canonical workspace containment also passes because unowned remains inside the workspace. Node follows the parent symlink and creates unowned/new.txt.
An alias into an in-workspace protected directory similarly avoids lexical protection matching. The final-component symlink test does not cover this.
Minimal fix: enforce ownership and protection against canonical destinations, including existing ancestors of new files. Use a race-resistant write mechanism or reject symlink traversal.

3. MAJOR — Validator still manufactures independent qualification from unsupported claims.
benchmark/evidence/gate-e-qualification-record.mjs:102, :143–149, :166–176, :219, :233, :317 and :337–340.
Executed read-only probe: supplied an all-zero nonexistent commit, runner “IMAGINARY”, command “echo tests/policy/rule-evaluator.test.ts”, fabricated 999999/999999 counts, “x” negative cases, and rule-evaluator.ts as every clause’s evidence. Retained the existing qualifier reference to the previous rejecting review.
Result: ok:true, QUALIFIED-INDEPENDENT for both model-independent and declared-independent.
The validator checks command substrings, file existence/extensions, supplied arithmetic, and whether review text contains an identity. It does not verify execution, assertion semantics, review verdict, reviewed artifact, or independent authority.
Minimal fix: bind qualification to commit/build-bound execution receipts and an independently controlled review verdict covering those clauses and that artifact. Until then, describe this as structural record validation, not semantic qualification.

4. MAJOR — Execution logs are locally present but absent from the committed evidence set.
.gitignore:15; docs/prd/evidence/lean-01/D9-phase-f-req1-x86-64-qualification-2026-11-02.md:7; evidence/d9-x86-64-2026-11-02/SHA256SUMS:2–14.
git ls-files lists only RESULT.txt, SHA256SUMS and environment.txt in that directory. The 13 logs are ignored. Hashes cannot reconstruct missing files; a fresh checkout cannot inspect the claimed executions.
Minimal fix: retain the logs as tracked evidence or in an immutable, explicitly referenced archive.

5. MAJOR — Invalid policy can remove deny authority.
src/governance/policy/policy-loader.ts:43–45, :54–59.
An invalid deny rule/file is skipped; surviving permissive rules remain, or defaults replace the failed policy set.
Minimal fix: distinguish initial absence from malformed/unreadable configured authority and fail closed on the latter. Add malformed-deny plus matching-allow execution tests.
The ownership-registry half of old D8 has improved: ownership-registry.ts:167 rejects failed reloads; ownership-registry.test.ts:153–164 tests malformed-state denial.

6. MAJOR — mkdir lock recovery can temporarily remove a live successor’s lock.
src/governance/approvals/approval-store-lock.ts:252–269; approval-store.ts:343.
Source-derived interleaving: two reclaimers observe a dead lock. One replaces it and acquires a live lock. The delayed reclaimer renames that live successor away. Before restoration, a third contender acquires the vacant pathname. Restoration can fail and is ignored. Two critical sections can overlap.
The ledger version is obtained at append time, rather than retained from the state used to authorize consumption, so it does not reliably repair this interleaving.
Minimal fix: disable automatic fallback reclamation until it is ownership-safe, or use an OS-managed lock. Also make approved-to-consumed conditional on the version originally read.
This affects the fallback backend, not the reviewed Linux flock path. The concurrent fallback test at approval-lock-liveness.test.ts:138 does not force this interleaving.

7. MAJOR — Earlier ask branches conceal hard evasion denies.
src/governance/policy/policy-gate.ts:157–161 and :318–347.
Counterexamples: a command containing “sudo su -” and “passwd root” matches the earlier ask before the later deny. With an enabled whitelist and allowUnmatched:true, an unmatched download-and-execute command returns ask before evasion denial runs.
Explicit capability-deny precedence is fixed, but the gate does not apply deny-wins across these other rule families.
Minimal fix: evaluate mandatory denies before returning any ask, and select the strictest matching evasion result.
This proves deny-to-ask conversion; it does not, by itself, prove successful dispatch without approval.

8. MINOR — Coordination replay denies uncertainty without classifying it.
src/governance/policy/policy-gate.ts:758–767; tests/security/approval-consumed-propagation.test.ts:210–219.
The branch never calls markExecutionUnverified. A pending consumed coordination claim remains pending. The test checks consumed status, identity and record count but omits executionOutcome.
Minimal fix: classify pending consumption under the locked store operation, or explicitly document a narrower pending/unknown contract and stop claiming uniform unverified classification.

9. MAJOR — A later ownership denial can strand a preconsumed coordination approval.
src/governance/policy/policy-gate.ts:780–785; src/runtime-state/runtime/execution-authorization.ts:151–169; src/capabilities/tools/executor.ts:845.
The gate consumes first. A subsequent ownership conflict produces a denied execution decision. The executor therefore never reaches its allowed-decision receipt handling, leaving consumed/pending state despite no router execution.
Minimal fix: defer consumption until all authorization checks pass, or durably record a proven pre-dispatch rejection. Test denial, zero router calls, approval state and lease state together.

10. MINOR — Record text is stale and internally contradictory.
docs/audits/2026-10-24-gate-e-qualification.md:158 says the command exits 3; the actual read-only invocation exits 1/HOLD.
qualification-record.json:203–210 still lists D5/D7 as unfixed despite substantial current remediation, while its D9 closure claim exceeds what the validator establishes.
Minimal fix: update the record against a pinned re-review artifact without upgrading unresolved clauses.

- No compiled-output hash/build manifest identifies the executable files tested; build.log:2 records only the build command.
- Dot-reporter focused-vitest.log:10–11 retains aggregate counts rather than individual test identities.

The local files allow partial re-derivation. A fresh checkout cannot re-derive even the logged execution claims without obtaining the ignored logs. The report appropriately disclaims REQ 2 and broader durability certification at qualification.md:69–75.


VERDICT

NO.

Several remediations are real, particularly D1, evaluator deny-wins, unscopable-channel denial, coordination no-replacement replay, receipt propagation and worker identity enforcement. They do not establish all five clauses.

A direct disqualifier remains: the constructor-enforcement claim can survive deletion of worker-approval-port.ts:211 because its tests call the guard separately. More materially, same-user child authority, canonical scope escape, validator false qualification and incomplete durable evidence prevent acceptance.

An independent HUMAN qualifier must adjudicate the threat model and remaining gaps, obtain the complete retained logs and build identities, authorize and reproduce the source-derived counterexamples in a disposable environment, mutation-check the actual construction/dispatch boundaries, and issue an artifact-bound decision under separate authority. This read-only review did not execute those runtime checks.

This verdict may be cited as independent model criticism. It may not be cited as human independence, human qualification, or affirmative Gate E/Phase F clearance.
